13.s:
dharaṇyuvāca .
etat tanmahadāścaryaṃ dṛṣṭvā gauramukho muniḥ .
te cāpi maṇijāḥ prāptāḥ kiṃ phalaṃ tu varaṃ guroḥ .. 13.1 ..
13.d:
धरण्युवाच ।
एतत् तन्महदाश्चर्यं दृष्ट्वा गौरमुखो मुनिः ।
ते चापि मणिजाः प्राप्ताः किं फलं तु वरं गुरोः ॥ 13.1 ॥
13.m: Dharaṇī said: / Having seen that great wonder, the sage Gauramukha— / and those who were jewel-born arrived—what excellent fruit of the guru [was attained]?

13.s:
ko'sau gauramukhaḥ śrīmān muniḥ paramadhārmmikaḥ .
kiṃ cakāra hareḥ karmma dṛṣṭvā'sau munipuṃgavaḥ .. 13.2 ..
13.d:
कोऽसौ गौरमुखः श्रीमान् मुनिः परमधार्म्मिकः ।
किं चकार हरेः कर्म्म दृष्ट्वाऽसौ मुनिपुंगवः ॥ 13.2 ॥
13.m: Who is this illustrious Gauramukha, the most righteous sage? / Having seen Hari's work, what did that bull among sages do?

13.s:
śrīvarāha uvāca .
nimiṣeṇa kṛtaṃ karma dṛṣṭvā bhagavato muniḥ .
ārirādhayiṣurdevaṃ tameva prayayau vanam .
prabhāsaṃ nāma somasya tīrthaṃ paramadurlabham .. 13.3 ..
13.d:
श्रीवराह उवाच ।
निमिषेण कृतं कर्म दृष्ट्वा भगवतो मुनिः ।
आरिराधयिषुर्देवं तमेव प्रययौ वनम् ।
प्रभासं नाम सोमस्य तीर्थं परमदुर्लभम् ॥ 13.3 ॥
13.m: The glorious Varāha said: / Having seen the deed of the Lord done in a twinkling, the sage, / desiring to worship the god, went to that very forest, / the most rare sacred place belonging to Soma named Prabhāsa.

13.s:
tatra daityāntakṛd devaḥ procyate tīrthacintakaiḥ .
ārādhayāmāsa hariṃ daityasūdanasaṃjñitam .. 13.4 ..
13.d:
तत्र दैत्यान्तकृद् देवः प्रोच्यते तीर्थचिन्तकैः ।
आराधयामास हरिं दैत्यसूदनसंज्ञितम् ॥ 13.4 ॥
13.m: There the god who slays daityas is praised by those who ponder sacred places; / he worshipped Hari, known as the slayer of daityas.

13.s:
tasyārādhayato devaṃ hariṃ nārāyaṇaṃ prabhum .
ājagāma mahāyogī mārkaṇḍeyo mahāmuniḥ .. 13.5 ..
13.d:
तस्याराधयतो देवं हरिं नारायणं प्रभुम् ।
आजगाम महायोगी मार्कण्डेयो महामुनिः ॥ 13.5 ॥
13.m: As he was worshipping the god Hari, the lord Nārāyaṇa, / the great yogin Mārkaṇḍeya, the great sage, arrived.

13.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā'bhyāgataṃ dūrādarghapādyena so muniḥ .
arcayāmāsa taṃ bhaktyā mudā paramayā yutaḥ .. 13.6 ..
13.d:
तं दृष्ट्वाऽभ्यागतं दूरादर्घपाद्येन सो मुनिः ।
अर्चयामास तं भक्त्या मुदा परमया युतः ॥ 13.6 ॥
13.m: Seeing him arrived from afar, that sage, / filled with supreme joy, worshipped him with devotion using water for honor and foot-washing.

13.s:
kauśyāṃ vṛṣyāṃ tadāsīnaṃ papracchedaṃ munistadā .
śādhiṃ māṃ muniśārdūla kiṃ karomi mahāvrata .. 13.7 ..
13.d:
कौश्यां वृष्यां तदासीनं पप्रच्छेदं मुनिस्तदा ।
शाधिं मां मुनिशार्दूल किं करोमि महाव्रत ॥ 13.7 ॥
13.m: To him then seated on a kuśa-grass seat, the sage then asked this: / "Instruct me, tiger among sages; what should I do, O one of great vows?"

13.s:
evamuktaḥ sa viprendro mārkaṇḍeyo mahātapāḥ .
uvāca ślakṣṇayā vācā muniṃ gauramukhaṃ tadā .. 13.8 ..
13.d:
एवमुक्तः स विप्रेन्द्रो मार्कण्डेयो महातपाः ।
उवाच श्लक्ष्णया वाचा मुनिं गौरमुखं तदा ॥ 13.8 ॥
13.m: Addressed thus, that best of vipras, Mārkaṇḍeya of great austerities, / then spoke with gentle words to the sage Gauramukha.

13.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca .
etadeva mahatkṛtyaṃ yatsatāṃ saṃgamo bhavet .
yattu sāndehikaṃ kāryaṃ tatpṛcchasva mahāmune .. 13.9 ..
13.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ।
एतदेव महत्कृत्यं यत्सतां संगमो भवेत् ।
यत्तु सान्देहिकं कार्यं तत्पृच्छस्व महामुने ॥ 13.9 ॥
13.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / "This alone is a great deed: that there should be an association of the good. / But whatever matter is doubtful, ask about that, O great sage."

13.s:
gauramukha uvāca .
ete hi pitaro nāma procyante vedavādibhiḥ .
sarvavarṇaṣu sāmānyā utāhosvit pṛthak pṛthak .. 13.10 ..
13.d:
गौरमुख उवाच ।
एते हि पितरो नाम प्रोच्यन्ते वेदवादिभिः ।
सर्ववर्णषु सामान्या उताहोस्वित् पृथक् पृथक् ॥ 13.10 ॥
13.m: Gauramukha said: / "These indeed are called the Pitṛs by those who proclaim the Vedas; / are they common to all social classes, or are they distinct?"

13.s:
mārkaṇḍeyaḥ .
sarveṣāmeva devānāmādyo nārāyaṇo guruḥ .
tasmād brahmā samutpannaḥ so'pi saptāsṛjanmunīn .. 13.11 ..
13.d:
मार्कण्डेयः ।
सर्वेषामेव देवानामाद्यो नारायणो गुरुः ।
तस्माद् ब्रह्मा समुत्पन्नः सोऽपि सप्तासृजन्मुनीन् ॥ 13.11 ॥
13.m: Mārkaṇḍeya [said]: / Nārāyaṇa is the first guru of all the gods. / From him Brahmā arose, and he created seven sages.

13.s:
māṃ yajasveti tenoktāstadā te parameṣṭhinā .
ātmanātmānamevāgre ayajanta iti śrutiḥ .. 13.12 ..
13.d:
मां यजस्वेति तेनोक्तास्तदा ते परमेष्ठिना ।
आत्मनात्मानमेवाग्रे अयजन्त इति श्रुतिः ॥ 13.12 ॥
13.m: Addressed then by that Parameṣṭhin, 'Sacrifice to me!', / they first sacrificed to the self through the self alone—so runs the Vedic text.

13.s:
teṣāṃ vai brahmajātānāṃ mahāvaikārikarmaṇām .
aśapad vyabhicāro hi mahāneṣa kṛto yataḥ .
prabhraṣṭajñāninaḥ sarve bhaviṣyatha na saṃśayaḥ .. 13.13 ..
13.d:
तेषां वै ब्रह्मजातानां महावैकारिकर्मणाम् ।
अशपद् व्यभिचारो हि महानेष कृतो यतः ।
प्रभ्रष्टज्ञानिनः सर्वे भविष्यथ न संशयः ॥ 13.13 ॥
13.m: Them, born of Brahmā, of great prideful action, / he cursed: 'Because this great transgression has been committed, / you will all become fallen from knowledge, there is no doubt.'

13.s:
evaṃ śaptāstataste vai brahmaṇātmasamudbhavāḥ .
sadyo vaṃśakarān putrānutpādya tridivaṃ yayuḥ .. 13.14 ..
13.d:
एवं शप्तास्ततस्ते वै ब्रह्मणात्मसमुद्भवाः ।
सद्यो वंशकरान् पुत्रानुत्पाद्य त्रिदिवं ययुः ॥ 13.14 ॥
13.m: Cursed thus by Brahmā, those born of himself / immediately fathered sons who would continue their line, and went to heaven.

13.s:
tatasteṣu prayāteṣu tridivaṃ brahmavādiṣu .
tatputrāḥ śrāddhadānena tarpayāmāsurañjasā .. 13.15 ..
13.d:
ततस्तेषु प्रयातेषु त्रिदिवं ब्रह्मवादिषु ।
तत्पुत्राः श्राद्धदानेन तर्पयामासुरञ्जसा ॥ 13.15 ॥
13.m: Then, when those proclaimers of the Veda had departed to heaven, / their sons easily gratified them with the offering of a śrāddha.

13.s:
te ca vaimānikāḥ sarve brahmaṇaḥ sapta mānasāḥ .
tat piṇḍadānaṃ mantroktaṃ prapaśyanto vyavasthitāḥ .. 13.16 ..
13.d:
ते च वैमानिकाः सर्वे ब्रह्मणः सप्त मानसाः ।
तत् पिण्डदानं मन्त्रोक्तं प्रपश्यन्तो व्यवस्थिताः ॥ 13.16 ॥
13.m: And all those seven mind-born sons of Brahmā, riders of aerial chariots, / remained looking upon that offering of piṇḍas enjoined by mantra.

13.s:
gauramukha uvāca .
ye ca te pitaro brahman yaṃ ca kālaṃ samāsate .
kiṃ yato vai pitṛgaṇāstasmiṃlloke vyavasthitāḥ .. 13.17 ..
13.d:
गौरमुख उवाच ।
ये च ते पितरो ब्रह्मन् यं च कालं समासते ।
किं यतो वै पितृगणास्तस्मिंल्लोके व्यवस्थिताः ॥ 13.17 ॥
13.m: Gauramukha said: / "And those who are the Pitṛs, O Brahmin, and what time they wait upon— / why is it that the groups of Pitṛs are stationed in that world?"

13.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca .
pravarttante varāḥ kecid devānāṃ somavarddhanāḥ .
te marīcyādayaḥ sapta svarge te pitaraḥ smṛtāḥ .. 13.18 ..
13.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ।
प्रवर्त्तन्ते वराः केचिद् देवानां सोमवर्द्धनाः ।
ते मरीच्यादयः सप्त स्वर्गे ते पितरः स्मृताः ॥ 13.18 ॥
13.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Some excellent ones, who nourish Soma for the gods, proceed [there]; / they are Marīci and the rest, the seven considered Pitṛs in heaven.

13.s:
catvāro mūrttimanto vai trayastvanye hyamūrttayaḥ .
teṣāṃ lokanisargaṃ ca kīrttayiṣyāmi tacchṛṇu .. 13.19 ..
13.d:
चत्वारो मूर्त्तिमन्तो वै त्रयस्त्वन्ये ह्यमूर्त्तयः ।
तेषां लोकनिसर्गं च कीर्त्तयिष्यामि तच्छृणु ॥ 13.19 ॥
13.m: Four indeed possess form, while the other three are formless. / I will proclaim their world and nature; listen to that!

13.s:
prabhāvaṃ ca mahardhi ca vistareṇa nibodha me .
dharmamūrtidharāsteṣāṃ trayo'nye paramā gaṇāḥ .
teṣāṃ nāmāni lokāṃśca kīrtayiṣyāmi tacchṛṇu .. 13.20 ..
13.d:
प्रभावं च महर्धि च विस्तरेण निबोध मे ।
धर्ममूर्तिधरास्तेषां त्रयोऽन्ये परमा गणाः ।
तेषां नामानि लोकांश्च कीर्तयिष्यामि तच्छृणु ॥ 13.20 ॥
13.m: And comprehend from me in detail their power and great prosperity: / three other supreme hosts among them bear forms of dharma; / I shall proclaim their names and their worlds; listen to that!

13.s:
lokāḥ saṃtānakā nāma yatra tiṣṭhanti bhāsvarāḥ .
amūrttayaḥ pitṛgaṇāste vai putrāḥ prajāpateḥ .. 13.21 ..
13.d:
लोकाः संतानका नाम यत्र तिष्ठन्ति भास्वराः ।
अमूर्त्तयः पितृगणास्ते वै पुत्राः प्रजापतेः ॥ 13.21 ॥
13.m: The worlds are named Saṃtānaka, where the radiant / formless hosts of Pitṛs dwell, who are the sons of Prajāpati.

13.s: virājasya prajāśreṣṭhā vairājā iti te smṛtāḥ ..
13.d: विराजस्य प्रजाश्रेष्ठा वैराजा इति ते स्मृताः ॥
13.m:
The best offspring of Virāj are traditionally remembered as the Vairājas;
they are indeed the ancestors of the gods, and the deities worship them here.

13.s: devānāṃ pitaraste hi tān yajantīha devatāḥ .. 13.22 ..
13.d: देवानां पितरस्ते हि तान् यजन्तीह देवताः ॥ 13.22 ॥

13.s:
ete vai lokavibhraṣṭā lokān prāpya sanātanān .
punaryugaśatānteṣu jāyante brahmavādinaḥ .. 13.23 ..
13.d:
एते वै लोकविभ्रष्टा लोकान् प्राप्य सनातनान् ।
पुनर्युगशतान्तेषु जायन्ते ब्रह्मवादिनः ॥ 13.23 ॥
13.m: These indeed, fallen from the worlds, having reached eternal worlds, / are born again at the end of hundreds of yugas as proclaimers of the Veda.

13.s:
te prāpya tāṃ smṛtiṃ bhūyaḥ sādhya yogamanuttamam .
cintya yogagatiṃ śuddhāṃ punarāvṛttidurlabhām .. 13.24 ..
13.d:
ते प्राप्य तां स्मृतिं भूयः साध्य योगमनुत्तमम् ।
चिन्त्य योगगतिं शुद्धां पुनरावृत्तिदुर्लभाम् ॥ 13.24 ॥
13.m: They, having obtained that memory again, accomplishing unexcelled yoga, / contemplating the pure path of yoga from which return is hard to obtain—

13.s:
ete sma pitaraḥ śrāddhe yogināṃ yogavarddhanāḥ .
āpyāyitāstu te pūrvaṃ yogaṃ yogabale ratau .. 13.25 ..
13.d:
एते स्म पितरः श्राद्धे योगिनां योगवर्द्धनाः ।
आप्यायितास्तु ते पूर्वं योगं योगबले रतौ ॥ 13.25 ॥
13.m: these are the Pitṛs at a śrāddha who increase the yoga of yogins. / But they were previously nourished, devoted to yoga and the power of yoga.

13.s:
tasmācchrāddhāni deyāni yogināṃ yogisattama .
eṣa vai prathamaḥ sargaḥ somapānāmanuttamaḥ .. 13.26 ..
13.d:
तस्माच्छ्राद्धानि देयानि योगिनां योगिसत्तम ।
एष वै प्रथमः सर्गः सोमपानामनुत्तमः ॥ 13.26 ॥
13.m: Therefore śrāddhas should be given to yogins, O best of yogins! / This is the first, unexcelled creation of the Soma-drinkers.

13.s:
ete ta ekatanavo vartante dbijasattamāḥ .
bhūrlokavāsināṃ yājyāḥ svargalokanivāsinaḥ ..
13.d:
एते त एकतनवो वर्तन्ते द्बिजसत्तमाः ।
भूर्लोकवासिनां याज्याः स्वर्गलोकनिवासिनः ॥

13.s: brahmaputrā marīcyādyāsteṣāṃ yājyā mahadgatāḥ .. 13.27 ..
13.d: ब्रह्मपुत्रा मरीच्याद्यास्तेषां याज्या महद्गताः ॥ 13.27 ॥

13.s:
kalpavāsikasaṃjñānāṃ teṣāmapi jane gatāḥ .
sanakādyāstatasteṣāṃ vairājāstapasi sthitāḥ .
teṣāṃ satyagatā muktā ityeṣā pitṛsaṃtatiḥ .. 13.28 ..
13.d:
कल्पवासिकसंज्ञानां तेषामपि जने गताः ।
सनकाद्यास्ततस्तेषां वैराजास्तपसि स्थिताः ।
तेषां सत्यगता मुक्ता इत्येषा पितृसंततिः ॥ 13.28 ॥
13.m: Those known as Kalpavāsikas, gone to Janaloka, [worship] them; / then Sanaka and the rest, the Vairājas established in austerity, [worship] them; / the liberated ones gone to Satyaloka [worship] them—such is the lineage of Pitṛs.

13.s:
agniṣvātteti mārīcyā vairājā barhisaṃjñitāḥ .
sukāleyāpi pitaro vasiṣṭhasya prajāpateḥ .
te'pi yājyāstribhirvarṇairna śūdreṇa pṛthakkṛtam .. 13.29 ..
13.d:
अग्निष्वात्तेति मारीच्या वैराजा बर्हिसंज्ञिताः ।
सुकालेयापि पितरो वसिष्ठस्य प्रजापतेः ।
तेऽपि याज्यास्त्रिभिर्वर्णैर्न शूद्रेण पृथक्कृतम् ॥ 13.29 ॥
13.m: The descendants of Marīci are named Agniṣvāttas; the Vairājas are designated Barhiṣads; / the Sukāleyas are the Pitṛs of the Prajāpati Vasiṣṭha. / They too are worthy of worship by the three social classes, not separately by a śūdra.

13.s:
varṇatrayābhyanujñātaḥ śūdraḥ sarvān pitṛn yajet .
na tu tasya pṛthak santi pitaraḥ śūdrajātayaḥ .. 13.30 ..
13.d:
वर्णत्रयाभ्यनुज्ञातः शूद्रः सर्वान् पितृन् यजेत् ।
न तु तस्य पृथक् सन्ति पितरः शूद्रजातयः ॥ 13.30 ॥
13.m: Permitted by the three [higher] classes, a Śūdra may worship all the ancestors; / for there are no separate ancestors belonging to the Śūdra class.

13.s:
muktaścetanako brahman nanu vipreṣu dṛśyate .
viśeṣaśāstradṛṣṭyā tu purāṇānāṃ ca darśanāt .. 13.31 ..
13.d:
मुक्तश्चेतनको ब्रह्मन् ननु विप्रेषु दृश्यते ।
विशेषशास्त्रदृष्ट्या तु पुराणानां च दर्शनात् ॥ 13.31 ॥
13.m: O sage, a liberated conscious soul is indeed seen among the Brahmins, / by virtue of special scriptural views and from the teaching of the Purāṇas.

13.s:
evaṃ ṛṣistutaiḥ śāstraṃ jñātvā yājyakasaṃbhavān .
svayaṃ sṛṣṭyāṃ smṛtirlabdhā putrāṇāṃ brahmaṇā tataḥ .
paraṃ nirvāṇamāpannāste'pi jñānena eva ca .. 13.32 ..
13.d:
एवं ऋषिस्तुतैः शास्त्रं ज्ञात्वा याज्यकसंभवान् ।
स्वयं सृष्ट्यां स्मृतिर्लब्धा पुत्राणां ब्रह्मणा ततः ।
परं निर्वाणमापन्नास्तेऽपि ज्ञानेन एव च ॥ 13.32 ॥
13.m: Thus knowing from the scriptures praised by the sages that they were born as worthy recipients, / Brahmā then attained recollection of his sons in his own creation; / and through knowledge, they too reached the supreme Nirvāṇa.

13.s:
vasvādīnāṃ kaśyapādyā varṇānāṃ vasavādayaḥ .
aviśeṣeṇa vijñeyā gandharvādyā api dhruvam .. 13.33 ..
13.d:
वस्वादीनां कश्यपाद्या वर्णानां वसवादयः ।
अविशेषेण विज्ञेया गन्धर्वाद्या अपि ध्रुवम् ॥ 13.33 ॥
13.m: Kaśyapa and the rest [are ancestors] of the Vasus and others, and the Vasus and others [are ancestors] of the classes; / Gandharvas and others should also certainly be understood without distinction.

13.s:
eṣa te paitṛkaḥ sarga uddeśena mahāmune .
kathito nānta evāsya varṣakoṭyā hi dṛśyate .. 13.34 ..
13.d:
एष ते पैतृकः सर्ग उद्देशेन महामुने ।
कथितो नान्त एवास्य वर्षकोट्या हि दृश्यते ॥ 13.34 ॥
13.m: This creation of the ancestors has been narrated to you in brief, O great sage; / indeed, its end cannot be seen even in a crore of years.

13.s:
śrāddhasya kālān vakṣyāmi tān śrṛṇuṣva dvijottama .
śrāddhārhamāgataṃ dravyaṃ viśiṣṭamathavā dvijam .. 13.35 ..
13.d:
श्राद्धस्य कालान् वक्ष्यामि तान् श्रृणुष्व द्विजोत्तम ।
श्राद्धार्हमागतं द्रव्यं विशिष्टमथवा द्विजम् ॥ 13.35 ॥
13.m: I shall explain the times for the śrāddha; listen to them, O best of the twice-born. / When an article worthy of a śrāddha has arrived, or an eminent twice-born [guest],

13.s:
śrāddhaṃ kurvīta vijñāya vyatīpāte'yane tathā .
viṣuve caiva saṃprāpte grahaṇe śaśisūryayoḥ .
samasteṣveva viprendra rāśiṣvarke'tigacchati .. 13.36 ..
13.d:
श्राद्धं कुर्वीत विज्ञाय व्यतीपातेऽयने तथा ।
विषुवे चैव संप्राप्ते ग्रहणे शशिसूर्ययोः ।
समस्तेष्वेव विप्रेन्द्र राशिष्वर्केऽतिगच्छति ॥ 13.36 ॥
13.m: recognizing it, one should perform a śrāddha; likewise at a Vyatīpāta, at a solstice, / upon an equinox, at an eclipse of the moon or sun, / and, O prince of sages, at each time the sun passes into a zodiacal sign.

13.s:
nakṣatragrahapīḍāsu duṣṭasvapnāvalokane .
icchāśrāddhāni kurvīta navasasyāgame tathā .. 13.37 ..
13.d:
नक्षत्रग्रहपीडासु दुष्टस्वप्नावलोकने ।
इच्छाश्राद्धानि कुर्वीत नवसस्यागमे तथा ॥ 13.37 ॥
13.m: During afflictions caused by asterisms and planets, upon seeing a bad dream, / and upon the arrival of fresh grain, one should perform occasional śrāddhas as desired.

13.s:
amāvāsyā yadā ārdrāviśākhāsvātiyogino .
śrāddhaiḥ pitṛgaṇastṛptiṃ tadāpnotyaṣṭavārṣikīm .. 13.38 ..
13.d:
अमावास्या यदा आर्द्राविशाखास्वातियोगिनो ।
श्राद्धैः पितृगणस्तृप्तिं तदाप्नोत्यष्टवार्षिकीम् ॥ 13.38 ॥
13.m: When a new moon coincides with Ārdrā, Viśākhā, or Svāti, / the host of ancestors then attains satisfaction for eight years through the śrāddhas.

13.s:
amāvasyā yadā puṣye raudre'tharkṣe punarvasau .
dvādaśābdaṃ tathā tṛptiṃ prayānti pitaro'rccitāḥ .. 13.39 ..
13.d:
अमावस्या यदा पुष्ये रौद्रेऽथर्क्षे पुनर्वसौ ।
द्वादशाब्दं तथा तृप्तिं प्रयान्ति पितरोऽर्च्चिताः ॥ 13.39 ॥
13.m: When a new moon [falls] in Puṣya, or in the Rudra-asterism [Ārdrā], or in Punarvasu, / the ancestors, being worshipped, thus attain satisfaction for twelve years.

13.s:
vāsavājaikapādarkṣe pitṝṇāṃ tṛptimicchatām .
vāruṇe cāpyamāvāsyā devānāmapi durlabhā .. 13.40 ..
13.d:
वासवाजैकपादर्क्षे पितॄणां तृप्तिमिच्छताम् ।
वारुणे चाप्यमावास्या देवानामपि दुर्लभा ॥ 13.40 ॥
13.m: For those desiring satisfaction of the ancestors, a new moon / in the asterism of the Vasus [Dhaniṣṭhā], Ajaikapād [Pūrvabhādrapadā], or Varuṇa [Śatabhiṣaj] is difficult even for the gods to obtain.

13.s:
navasvarkṣeṣvamāvāsyā yadā teṣu dvijottama .
tadā śrāddhāni deyāni akṣayyaphalamicchatām .
api koṭisahastreṇa puṇyasyānto na vidyate .. 13.41 ..
13.d:
नवस्वर्क्षेष्वमावास्या यदा तेषु द्विजोत्तम ।
तदा श्राद्धानि देयानि अक्षय्यफलमिच्छताम् ।
अपि कोटिसहस्त्रेण पुण्यस्यान्तो न विद्यते ॥ 13.41 ॥
13.m: When a new moon falls in these nine asterisms, O best of the twice-born, / śrāddhas are then to be offered by those desiring inexhaustible fruit; / there is no end to the merit, even through a thousand crores [of years].

13.s:
athāparaṃ pitaraḥ śrāddhakālaṃ
rahasyamasmat pravadanti puṇyam .
vaiśākhamāsasya tu yā tṛtīyā
navamyasau kārttikaśuklapakṣe .. 13.42 ..
13.d:
अथापरं पितरः श्राद्धकालं
रहस्यमस्मत् प्रवदन्ति पुण्यम् ।
वैशाखमासस्य तु या तृतीया
नवम्यसौ कार्त्तिकशुक्लपक्षे ॥ 13.42 ॥
13.m: Now the ancestors declare another sacred, secret time for the śrāddha: / the third day of the month of Vaiśākha, and the ninth in the bright fortnight of Kārttika;

13.s:
nabhasyamāsasya tamistrapakṣe
trayodaśī pañcadaśī ca māghe .
upaplave candramaso raveśca
tathāṣṭakāsvapyayanadvaye ca .. 13.43 ..
13.d:
नभस्यमासस्य तमिस्त्रपक्षे
त्रयोदशी पञ्चदशी च माघे ।
उपप्लवे चन्द्रमसो रवेश्च
तथाष्टकास्वप्ययनद्वये च ॥ 13.43 ॥
13.m: the thirteenth in the dark fortnight of the month of Nabhasya [Bhādrapada], the fifteenth in Māgha, / during an eclipse of the moon and the sun, / on the Aṣṭakās, and at the two solstices.

13.s:
pānīyamapyatra tilairvimiśraṃ
dadyātpitṛbhyaḥ prayato manuṣyaḥ .
śrāddhaṃ kṛtaṃ tena samāḥsahastraṃ
rahasyametat pitaro vadanti .. 13.44 ..
13.d:
पानीयमप्यत्र तिलैर्विमिश्रं
दद्यात्पितृभ्यः प्रयतो मनुष्यः ।
श्राद्धं कृतं तेन समाःसहस्त्रं
रहस्यमेतत् पितरो वदन्ति ॥ 13.44 ॥
13.m: Even if a restrained man offers here to the ancestors / only water mixed with sesame seeds, / a śrāddha is performed by him for a thousand years; this is the secret the ancestors proclaim.

13.s:
māghāsite pañcadaśī kadāci-
dupaiti yogaṃ yadi vāruṇena .
ṛkṣeṇa kālaḥ paramaḥ pitṝṇāṃ
na tvalpapuṇyairdvija labhyate'sau .. 13.45 ..
13.d:
माघासिते पञ्चदशी कदाचि-
दुपैति योगं यदि वारुणेन ।
ऋक्षेण कालः परमः पितॄणां
न त्वल्पपुण्यैर्द्विज लभ्यतेऽसौ ॥ 13.45 ॥
13.m: If the fifteenth day in the dark half of Māgha / should ever conjunction with the asterism of Varuṇa [Śatabhiṣaj], / it is a supreme time for the ancestors; it is not obtained by those of little merit, O twice-born.

13.s:
kāle dhaniṣṭhā yadi nāma tasmin
bhavettu viprendra sadā pitṛbhyaḥ .
dattaṃ jalānnaṃ pradadāti tṛptiṃ
varṣāyutaṃ tatkulajairmanuṣyaiḥ .. 13.46 ..
13.d:
काले धनिष्ठा यदि नाम तस्मिन्
भवेत्तु विप्रेन्द्र सदा पितृभ्यः ।
दत्तं जलान्नं प्रददाति तृप्तिं
वर्षायुतं तत्कुलजैर्मनुष्यैः ॥ 13.46 ॥
13.m: If indeed Dhaniṣṭhā should occur at that time, O prince of sages, / water and food then offered by men born in that family / forever gives satisfaction to the ancestors for ten thousand years.

13.s:
tatraiva ced bhādrapadāstu pūrvāḥ
kāle tadā yaiḥ kriyate pitṛbhyaḥ .
śrāddhaṃ parā tṛptimupetya tena
yugaṃ samagraṃ pitaraḥ svapanti ..
13.d:
तत्रैव चेद् भाद्रपदास्तु पूर्वाः
काले तदा यैः क्रियते पितृभ्यः ।
श्राद्धं परा तृप्तिमुपेत्य तेन
युगं समग्रं पितरः स्वपन्ति ॥
13.m:
If at that very time the asterism is Pūrvabhādrapadā,
those by whom a śrāddha is performed for the ancestors at that time,
attaining supreme satisfaction through it,
the ancestors sleep [in contentment] for a whole yuga.
As for that fortnight which they proclaim for śrāddha,
the hosts of sages declare it to be the ancestral satisfaction.

13.s:
śrāddhaṃ tu yatpakṣamudāharanti
tatpaitṛkaṃ munigaṇāḥ pravadanti tuṣṭim .. 13.47 ..
13.d:
श्राद्धं तु यत्पक्षमुदाहरन्ति
तत्पैतृकं मुनिगणाः प्रवदन्ति तुष्टिम् ॥ 13.47 ॥

13.s:
gaṅgāsarayūmathavā vipāśāṃ
sarasvatīṃ naimiṣagomatīṃ vā .
tato'vagāhyārcanamādareṇa
kṛtvā pitṝṇāmahitāni hanti .. 13.48 ..
13.d:
गङ्गासरयूमथवा विपाशां
सरस्वतीं नैमिषगोमतीं वा ।
ततोऽवगाह्यार्चनमादरेण
कृत्वा पितॄणामहितानि हन्ति ॥ 13.48 ॥
13.m: Having bathed in the Gaṅgā, the Sarayū, or the Vipāśā, / the Sarasvatī, or the Gomatī in Naimiṣa, / and then reverently worshipping the ancestors, one destroys adversities.

13.s:
gāyanti caitat pitaraḥ kadā tu
varṣāmaghātṛptimavāpya bhūyaḥ .
māghāsitānte śubhatīrthatoyai-
ryāsyāma tṛptiṃ tanayādidattaiḥ .. 13.49 ..
13.d:
गायन्ति चैतत् पितरः कदा तु
वर्षामघातृप्तिमवाप्य भूयः ।
माघासितान्ते शुभतीर्थतोयै-
र्यास्याम तृप्तिं तनयादिदत्तैः ॥ 13.49 ॥
13.m: And the ancestors sing this: 'When shall we, / having attained satisfaction again during the rains in Maghā, / reach satisfaction through the waters of auspicious sacred places offered by sons and others at the end of the dark half of Māgha?'

13.s:
cittaṃ ca vittaṃ ca nṛṇāṃ viśuddhaṃ
śastaśca kālaḥ kathito vidhiśca .
pātraṃ yathoktaṃ paramā ca bhakti-
rnṛṇāṃ prayacchantyabhivāñchitāni .. 13.50 ..
13.d:
चित्तं च वित्तं च नृणां विशुद्धं
शस्तश्च कालः कथितो विधिश्च ।
पात्रं यथोक्तं परमा च भक्ति-
र्नृणां प्रयच्छन्त्यभिवाञ्छितानि ॥ 13.50 ॥
13.m: A pure heart and pure wealth of men, / the praised time, the prescribed rite, / a worthy recipient as declared, and supreme devotion—these grant the desires of men.

13.s:
pitṛgītāstathaivātra ślokāstān śrṛṇu sattama .
śrutvā tathaiva bhavitā bhāvyaṃ tatra vidhātmanā .. 13.51 ..
13.d:
पितृगीतास्तथैवात्र श्लोकास्तान् श्रृणु सत्तम ।
श्रुत्वा तथैव भविता भाव्यं तत्र विधात्मना ॥ 13.51 ॥
13.m: Listen to the verses sung by the ancestors here in this regard, O best of beings. / Having heard them, one should be devoted to the rite in that manner with mind focused on the ordinance.

13.s:
api dhanyaḥ kule jāyādasmākaṃ matimān naraḥ .
akurvan vittaśāṭhyaṃ yaḥ piṇḍān yo nirvapiṣyati .. 13.52 ..
13.d:
अपि धन्यः कुले जायादस्माकं मतिमान् नरः ।
अकुर्वन् वित्तशाठ्यं यः पिण्डान् यो निर्वपिष्यति ॥ 13.52 ॥
13.m: 'May a fortunate, intelligent man be born in our family, / who, without holding back his wealth through deceit, will offer the funeral rice-balls;

13.s:
ratnavastramahāyānaṃ sarvaṃ bhogādikaṃ vasu .
vibhave sati viprebhyo asmānuddiśya dāsyati .. 13.53 ..
13.d:
रत्नवस्त्रमहायानं सर्वं भोगादिकं वसु ।
विभवे सति विप्रेभ्यो अस्मानुद्दिश्य दास्यति ॥ 13.53 ॥
13.m: who, if he has the means, will give gems, garments, fine conveyances, / and all wealth consisting of enjoyments to the Brahmins for our sake;

13.s:
annena vā yathāśaktyā kāle'smin bhaktinamradhīḥ .
bhojayiṣyati viprāgryāṃstanmātravibhavo naraḥ .. 13.54 ..
13.d:
अन्नेन वा यथाशक्त्या कालेऽस्मिन् भक्तिनम्रधीः ।
भोजयिष्यति विप्राग्र्यांस्तन्मात्रविभवो नरः ॥ 13.54 ॥
13.m: or, with a mind humble through devotion, will feed the foremost Brahmins / with food according to his capacity at this time, if he is a man of only modest means;

13.s:
asamartho'nnadānasya vanyaśākaṃ svaśaktitaḥ .
pradāsyatidvijāgryebhyaḥ svalpāṃ yo vāpi dakṣiṇām .. 13.55 ..
13.d:
असमर्थोऽन्नदानस्य वन्यशाकं स्वशक्तितः ।
प्रदास्यतिद्विजाग्र्येभ्यः स्वल्पां यो वापि दक्षिणाम् ॥ 13.55 ॥
13.m: or who, unable to give food, according to his capacity will give wild greens / to the foremost twice-born, or even a very small gift;

13.s:
tatrāpyasāmarthyayutaḥ karāgrāgrasthitāṃstilān .
praṇamya dvijamukhyāya kasmaicid dvija dāsyati .. 13.56 ..
13.d:
तत्राप्यसामर्थ्ययुतः कराग्राग्रस्थितांस्तिलान् ।
प्रणम्य द्विजमुख्याय कस्मैचिद् द्विज दास्यति ॥ 13.56 ॥
13.m: or being unable even in that, O twice-born, will bow / and give sesame seeds held on the tips of his fingers to some eminent twice-born;

13.s:
tilaiḥ saptāṣṭabhirvāpi samavetāṃ jalāñjalim .
bhaktinamraḥ samuddiśyāpyasmākaṃ saṃpradāsyati .. 13.57 ..
13.d:
तिलैः सप्ताष्टभिर्वापि समवेतां जलाञ्जलिम् ।
भक्तिनम्रः समुद्दिश्याप्यस्माकं संप्रदास्यति ॥ 13.57 ॥
13.m: or humble with devotion, will offer a handful of water / accompanied by seven or eight sesame seeds, intending it for us;

13.s:
yataḥ kutaścit saṃprāpya gobhyo vāpi gavāhnikam .
abhāve prīṇayatyasmān bhaktyā yuktaḥ pradāsyati .. 13.58 ..
13.d:
यतः कुतश्चित् संप्राप्य गोभ्यो वापि गवाह्निकम् ।
अभावे प्रीणयत्यस्मान् भक्त्या युक्तः प्रदास्यति ॥ 13.58 ॥
13.m: or having obtained it from anywhere, will give cows' daily fodder to cows, / or in their absence, will gladden us endowed with devotion;

13.s:
sarvābhāve vanaṃ gatvā kakṣāmūlapradarśakaḥ .
sūryādilokapālānāmidamuccaiḥ paṭhiṣyati .. 13.59 ..
13.d:
सर्वाभावे वनं गत्वा कक्षामूलप्रदर्शकः ।
सूर्यादिलोकपालानामिदमुच्चैः पठिष्यति ॥ 13.59 ॥
13.m: or in the absence of everything, will go into the forest, expose his armpits, / and recite this aloud to the sun and other world-protectors:

13.s:
na me'sti vittaṃ na dhanaṃ na cānya-
cchrāddhasya yogyaṃ svapitṝn nato'smi .
tṛpyantu bhaktyā pitaro mayaitau
bhujau tatau vartmani mārutasya .. 13.60 ..
13.d:
न मेऽस्ति वित्तं न धनं न चान्य-
च्छ्राद्धस्य योग्यं स्वपितॄन् नतोऽस्मि ।
तृप्यन्तु भक्त्या पितरो मयैतौ
भुजौ ततौ वर्त्मनि मारुतस्य ॥ 13.60 ॥
13.m: "I have no property, no wealth, nor anything else / suitable for a śrāddha; I bow to my ancestors. / May the ancestors be satisfied by my devotion; these two / arms of mine are raised into the path of the wind."'

13.s:
ityetat pitṛbhirgītaṃ bhāvābhāvaprayojanam .
kṛtaṃ tena bhavecchrāddhaṃ ya evaṃ kurute dvija .. 13.61 ..
13.d:
इत्येतत् पितृभिर्गीतं भावाभावप्रयोजनम् ।
कृतं तेन भवेच्छ्राद्धं य एवं कुरुते द्विज ॥ 13.61 ॥
13.m: Thus this, sung by the ancestors, serves in abundance and in want. / By him who acts thus, O twice-born, the śrāddha is accomplished.

13.s: .. iti śrīvarāhapurāṇe bhagavacchāstre trayodaśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 13 ..
13.d: ॥ इति श्रीवराहपुराणे भगवच्छास्त्रे त्रयोदशोऽध्यायः ॥ 13 ॥
13.m: Thus ends the thirteenth chapter in the glorious Varāha Purāṇa, the sacred teaching of the Lord.

14.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca .
etanme kathitaṃ pūrvaṃ brahmaputreṇa dhīmatā .
sanakānujena viprarṣe brāhmaṇān śrṛṇu sāṃpratam .. 14.1 ..
14.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ।
एतन्मे कथितं पूर्वं ब्रह्मपुत्रेण धीमता ।
सनकानुजेन विप्रर्षे ब्राह्मणान् श्रृणु सांप्रतम् ॥ 14.1 ॥
14.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / This was formerly told to me by the wise son of Brahmā, / the younger brother of Sanaka, O Brahmin sage. Now hear about the Brahmins [to be invited]:

14.s:
triṇāciketastrimadhustrisuparṇaḥ ṣaḍaṅgavit .
vedavit śrotriyo yogī tathā vai jyoṣṭhasāmagaḥ .. 14.2 ..
14.d:
त्रिणाचिकेतस्त्रिमधुस्त्रिसुपर्णः षडङ्गवित् ।
वेदवित् श्रोत्रियो योगी तथा वै ज्योष्ठसामगः ॥ 14.2 ॥
14.m: one who maintains the three Nāciketa fires, knows the Trimadhu, recites the Trisuparṇa, knows the six auxiliary limbs, / knows the Veda, is learned in Vedic lore, is a yogin, and sings the Jyeṣṭhasāman;

14.s:
ṛtvijaṃ bhāgineyaṃ ca dauhitraṃ śvasuraṃ tathā .
jāmātaraṃ mātulaṃ ca taponiṣṭhaṃ ca brāhmaṇam .. 14.3 ..
14.d:
ऋत्विजं भागिनेयं च दौहित्रं श्वसुरं तथा ।
जामातरं मातुलं च तपोनिष्ठं च ब्राह्मणम् ॥ 14.3 ॥
14.m: the officiating priest, a sister's son, a daughter's son, a father-in-law, / a son-in-law, a maternal uncle, and an ascetic Brahmin;

14.s:
pañcāgnyabhirataṃ caiva śiṣyaṃ saṃbandhinaṃ tathā .
mātāpitṛrataṃ caiva etāñchrāddhe niyojayet .. 14.4 ..
14.d:
पञ्चाग्न्यभिरतं चैव शिष्यं संबन्धिनं तथा ।
मातापितृरतं चैव एताञ्छ्राद्धे नियोजयेत् ॥ 14.4 ॥
14.m: one devoted to the five sacred fires, a disciple, a relative, / and one devoted to mother and father—these one should employ in the śrāddha.

14.s:
mitradhruk kunakhī caiva śyāvadantastathā dvijaḥ .
kanyādūṣayitā vahnivedojjhaḥ somavikrayī .. 14.5 ..
14.d:
मित्रध्रुक् कुनखी चैव श्यावदन्तस्तथा द्विजः ।
कन्यादूषयिता वह्निवेदोज्झः सोमविक्रयी ॥ 14.5 ॥
14.m: A betrayer of friends, one with deformed nails, a twice-born with black teeth, / a defiler of maidens, one who has abandoned the sacred fire and the Veda, a seller of soma,

14.s:
abhiśaptastathā stenaḥ piśuno grāmayājakaḥ .
bhṛtakādhyāpakaścaiva bhṛtakādhyāpitaśca yaḥ .. 14.6 ..
14.d:
अभिशप्तस्तथा स्तेनः पिशुनो ग्रामयाजकः ।
भृतकाध्यापकश्चैव भृतकाध्यापितश्च यः ॥ 14.6 ॥
14.m: Likewise, an accursed man, a thief, a slanderer, a village priest, / one who teaches for a wage, and one who is taught for a wage,

14.s:
parapūrvāpatiścaiva mātāpitrostathojjhakaḥ .
vṛṣalīsūtipoṣyaśca vṛṣalīpatireva ca .
tathā devalakaścāpi śrāddhe nārhanti ketanam .. 14.7 ..
14.d:
परपूर्वापतिश्चैव मातापित्रोस्तथोज्झकः ।
वृषलीसूतिपोष्यश्च वृषलीपतिरेव च ।
तथा देवलकश्चापि श्राद्धे नार्हन्ति केतनम् ॥ 14.7 ॥
14.m: the husband of a woman previously married to another, one who abandons his parents, / one maintained by the offspring of a Śūdra woman, the husband of a Śūdra woman, / and a temple priest—these do not deserve an invitation at a śrāddha.

14.s:
prathame'hni budhaḥ kuryād viprāgryāṇāṃ nimantraṇam .
ānimantrya dvijān gehamāgatān bhojayed yatīn .. 14.8 ..
14.d:
प्रथमेऽह्नि बुधः कुर्याद् विप्राग्र्याणां निमन्त्रणम् ।
आनिमन्त्र्य द्विजान् गेहमागतान् भोजयेद् यतीन् ॥ 14.8 ॥
14.m: On the day before, a wise man should invite the foremost of brahmins; / having invited [them], he should feed ascetics who arrive at his house.

14.s:
pādaśaucādinā gehamāgatān bhojayed dvijān .
pavitrapāṇirācāntānāsaneṣūpaveśayet .. 14.9 ..
14.d:
पादशौचादिना गेहमागतान् भोजयेद् द्विजान् ।
पवित्रपाणिराचान्तानासनेषूपवेशयेत् ॥ 14.9 ॥
14.m: He should feed the brahmins who have come to his house, starting with the washing of their feet; / with kuśa grass in his hand, he should seat them on their seats after they have sipped water.

14.s:
pitṝṇāmayujo yugmān devānāmapi yojayet .
devānāmekamekaṃ vā pitṝṇāṃ ca niyojayet .. 14.10 ..
14.d:
पितॄणामयुजो युग्मान् देवानामपि योजयेत् ।
देवानामेकमेकं वा पितॄणां च नियोजयेत् ॥ 14.10 ॥
14.m: He should engage an odd number [of brahmins] for the ancestors, and an even number for the gods; / or he may assign one for the gods and one for the ancestors.

14.s:
tathā mātāmahaśrāddhaṃ vaiśvadevasamanvitam .
kurvīta bhaktisaṃpannasaktantraṃ vā vaiśvadevikam .. 14.11 ..
14.d:
तथा मातामहश्राद्धं वैश्वदेवसमन्वितम् ।
कुर्वीत भक्तिसंपन्नसक्तन्त्रं वा वैश्वदेविकम् ॥ 14.11 ॥
14.m: Likewise, endowed with devotion, he should perform the śrāddha for the maternal grandfather accompanied by the Vaiśvadeva, / or combine the ritual procedure with that of the Vaiśvadeva.

14.s:
prāṅmukhaṃ bhojabhed vipraṃ devānāmubhayātmakam .
pitṛpaitāmahānāṃ ca bhojayeccāpyudaṅmukhān .. 14.12 ..
14.d:
प्राङ्मुखं भोजभेद् विप्रं देवानामुभयात्मकम् ।
पितृपैतामहानां च भोजयेच्चाप्युदङ्मुखान् ॥ 14.12 ॥
14.m: He should feed facing east the brahmin who represents both the gods, / and he should feed facing north those for the father and paternal ancestors.

14.s:
pṛthak tayoḥ kecidāhuḥ śrāddhasya karaṇaṃ dvija .
ekatraikena pākena vadantyanye maharṣayaḥ .. 14.13 ..
14.d:
पृथक् तयोः केचिदाहुः श्राद्धस्य करणं द्विज ।
एकत्रैकेन पाकेन वदन्त्यन्ये महर्षयः ॥ 14.13 ॥
14.m: Some say the performance of the two śrāddhas should be separate, O twice-born; / other great sages declare it to be in one place with a single cooking.

14.s:
viṣṭarārthaṃ kuśān dattvā saṃpūjyārghavidhānataḥ .
kuryādāvāhanaṃ prājño devānāṃ tadanujñayā .. 14.14 ..
14.d:
विष्टरार्थं कुशान् दत्त्वा संपूज्यार्घविधानतः ।
कुर्यादावाहनं प्राज्ञो देवानां तदनुज्ञया ॥ 14.14 ॥
14.m: Having offered kuśa grass for a seat and worshipped according to the rite of water for hospitality, / the wise man, with their permission, should perform the invocation of the gods.

14.s:
yavāmbunā ca devānāṃ dadyādarghyaṃ vidhānavit .
sugandhadhūpadīpāṃśca dattvā tebhyo yathāvidhi .
pitṝṇāmapasakavyena sarvamevopakalpayet .. 14.15 ..
14.d:
यवाम्बुना च देवानां दद्यादर्घ्यं विधानवित् ।
सुगन्धधूपदीपांश्च दत्त्वा तेभ्यो यथाविधि ।
पितॄणामपसकव्येन सर्वमेवोपकल्पयेत् ॥ 14.15 ॥
14.m: And the knower of the rite should offer water for hospitality to the gods with barley-water; / having offered fragrant incense and lamps to them according to rule, / he should arrange everything for the ancestors with the sacred thread over the right shoulder.

14.s:
anujñāṃ ca tataḥ prāpya dattvā darbhān dvidhākṛtān .
mantrapūrvaṃ pitṝṇāṃ tu kuryādāvāhanaṃ budhaḥ .
tilāmbunā cāpasavyaṃ dadyādardhyādikaṃ budhaḥ .. 14.16 ..
14.d:
अनुज्ञां च ततः प्राप्य दत्त्वा दर्भान् द्विधाकृतान् ।
मन्त्रपूर्वं पितॄणां तु कुर्यादावाहनं बुधः ।
तिलाम्बुना चापसव्यं दद्यादर्ध्यादिकं बुधः ॥ 14.16 ॥
14.m: Then, having obtained permission and offered darbha grass split in two, / the wise man should perform the invocation of the ancestors preceded by mantras; / and with the sacred thread over the right shoulder, the wise man should offer water for hospitality and the like with sesame-water.

14.s:
kāle tatrātithiṃ prāptamannakāmaṃ dvijādhvagam .
brāhmaṇairabhyanujñātaḥ kāmaṃ tamapi pūjayet .. 14.17 ..
14.d:
काले तत्रातिथिं प्राप्तमन्नकामं द्विजाध्वगम् ।
ब्राह्मणैरभ्यनुज्ञातः कामं तमपि पूजयेत् ॥ 14.17 ॥
14.m: If a wandering twice-born guest seeking food arrives at that time, / permitted by the brahmins, he should gladly honour him as well.

14.s:
yogino vividhai rūpairnarāṇāmupakāriṇaḥ .
bhramanti pṛthivīmetāmavijñātasvarūpiṇaḥ .. 14.18 ..
14.d:
योगिनो विविधै रूपैर्नराणामुपकारिणः ।
भ्रमन्ति पृथिवीमेतामविज्ञातस्वरूपिणः ॥ 14.18 ॥
14.m: Benefactors of humanity, yogins wander this earth in various forms, / their true nature unrecognized.

14.s:
tasmādabhyarcayet prāptaṃ śrāddhakāle'tithiṃ budhaḥ .
śrāddhakriyāphalaṃ hanti dvijendrāpūjito'tithiḥ .. 14.19 ..
14.d:
तस्मादभ्यर्चयेत् प्राप्तं श्राद्धकालेऽतिथिं बुधः ।
श्राद्धक्रियाफलं हन्ति द्विजेन्द्रापूजितोऽतिथिः ॥ 14.19 ॥
14.m: Therefore, the wise man should honour a guest who arrives at the time of the śrāddha; / an unhonoured guest destroys the fruit of the śrāddha rite, O best of the twice-born.

14.s:
juhuyād vyañjanaṃ kṣārairvarjyamannaṃ tato'nale .
anujñāto dbijaistaistu triḥ kṛtvā puruṣarṣabha .. 14.20 ..
14.d:
जुहुयाद् व्यञ्जनं क्षारैर्वर्ज्यमन्नं ततोऽनले ।
अनुज्ञातो द्बिजैस्तैस्तु त्रिः कृत्वा पुरुषर्षभ ॥ 14.20 ॥
14.m: Then, permitted by those twice-born, O bull among men, / having done so thrice, he should offer into the fire food with condiment, free of salt.

14.s:
agnaye kavyavāhanāya svāheti prathamāhutiḥ .
somāya vai pitṛmate dātavyā tadanantaram .. 14.21 ..
14.d:
अग्नये कव्यवाहनाय स्वाहेति प्रथमाहुतिः ।
सोमाय वै पितृमते दातव्या तदनन्तरम् ॥ 14.21 ॥
14.m: The first oblation is: 'To Agni, bearer of ancestral offerings, svāhā'; / immediately after that, an oblation should be given to Soma accompanied by the ancestors.

14.s:
vaivasvatāya caivānyā tṛtīyā dīyatāhutiḥ .
hutāvaśiṣṭamalpālpaṃ viprapātreṣu nirvapet .. 14.22 ..
14.d:
वैवस्वताय चैवान्या तृतीया दीयताहुतिः ।
हुतावशिष्टमल्पाल्पं विप्रपात्रेषु निर्वपेत् ॥ 14.22 ॥
14.m: And let another, a third oblation, be given to Vaivasvata; / he should distribute a very small portion of the remainder of the oblation into the vessels of the brahmins.

14.s:
tato'nnaṃ mṛṣṭamatyarthamabhīṣṭamabhisaṃskṛtam .
dattvā juṣadhvamicchāto vācyametadaniṣṭhuram .. 14.23 ..
14.d:
ततोऽन्नं मृष्टमत्यर्थमभीष्टमभिसंस्कृतम् ।
दत्त्वा जुषध्वमिच्छातो वाच्यमेतदनिष्ठुरम् ॥ 14.23 ॥
14.m: Then, having served exceedingly delicious, desirable, and carefully prepared food, / this gentle phrase should be spoken: 'Enjoy it as you please.'

14.s:
bhoktavyaṃ taiśca taccittairmaunibhiḥ sumukhaiḥ sukham .
akrudhyatā atvaratā deyaṃ tenāpi bhaktitaḥ .. 14.24 ..
14.d:
भोक्तव्यं तैश्च तच्चित्तैर्मौनिभिः सुमुखैः सुखम् ।
अक्रुध्यता अत्वरता देयं तेनापि भक्तितः ॥ 14.24 ॥
14.m: And it should be eaten by them with focused minds, in silence, with pleasant countenances, and at ease; / it should also be served by him with devotion, without anger and without haste.

14.s:
rakṣoghnamantrapaṭhanaṃ bhūmerāstaraṇaṃ tilaiḥ .
kṛtvā'dhyeyāśca pitarasta eva dvijasattamāḥ .. 14.25 ..
14.d:
रक्षोघ्नमन्त्रपठनं भूमेरास्तरणं तिलैः ।
कृत्वाऽध्येयाश्च पितरस्त एव द्विजसत्तमाः ॥ 14.25 ॥
14.m: Having recited the demon-slaying mantras and strewn the ground with sesame seeds, / the ancestors should be meditated upon as those very foremost of the twice-born:

14.s:
pitā pitāmahaścaiva tathaiva prapitāmahaḥ .
mama tṛptiṃ prayāntvadya homāpyāyitamūrttayaḥ .. 14.26 ..
14.d:
पिता पितामहश्चैव तथैव प्रपितामहः ।
मम तृप्तिं प्रयान्त्वद्य होमाप्यायितमूर्त्तयः ॥ 14.26 ॥
14.m: 'May my father, paternal grandfather, and likewise great-grandfather, / their forms satisfied by the fire-offering, attain contentment today through me!

14.s:
pitāpitāmahaścaiva tathaiva prapitāmahaḥ .
mama tṛptiṃ prayāntvadya vipradeheṣu saṃsthitāḥ .. 14.27 ..
14.d:
पितापितामहश्चैव तथैव प्रपितामहः ।
मम तृप्तिं प्रयान्त्वद्य विप्रदेहेषु संस्थिताः ॥ 14.27 ॥
14.m: May my father, paternal grandfather, and likewise great-grandfather, / dwelling within the bodies of the brahmins, attain contentment today through me!

14.s:
pitā pitāmahaścaiva tathaiva prapitāmahaḥ .
tṛptiṃ prayāntu piṇḍeṣu mayā datteṣu bhūtale .. 14.28 ..
14.d:
पिता पितामहश्चैव तथैव प्रपितामहः ।
तृप्तिं प्रयान्तु पिण्डेषु मया दत्तेषु भूतले ॥ 14.28 ॥
14.m: May my father, paternal grandfather, and likewise great-grandfather, / attain contentment in the balls of rice offered by me on the ground!

14.s:
pitā pitāmahaścaiva tathaiva prapitāmahaḥ .
tṛptiṃ prayāntu me bhaktyā yanmayaitadudāhṛtam .. 14.29 ..
14.d:
पिता पितामहश्चैव तथैव प्रपितामहः ।
तृप्तिं प्रयान्तु मे भक्त्या यन्मयैतदुदाहृतम् ॥ 14.29 ॥
14.m: May my father, paternal grandfather, and likewise great-grandfather, / attain contentment through my devotion, in that this has been recited by me!

14.s:
mātāmahastṛptimupaitu tasya
tathā pitā tasya pitā tato'nyaḥ .
viśve'tha devāḥ paramāṃ prayāntu
tṛptiṃ praṇaśyantu ca yātudhānāḥ .. 14.30 ..
14.d:
मातामहस्तृप्तिमुपैतु तस्य
तथा पिता तस्य पिता ततोऽन्यः ।
विश्वेऽथ देवाः परमां प्रयान्तु
तृप्तिं प्रणश्यन्तु च यातुधानाः ॥ 14.30 ॥
14.m: May the maternal grandfather attain contentment, / likewise his father, and the other father beyond him; / then may all the gods attain supreme contentment, / and may the evil spirits perish!

14.s:
yajñeśvaro havyasamastakavya-
bhoktā'vyayātmā harirīśvaro'tra .
tatsannidhānādapayāntu sadyo
rakṣāṃsyaśeṣāṇyasurāśca sarve .. 14.31 ..
14.d:
यज्ञेश्वरो हव्यसमस्तकव्य-
भोक्ताऽव्ययात्मा हरिरीश्वरोऽत्र ।
तत्सन्निधानादपयान्तु सद्यो
रक्षांस्यशेषाण्यसुराश्च सर्वे ॥ 14.31 ॥
14.m: Hari, the lord of sacrifice, the consumer of all oblations to gods and ancestors, / the imperishable Self, is the Lord here; / by his presence, let all the demons / and all the asuras instantly depart!'

14.s:
tṛpteṣveteṣu vipreṣu kiredannaṃ mahītale .
dadyādācamanārthāya tebhyo vāri sakṛtsakṛt .. 14.32 ..
14.d:
तृप्तेष्वेतेषु विप्रेषु किरेदन्नं महीतले ।
दद्यादाचमनार्थाय तेभ्यो वारि सकृत्सकृत् ॥ 14.32 ॥
14.m: When these brahmins are satisfied, he should scatter food on the ground; / he should give water to them, each in turn, for sipping.

14.s:
sutṛptaistairanujñātaḥ sarveṇānnena bhūtale .
salilena tataḥ piṇḍān samāgṛhya samāhitaḥ .. 14.33 ..
14.d:
सुतृप्तैस्तैरनुज्ञातः सर्वेणान्नेन भूतले ।
सलिलेन ततः पिण्डान् समागृह्य समाहितः ॥ 14.33 ॥
14.m: Permitted with all the food on the ground by those who are fully satisfied, / then, concentrated in mind, gathering the balls of rice with water,

14.s:
pitṛtīrthena salilaṃ tathaiva salilāñjalim .
mātāmahebhyastenaiva piṇḍāṃstīrthena nirvapet.
dakṣiṇāgreṣu darbheṣu puṣpadhūpādipūjitām .. 14.34 ..
14.d:
पितृतीर्थेन सलिलं तथैव सलिलाञ्जलिम् ।
मातामहेभ्यस्तेनैव पिण्डांस्तीर्थेन निर्वपेत्।
दक्षिणाग्रेषु दर्भेषु पुष्पधूपादिपूजिताम् ॥ 14.34 ॥
14.m: he should offer water via the pitṛtīrtha, and likewise a handful of water; / via that same tīrtha he should present the balls of rice to the maternal ancestors, / worshipped with flowers, incense, and the like, upon darbha grass with its tips pointing south.

14.s:
svapitre prathamaṃ piṇḍaṃ dadyāducchiṣṭasannidhau .
pitāmahāya caivānyaṃ tatpitre ca tathā'param .. 14.35 ..
14.d:
स्वपित्रे प्रथमं पिण्डं दद्यादुच्छिष्टसन्निधौ ।
पितामहाय चैवान्यं तत्पित्रे च तथाऽपरम् ॥ 14.35 ॥
14.m: He should offer the first ball of rice to his own father near the remnants of the meal, / another to his grandfather, and likewise another to the father of that [grandfather].

14.s:
darbhamūle lepabhujaḥ prīṇayellepagharṣaṇāt .
piṇḍe mātāmahe tadvad gandhamālyādisaṃyutaiḥ .. 14.36 ..
14.d:
दर्भमूले लेपभुजः प्रीणयेल्लेपघर्षणात् ।
पिण्डे मातामहे तद्वद् गन्धमाल्यादिसंयुतैः ॥ 14.36 ॥
14.m: At the root of the darbha grass he should satisfy the eaters of the remnants by wiping off the residues; / likewise for the maternal grandfather's ball of rice, along with perfumes, garlands, and the like.

14.s:
pūjayitvā dvijāgryāṇāṃ dadyādācamanaṃ budhaḥ .
paitrebhyaḥ prathamaṃ bhaktyā tanmanasko dvijeśvara .. 14.37 ..
14.d:
पूजयित्वा द्विजाग्र्याणां दद्यादाचमनं बुधः ।
पैत्रेभ्यः प्रथमं भक्त्या तन्मनस्को द्विजेश्वर ॥ 14.37 ॥
14.m: Having worshipped, the wise man, with his mind fixed on that, / should offer water for sipping to the foremost twice-born, first to those representing the ancestors, O lord of the twice-born.

14.s:
susvadhetyāśiṣā yuktāṃ dadyācchaktyā ca dakṣiṇām .
dattvā ca dakṣiṇāṃ tebhyo vācayed vaiśvadevikān .
prīyantāmiti ye viśve devāstena itīrayet .. 14.38 ..
14.d:
सुस्वधेत्याशिषा युक्तां दद्याच्छक्त्या च दक्षिणाम् ।
दत्त्वा च दक्षिणां तेभ्यो वाचयेद् वैश्वदेविकान् ।
प्रीयन्तामिति ये विश्वे देवास्तेन इतीरयेत् ॥ 14.38 ॥
14.m: He should give a sacrificial fee according to his means, accompanied by the blessing 'May there be good svadhā'; / and having given the sacrificial fee to them, he should make those representing the Vaiśvadeva recite [the benediction]: / he should say, 'May those who are the All-gods be pleased.'

14.s:
tatheti cokte tairvipraiḥ prārthanīyāstathāśiṣaḥ .
paścād visarjayed devān pūrvaṃ paitrānmahāmate .. 14.39 ..
14.d:
तथेति चोक्ते तैर्विप्रैः प्रार्थनीयास्तथाशिषः ।
पश्चाद् विसर्जयेद् देवान् पूर्वं पैत्रान्महामते ॥ 14.39 ॥
14.m: And when 'So be it' is spoken by those brahmins, blessings should likewise be requested; / afterwards he should dismiss the gods, and first those for the ancestors, O wise one.

14.s:
mātāmahānāmapyevaṃ saha devaiḥ kramaḥ smṛtaḥ .
bhojane ca svaśaktyā ca dāne tadvad visarjjane .
āpādaśaucanāt pūrvaṃ kuryādeva dvijanmasu .. 14.40 ..
14.d:
मातामहानामप्येवं सह देवैः क्रमः स्मृतः ।
भोजने च स्वशक्त्या च दाने तद्वद् विसर्ज्जने ।
आपादशौचनात् पूर्वं कुर्यादेव द्विजन्मसु ॥ 14.40 ॥
14.m: In this way, the order for the maternal ancestors along with the gods is also taught, / in feeding, in giving according to one's means, and likewise in dismissal; / he should perform this among the twice-born, beginning from the washing of feet.

14.s:
jānantaṃ prathamaṃ pitryaṃ tathā mātāmaheṣu ca .
visarjayet prītivacaḥ saṃmānyābhyarthitāṃstataḥ .
nivarttetābhyanujñāta ādvārāntamanuvrajet .. 14.41 ..
14.d:
जानन्तं प्रथमं पित्र्यं तथा मातामहेषु च ।
विसर्जयेत् प्रीतिवचः संमान्याभ्यर्थितांस्ततः ।
निवर्त्तेताभ्यनुज्ञात आद्वारान्तमनुव्रजेत् ॥ 14.41 ॥
14.m: Acknowledging first the ancestral rite, and likewise among the maternal grandfathers, / having honoured and requested them, he should dismiss them with affectionate words; / permitted by them, he should turn back, having accompanied them as far as the doorway.

14.s:
tatastu vaiśvadevākhyāṃ kuryānnityakriyāṃ tataḥ .
bhuñjīyācca samaṃ pūjya bhṛtyabandhubhirātmanā .. 14.42 ..
14.d:
ततस्तु वैश्वदेवाख्यां कुर्यान्नित्यक्रियां ततः ।
भुञ्जीयाच्च समं पूज्य भृत्यबन्धुभिरात्मना ॥ 14.42 ॥
14.m: Thereafter, he should perform the daily rite called the Vaiśvadeva; / and having worshipped, he should eat himself together with his servants and relatives.

14.s:
evaṃ śrāddhaṃ budhaḥ kuryāt pitryaṃ mātāmahaṃ tathā .
śrāddhairāpyāyitā dadyuḥ sarvān kāmān pitāmahāḥ .. 14.43 ..
14.d:
एवं श्राद्धं बुधः कुर्यात् पित्र्यं मातामहं तथा ।
श्राद्धैराप्यायिता दद्युः सर्वान् कामान् पितामहाः ॥ 14.43 ॥
14.m: In this manner the wise man should perform the śrāddha for the paternal and maternal ancestors; / gratified by the śrāddhas, the ancestors will grant all desires.

14.s:
trīṇi śrāddhe pavitrāṇi dauhitraḥ kutapastilāḥ .
rajatasya tathā dānaṃ tathā saṃdarśanādikam .. 14.44 ..
14.d:
त्रीणि श्राद्धे पवित्राणि दौहित्रः कुतपस्तिलाः ।
रजतस्य तथा दानं तथा संदर्शनादिकम् ॥ 14.44 ॥
14.m: Three things are purifying at a śrāddha: a daughter's son, a kutapa blanket, and sesame seeds; / likewise the giving of silver, as well as the sight of it and so forth.

14.s:
varjyastu kurvatā śrāddhaṃ krodho'dhvagamamaṃ tvarā .
bhokturapyatra viprendra trayametanna saṃśayaḥ .. 14.45 ..
14.d:
वर्ज्यस्तु कुर्वता श्राद्धं क्रोधोऽध्वगममं त्वरा ।
भोक्तुरप्यत्र विप्रेन्द्र त्रयमेतन्न संशयः ॥ 14.45 ॥
14.m: Anger, traveling on a road, and haste should be avoided by one performing a śrāddha; / and for the eater too, O best of vipras, there is no doubt regarding these three. 14.45

14.s:
viśvedevāḥ sapitarastathā mātāmahā dvija .
kulaṃ cāpyāyate puṃsāṃ sarvaṃ śrāddhaṃ prakurvatām .. 14.46 ..
14.d:
विश्वेदेवाः सपितरस्तथा मातामहा द्विज ।
कुलं चाप्यायते पुंसां सर्वं श्राद्धं प्रकुर्वताम् ॥ 14.46 ॥
14.m: The Viśvedevas, along with the ancestors and maternal grandfathers, O dvija, / and the entire family of men performing the śrāddha are nourished. 14.46

14.s:
somādhāraḥ pitṛgaṇo yogādhāraśca candramāḥ .
śrāddhaṃ yoginiyuktaṃ tu tasmad viprendra śasyate .. 14.47 ..
14.d:
सोमाधारः पितृगणो योगाधारश्च चन्द्रमाः ।
श्राद्धं योगिनियुक्तं तु तस्मद् विप्रेन्द्र शस्यते ॥ 14.47 ॥
14.m: The host of ancestors has Soma as its foundation, and the moon has yoga as its foundation. / Therefore, O best of vipras, a śrāddha attended by a yogin is praised. 14.47

14.s:
sahastrasyāpi viprāṇāṃ yogī cet purataḥ sthitaḥ .
sarvān bhoktṝṃstārayati yajamānaṃ tathā dvija .. 14.48 ..
14.d:
सहस्त्रस्यापि विप्राणां योगी चेत् पुरतः स्थितः ।
सर्वान् भोक्तॄंस्तारयति यजमानं तथा द्विज ॥ 14.48 ॥
14.m: Even among a thousand vipras, if a single yogin stands before them, / he delivers all who eat, and likewise the patron of the sacrifice, O dvija. 14.48

14.s:
mahyaṃ sanatkumāreṇa pūrvakalpe dvijottama .
kathitaṃ vāyunā cāpi devānāṃ śaṃbhunā tathā .. 14.49 ..
14.d:
मह्यं सनत्कुमारेण पूर्वकल्पे द्विजोत्तम ।
कथितं वायुना चापि देवानां शंभुना तथा ॥ 14.49 ॥
14.m: In a former kalpa, O best of dvijas, this was told to me by Sanatkumāra, / and by Vāyu, and by Śambhu to the gods; 14.49

14.s:
ṛṣīṇāṃ śaktiputreṇa tathā maitreyasaṃjñite .
bhaviṣyati kramād yāvan mayā te kathitaṃ dvija .. 14.50 ..)
iyaṃ sarvapurāṇeṣu sāmānyā paitṛkī kriyā .
etat kramāt karmakāṇḍaṃ jñātvā mucyeta bandhanāt .. 14.51 ..
14.d:
ऋषीणां शक्तिपुत्रेण तथा मैत्रेयसंज्ञिते ।
भविष्यति क्रमाद् यावन् मया ते कथितं द्विज ॥ 14.50 ॥)
इयं सर्वपुराणेषु सामान्या पैतृकी क्रिया ।
एतत् क्रमात् कर्मकाण्डं ज्ञात्वा मुच्येत बन्धनात् ॥ 14.51 ॥
14.m:
By the son of Śakti among the ṛṣis, and likewise unto the one named Maitreya,
as it will come to pass in sequence, so has it been told to you by me, O twice-born one.

This ancestral rite is common to all Purāṇas;
having understood this ritual section in sequence, one is freed from bondage.

14.s:
etadāśritya nirvāṇaṃ ṛṣayaḥ saṃśitavratāḥ .
prāptā gauramukhedānīṃ tvamapyevaṃ paro bhava .. 14.52 ..
14.d:
एतदाश्रित्य निर्वाणं ऋषयः संशितव्रताः ।
प्राप्ता गौरमुखेदानीं त्वमप्येवं परो भव ॥ 14.52 ॥
14.m: Resorting to this, the ṛṣis of strict vows attained nirvāṇa. / O Gauramukha, now you too become devoted to this! 14.52

14.s:
iti te kathitaṃ bhaktyā pṛcchato dvijasattama .
pitṝn yaṣṭvā hariṃ dhyāyed yastasya kimataḥ param .
na tasmāt parataḥ pitryaṃ tantramastīti niścayaḥ .. 14.53 ..
14.d:
इति ते कथितं भक्त्या पृच्छतो द्विजसत्तम ।
पितॄन् यष्ट्वा हरिं ध्यायेद् यस्तस्य किमतः परम् ।
न तस्मात् परतः पित्र्यं तन्त्रमस्तीति निश्चयः ॥ 14.53 ॥
14.m: Thus it has been related to you who asked with devotion, O best of dvijas. / Having worshipped the ancestors, if one meditates on Hari, what could be higher than that? / There is no ancestral ritual superior to that; this is certain. 14.53

14.s: .. iti śrīvarāhapurāṇe bhagavacchāstre caturdaśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 14 ..
14.d: ॥ इति श्रीवराहपुराणे भगवच्छास्त्रे चतुर्दशोऽध्यायः ॥ 14 ॥
14.m: Thus ends the fourteenth chapter in the glorious Varāha Purāṇa, the scripture of the Lord. 14

14.s:
dharaṇyuvāca .
evaṃ śrāddhavidhiṃ śrutvā mārkaṇḍeyānmahāmuniḥ .
tadā gauramukho deva kimūrdhvaṃ kṛtavān vibho .. 15.1 ..
14.d:
धरण्युवाच ।
एवं श्राद्धविधिं श्रुत्वा मार्कण्डेयान्महामुनिः ।
तदा गौरमुखो देव किमूर्ध्वं कृतवान् विभो ॥ 15.1 ॥
14.m: Dharaṇī said: / Having thus heard the rules of the śrāddha from Mārkaṇḍeya, O god, / what did the great sage Gauramukha do thereafter, O all-pervading Lord? 15.1

15.s:
śrīvarāha uvāca .
etacchrutvā tadā dhātri pitṛtantraṃ mahāmuniḥ .
saṃsmārito janmaśataṃ mārkaṇḍeyena dhīmatā .. 15.2 ..
15.d:
श्रीवराह उवाच ।
एतच्छ्रुत्वा तदा धात्रि पितृतन्त्रं महामुनिः ।
संस्मारितो जन्मशतं मार्कण्डेयेन धीमता ॥ 15.2 ॥
15.m: Śrī Varāha said: / Having heard this ancestral ritual at that time, O Dhātrī, the great sage / was caused to remember a hundred births by the wise Mārkaṇḍeya. 15.2

15.s:
dharaṇyuvāca .
bhagavan gauramukhaḥ ko'sau anyajanmani kaḥ smṛtaḥ .
kathaṃ ca smṛtavān smṛtvā kiṃ cakāra ca sattamaḥ .. 15.3 ..
15.d:
धरण्युवाच ।
भगवन् गौरमुखः कोऽसौ अन्यजन्मनि कः स्मृतः ।
कथं च स्मृतवान् स्मृत्वा किं चकार च सत्तमः ॥ 15.3 ॥
15.m: Dharaṇī said: / O Lord, who was this Gauramukha? Who is he remembered to have been in another birth? / And how did he remember, and having remembered, what did that best of beings do? 15.3

15.s:
śrīvarāha uvāca .
bhṛgurāsīt svayaṃ sākṣādanyasmin brahma janmani .
tadanvayātmajastveṣa mārkaṇḍeyo mahāmuniḥ .. 15.4 ..
15.d:
श्रीवराह उवाच ।
भृगुरासीत् स्वयं साक्षादन्यस्मिन् ब्रह्म जन्मनि ।
तदन्वयात्मजस्त्वेष मार्कण्डेयो महामुनिः ॥ 15.4 ॥
15.m: Śrī Varāha said: / In another birth of Brahmā he was Bhṛgu himself in person. / And born of his lineage was this great sage Mārkaṇḍeya. 15.4

15.s:
putraistu bodhitā yūyaṃ sugatiṃ prāpsyatheti yat .
prāguktaṃ brahmaṇā tena mārkaṇḍeyena bodhitaḥ .. 15.5 ..
15.d:
पुत्रैस्तु बोधिता यूयं सुगतिं प्राप्स्यथेति यत् ।
प्रागुक्तं ब्रह्मणा तेन मार्कण्डेयेन बोधितः ॥ 15.5 ॥
15.m: Because it had previously been spoken by Brahmā: 'Instructed by your sons, you will attain a good state,' / he was instructed by that Mārkaṇḍeya. 15.5

15.s:
sasmāra sarvajanmāni smṛtvā caiva tu yatkṛtam .
tacchṛṇuṣva varārohe kathayāmi samāsataḥ .. 15.6 ..
15.d:
सस्मार सर्वजन्मानि स्मृत्वा चैव तु यत्कृतम् ।
तच्छृणुष्व वरारोहे कथयामि समासतः ॥ 15.6 ॥
15.m: He remembered all his births; and what he did having remembered, / hear that, O fair-hipped one, I shall tell in brief. 15.6

15.s:
evaṃ śrāddhavidhānena dvādaśābdaṃ tataḥ pitṝn .
iṣṭvā paścāddhareḥ stotraṃ sa munistūpacakrame .. 15.7 ..
15.d:
एवं श्राद्धविधानेन द्वादशाब्दं ततः पितॄन् ।
इष्ट्वा पश्चाद्धरेः स्तोत्रं स मुनिस्तूपचक्रमे ॥ 15.7 ॥
15.m: Having thus worshipped the ancestors according to the rules of śrāddha for twelve years, / the sage then afterwards commenced a hymn of praise to Hari. 15.7

15.s:
prabhāsaṃ nāma yattīrthaṃ triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam .
tatra daityāntakaṃ devaṃ stotuṃ gauramukhaḥ sthitaḥ .. 15.8 ..
15.d:
प्रभासं नाम यत्तीर्थं त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतम् ।
तत्र दैत्यान्तकं देवं स्तोतुं गौरमुखः स्थितः ॥ 15.8 ॥
15.m: At the holy ford named Prabhāsa, famed in the three worlds, / Gauramukha stood there to praise the god who destroys the Daityas. 15.8

15.s:
gauramukha uvāca .
stoṣye mahendraṃ ripudarpahaṃ śivaṃ
nārāyaṇaṃ brahmavidāṃ pratiṣṭhitam .
ādityacandrāśviyugasthamādyaṃ
purātanaṃ daityaharaṃ sadā harim .. 15.9 ..
15.d:
गौरमुख उवाच ।
स्तोष्ये महेन्द्रं रिपुदर्पहं शिवं
नारायणं ब्रह्मविदां प्रतिष्ठितम् ।
आदित्यचन्द्राश्वियुगस्थमाद्यं
पुरातनं दैत्यहरं सदा हरिम् ॥ 15.9 ॥
15.m: Gauramukha said: / I shall praise the great ruler, the destroyer of foes' pride, the auspicious one, / Nārāyaṇa, established in knowers of Brahman, / the primeval one who abides in the sun, moon, and the pair of Aśvins, / the ancient destroyer of the Daityas, Hari forever. 15.9

15.s:
cakāra mātsyaṃ vapurātmano yaḥ
purākṛtaṃ vedavināśakāle .
mahāmahīdhṛgvapuragrapuccha -
chaṭāhavārcciḥ suraśatruhādyaḥ .. 15.10 ..
15.d:
चकार मात्स्यं वपुरात्मनो यः
पुराकृतं वेदविनाशकाले ।
महामहीधृग्वपुरग्रपुच्छ -
छटाहवार्च्चिः सुरशत्रुहाद्यः ॥ 15.10 ॥
15.m: He who assumed of his own accord the form of a fish / in ancient times at the time of the destruction of the Vedas, / his body bearing the great earth, his flame of battle with the tip of his tail, / the primal destroyer of the gods' enemies; 15.10

15.s:
tathābdhimanthānakṛte girīndraṃ
dadhāra yaḥ kaurmmavapuḥ purāṇam .
hitecchayā yaḥ puruṣaḥ purāṇaḥ
prapātu māṃ daityaharaḥ sureśaḥ .. 15.11 ..
15.d:
तथाब्धिमन्थानकृते गिरीन्द्रं
दधार यः कौर्म्मवपुः पुराणम् ।
हितेच्छया यः पुरुषः पुराणः
प्रपातु मां दैत्यहरः सुरेशः ॥ 15.11 ॥
15.m: and who, for the churning of the ocean, bore the king of mountains, / the ancient one assuming the form of a tortoise; / the primal Puruṣa who, through desire for welfare, / destroys the Daityas, the lord of gods—may he protect me! 15.11

15.s:
mahāvarāhaḥ satataṃ pṛthivyās
talāttalaṃ prāviśad yo mahātmā .
yajñāṅgasaṃjñaḥ surasiddhavandyaḥ
sa pātu māṃ daityaharaḥ purāṇaḥ .. 15.12 ..
15.d:
महावराहः सततं पृथिव्यास्
तलात्तलं प्राविशद् यो महात्मा ।
यज्ञाङ्गसंज्ञः सुरसिद्धवन्द्यः
स पातु मां दैत्यहरः पुराणः ॥ 15.12 ॥
15.m: The great Varāha, that great-souled one who continuously / entered beneath the Earth to Talātala, / known as the limbs of sacrifice, praised by the gods and Siddhas, / the ancient destroyer of the Daityas—may he protect me! 15.12

15.s:
nṛsiṃharūpī ca bhavatyajastraṃ
yuge yuge yogivarograbhīmaḥ .
karālavaktraḥ kanakāgravarcā
ratnāśayo'smānasurāntako'vyāt .. 15.13 ..
15.d:
नृसिंहरूपी च भवत्यजस्त्रं
युगे युगे योगिवरोग्रभीमः ।
करालवक्त्रः कनकाग्रवर्चा
रत्नाशयोऽस्मानसुरान्तकोऽव्यात् ॥ 15.13 ॥
15.m: He who ceaselessly takes the form of the man-lion / age after age, terrible and fierce among the foremost of yogins, / with a dreadful face and the splendor of finest gold, / having a heart of jewels, the slayer of Asuras—may he protect us! 15.13

15.s:
balermakhadhvaṃsakṛte mahātmā
svāṃ gūḍhatāṃ yogavapuḥsvarūpaḥ .
sa daṇḍakāṣṭhā'jinalakṣaṇaḥ punaḥ
kṣitiṃ ca padā krāntavān yaḥ sa pātu .. 15.14 ..
15.d:
बलेर्मखध्वंसकृते महात्मा
स्वां गूढतां योगवपुःस्वरूपः ।
स दण्डकाष्ठाऽजिनलक्षणः पुनः
क्षितिं च पदा क्रान्तवान् यः स पातु ॥ 15.14 ॥
15.m: The great-souled one who, to destroy Bali's sacrifice, / assumed his own concealed form as the embodiment of yoga, / having the marks of a wooden staff and an antelope skin, and then / strode over the earth with a foot—may he protect! 15.14

15.s:
triḥsaptakṛtvo jagatīṃ jigāya
jitvā dadau kaśyapāya pracaṇḍaḥ .
sa jāmadagnyo'bhijanasya goptā
hiraṇyagarbho'surahā prapātu .. 15.15 ..
15.d:
त्रिःसप्तकृत्वो जगतीं जिगाय
जित्वा ददौ कश्यपाय प्रचण्डः ।
स जामदग्न्योऽभिजनस्य गोप्ता
हिरण्यगर्भोऽसुरहा प्रपातु ॥ 15.15 ॥
15.m: He who conquered the earth thrice seven times, / and having conquered it, the fierce one gave it to Kaśyapa, / that son of Jamadagni, protector of his lineage, / Hiranyagarbha, the slayer of Asuras—may he protect! 15.15

15.s:
catuḥprakāraṃ ca vapurya ādyaṃ
hairaṇyagarbhapratimānalakṣyam .
rāmādirūpairbahurūpabheda-
ścakāra so'smānasurāntako'vyāt .. 15.16 ..
15.d:
चतुःप्रकारं च वपुर्य आद्यं
हैरण्यगर्भप्रतिमानलक्ष्यम् ।
रामादिरूपैर्बहुरूपभेद-
श्चकार सोऽस्मानसुरान्तकोऽव्यात् ॥ 15.16 ॥
15.m: And who made his primal body fourfold, / having the form conceived as Hiraṇyagarbha, / divided into many forms through the forms of Rāma and others— / that slayer of Asuras, may he protect us! 15.16

15.s:
cāṇūrakaṃsāsuradarpabhīte-
rbhītāmarāṇāmabhayāya devaḥ .
yuge yuge vāsudevo babhūva
kalpe bhavatyadbhutarūpakārī .
yuge yuge kalkināmnā mahātmā
varṇasthitiṃ karttumanekamūrttiḥ .. 15.17 ..
15.d:
चाणूरकंसासुरदर्पभीते-
र्भीतामराणामभयाय देवः ।
युगे युगे वासुदेवो बभूव
कल्पे भवत्यद्भुतरूपकारी ।
युगे युगे कल्किनाम्ना महात्मा
वर्णस्थितिं कर्त्तुमनेकमूर्त्तिः ॥ 15.17 ॥
15.m: For granting fearlessness to the gods who were terrified / by fear of the pride of the Asuras Cāṇūra and Kaṃsa, / the god became Vāsudeva age after age; / in a kalpa he assumes wondrous forms; / age after age the great-souled one of many forms / is named Kalki to establish the social orders. 15.17

15.s:
sanātano brahmamayaḥ purāṇo
na yasya rūpaṃ surasiddhadaityāḥ .
paśyanti vijñānagatiṃ vihāya
athopyanekāni samarcvayanti .
matsyādirūpāṇi carāṇi so'vyāt .. 15.18 ..
15.d:
सनातनो ब्रह्ममयः पुराणो
न यस्य रूपं सुरसिद्धदैत्याः ।
पश्यन्ति विज्ञानगतिं विहाय
अथोप्यनेकानि समर्च्वयन्ति ।
मत्स्यादिरूपाणि चराणि सोऽव्यात् ॥ 15.18 ॥
15.m: Eternal, composed of Brahman, ancient, / whose form gods, Siddhas, and Daityas do not see / without the path of discernment, / though they worship many / mobile forms such as the Fish—may he protect! 15.18

15.s:
namo namaste puruṣottamāya
punaśca bhūyo'pi namo namaste .
namaḥ purastādatha pṛṣṭhataste
nayasva māṃ muktipadaṃ namaste .. 15.19 ..
15.d:
नमो नमस्ते पुरुषोत्तमाय
पुनश्च भूयोऽपि नमो नमस्ते ।
नमः पुरस्तादथ पृष्ठतस्ते
नयस्व मां मुक्तिपदं नमस्ते ॥ 15.19 ॥
15.m: Homage, homage to you, the supreme Puruṣa! / Once again and yet again, homage, homage to you! / Homage in front and then behind you! / Lead me to the state of liberation; homage to you! 15.19

15.s:
evaṃ namasyatastasya maharṣerbhāvitātmanaḥ .
pratyakṣatāṃ gato devaḥ svayaṃ cakragadādharaḥ .. 15.20 ..
15.d:
एवं नमस्यतस्तस्य महर्षेर्भावितात्मनः ।
प्रत्यक्षतां गतो देवः स्वयं चक्रगदाधरः ॥ 15.20 ॥
15.m: As that great sage of purified self was thus paying homage, / the god himself, bearing the discus and mace, became visible to his eyes. 15.20

15.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā tasya vijñānaṃ nistaraṅgaṃ svadehataḥ .
uttasthau so'pi taṃ labdhvā tasmin brahmaṇi śāśvate .
layaṃ jagāma devātmā tvapunarbhavasaṃjñite .. 15.21 ..
15.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा तस्य विज्ञानं निस्तरङ्गं स्वदेहतः ।
उत्तस्थौ सोऽपि तं लब्ध्वा तस्मिन् ब्रह्मणि शाश्वते ।
लयं जगाम देवात्मा त्वपुनर्भवसंज्ञिते ॥ 15.21 ॥
15.m: Having seen him, waveless discernment arose / from his own body; and having attained him, that divine-natured one / dissolved into that eternal Brahman called non-rebirth. 15.21

15.s: .. iti śrīvarāhapurāṇe bhagavacchāstre pañcadaśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 15 ..
15.d: ॥ इति श्रीवराहपुराणे भगवच्छास्त्रे पञ्चदशोऽध्यायः ॥ 15 ॥
15.m: Thus ends the fifteenth chapter in the glorious Varāha Purāṇa, the scripture of the Lord. 15

16.s:
dharaṇyuvāca .
tadā durvāsasā śapto devarājaḥ śatakratuḥ .
vasiṣyasi tvaṃ marttyeṣu supratīkasutena tu .. 16.1 ..
16.d:
धरण्युवाच ।
तदा दुर्वाससा शप्तो देवराजः शतक्रतुः ।
वसिष्यसि त्वं मर्त्त्येषु सुप्रतीकसुतेन तु ॥ 16.1 ॥
16.m: Dharaṇī said: / Then the king of gods, Śatakratu, was cursed by Durvāsas: / 'You shall live among mortals, / having been expelled from heaven by the son of Supratīka, O fool!' 16.1

16.s:
utsādito divo mūḍhetyevamuktastu bhūdhara .
indro marttyamupāgamya sarvadevasamanvitaḥ .. 16.2 ..
16.d:
उत्सादितो दिवो मूढेत्येवमुक्तस्तु भूधर ।
इन्द्रो मर्त्त्यमुपागम्य सर्वदेवसमन्वितः ॥ 16.2 ॥
16.m: Having been spoken to thus, O supporter of the earth, / Indra came to the mortal world accompanied by all the gods. 16.2

16.s:
kiṃ cakāra ca tasmiṃstu durjaye ca nipātite .
parameṣṭhinā bhagavatā tena yogaviduttamau .. 16.3 ..
16.d:
किं चकार च तस्मिंस्तु दुर्जये च निपातिते ।
परमेष्ठिना भगवता तेन योगविदुत्तमौ ॥ 16.3 ॥
16.m: And when that Durjaya was struck down / by that Lord Parameṣṭhin, the best among knowers of yoga, / what did he do? 16.3

16.s:
svarge vidyutsuvidyucca tau ca kiṃ cakratustadā .
etanme saṃśayaṃ deva kathayasva prasādataḥ .. 16.4 ..
16.d:
स्वर्गे विद्युत्सुविद्युच्च तौ च किं चक्रतुस्तदा ।
एतन्मे संशयं देव कथयस्व प्रसादतः ॥ 16.4 ॥
16.m: And what did Vidyut and Suvidyut do in heaven at that time? / Explain this doubt of mine, O Lord, through your favor. 16.4

16.s:
śrīvarāha uvāca .
dūrjayena jito dhātri devarājaḥ śatakratuḥ .
bhārate hi tadā varṣe vārāṇasyāṃ tu pūrvataḥ .
āśritya saṃsthito devaiḥ saha yakṣamahoragaiḥ .. 16.5 ..
16.d:
श्रीवराह उवाच ।
दूर्जयेन जितो धात्रि देवराजः शतक्रतुः ।
भारते हि तदा वर्षे वाराणस्यां तु पूर्वतः ।
आश्रित्य संस्थितो देवैः सह यक्षमहोरगैः ॥ 16.5 ॥
16.m: Śrī Varāha said: / Having been defeated by Durjaya, O Dhātrī, the king of gods, Śatakratu, / taking refuge to the east of Vārāṇasī in the land of Bhārata, / resided there together with the gods, Yakṣas, and great serpents. 16.5

16.s:
vidyutsuvidyucca tadā yogamāsthāya śobhane .
dīrghatāpajvaraṃ vāyukarmayogena saṃśritau ..
16.d:
विद्युत्सुविद्युच्च तदा योगमास्थाय शोभने ।
दीर्घतापज्वरं वायुकर्मयोगेन संश्रितौ ॥

16.s: lokapālāyitaṃ kṛtsnaṃ cakraturyogamāyayā .. 16.6 ..
16.d: लोकपालायितं कृत्स्नं चक्रतुर्योगमायया ॥ 16.6 ॥

16.s:
taṃ durjayaṃ mṛtaṃ śrutvā samudrāntaḥsthitaṃ tadā .
ānīya caturaṅgaṃ tu devān prati vijagmatuḥ .. 16.7 ..
16.d:
तं दुर्जयं मृतं श्रुत्वा समुद्रान्तःस्थितं तदा ।
आनीय चतुरङ्गं तु देवान् प्रति विजग्मतुः ॥ 16.7 ॥
16.m: Having heard that Durjaya was dead within the ocean, / they gathered a fourfold army and marched against the gods. // 16.7

16.s:
āgatya tau tadā daityau mahatsainyena parvatam .
himavantaṃ samāśritya saṃsthitau tu babhūvatuḥ .. 16.8 ..
16.d:
आगत्य तौ तदा दैत्यौ महत्सैन्येन पर्वतम् ।
हिमवन्तं समाश्रित्य संस्थितौ तु बभूवतुः ॥ 16.8 ॥
16.m: Those two Daityas came with a vast army, / and encamped on Mount Himavat. // 16.8

16.s:
devā api mahatsainyaṃ saṃhatya kṛtadaṃśitāḥ .
mantrayāñcakruravyagrā aindraṃ padamabhīpsavaḥ .. 16.9 ..
16.d:
देवा अपि महत्सैन्यं संहत्य कृतदंशिताः ।
मन्त्रयाञ्चक्रुरव्यग्रा ऐन्द्रं पदमभीप्सवः ॥ 16.9 ॥
16.m: The gods also gathered a vast army and donned their armor; / desiring to regain Indra's domain, they deliberated without agitation. // 16.9

16.s:
abravīt tatra devānāṃ gururāṅgiraso muniḥ .
gomedhena yajaghvaṃ vai prathamena tadantaram .. 16.10 ..
16.d:
अब्रवीत् तत्र देवानां गुरुराङ्गिरसो मुनिः ।
गोमेधेन यजघ्वं वै प्रथमेन तदन्तरम् ॥ 16.10 ॥
16.m: There the teacher of the gods, the sage born of Aṅgiras, said: / 'First perform a cow-sacrifice, and then, // 16.10

16.s:
yaṣṭavyaṃ kratubhiḥ sarvairekasthitirathāmarāḥ .
upadeśo mayā dattaḥ kriyatāṃ śīghrameṣa vai .. 16.11 ..
16.d:
यष्टव्यं क्रतुभिः सर्वैरेकस्थितिरथामराः ।
उपदेशो मया दत्तः क्रियतां शीघ्रमेष वै ॥ 16.11 ॥
16.m: you must sacrifice with all the rites as one, O immortals! / This instruction has been given by me; let it be carried out quickly!' // 16.11

16.s:
evamuktāstadā devā gāḥ paśūṃścānukalpya te .
mumucuścaraṇārthāya rakṣārthaṃ saramāṃ daduḥ .. 16.12 ..
16.d:
एवमुक्तास्तदा देवा गाः पशूंश्चानुकल्प्य ते ।
मुमुचुश्चरणार्थाय रक्षार्थं सरमां ददुः ॥ 16.12 ॥
16.m: Thus spoken to, the gods then prepared the sacrificial cows and animals; / they turned them loose to graze and appointed Saramā to guard them. // 16.12

16.s:
tāśca gāvo devaśunyā rakṣyamāṇā dharādhare .
tatra jagmustadā gāvaścarantyo yatra te'surāḥ .. 16.13 ..
16.d:
ताश्च गावो देवशुन्या रक्ष्यमाणा धराधरे ।
तत्र जग्मुस्तदा गावश्चरन्त्यो यत्र तेऽसुराः ॥ 16.13 ॥
16.m: And while guarded by the divine bitch on the mountain, / those grazing cows went to where those asuras were. // 16.13

16.s:
te ca gāvastu tā dṛṣṭvā śukramūcuḥ purohitam .
paśvarthaṃ devagā brahmaṃścāryante rakṣamāṇayā .
devaśūnyā saramayā vada kiṃ kriyate'dhunā .. 16.14 ..
16.d:
ते च गावस्तु ता दृष्ट्वा शुक्रमूचुः पुरोहितम् ।
पश्वर्थं देवगा ब्रह्मंश्चार्यन्ते रक्षमाणया ।
देवशून्या सरमया वद किं क्रियतेऽधुना ॥ 16.14 ॥
16.m: Seeing those cows, they said to Śukra, the priest: / 'O brāhmaṇa, cows meant for the sacrifice of the gods are grazing, guarded / by Saramā, the divine bitch. Tell us, what should be done now?' // 16.14

16.s:
evamuktastadā śukraḥ pratyuvācāsurāṃstadā .
etā gā hriyatāṃ śīghramasurā mā vilambatha .. 16.15 ..
16.d:
एवमुक्तस्तदा शुक्रः प्रत्युवाचासुरांस्तदा ।
एता गा ह्रियतां शीघ्रमसुरा मा विलम्बथ ॥ 16.15 ॥
16.m: Thus addressed, Śukra then replied to the asuras: / 'Seize these cows quickly, O asuras! Do not delay!' // 16.15

16.s:
evamuktāstadā daityā jahrustā gā yadṛcchayā .
hṛtāsu tāsu saramā mārgamanveṣaṇe ratā .. 16.16 ..
16.d:
एवमुक्तास्तदा दैत्या जह्रुस्ता गा यदृच्छया ।
हृतासु तासु सरमा मार्गमन्वेषणे रता ॥ 16.16 ॥
16.m: Thus told, the Daityas then seized those cows at will. / When they had been carried off, Saramā was intent on tracking their trail. // 16.16

16.s:
apaśyat sā diteḥ putrairnītā gāvo dharādhare .
daityairapi śunī dṛṣṭā dṛṣṭamārgā viśeṣataḥ .. 16.17 ..
16.d:
अपश्यत् सा दितेः पुत्रैर्नीता गावो धराधरे ।
दैत्यैरपि शुनी दृष्टा दृष्टमार्गा विशेषतः ॥ 16.17 ॥
16.m: She saw that the cows had been taken to the mountain by the sons of Diti; / and the bitch was also spotted by the Daityas, especially as she was tracking the path. // 16.17

16.s:
dṛṣṭvā te tāṃ ca sāmnaiva sāmapūrvamidaṃ vacaḥ .
āsāṃ gavāṃ tu dugdhvaiva kṣīraṃ tvaṃ sarame śubhe .. 16.18 ..
16.d:
दृष्ट्वा ते तां च साम्नैव सामपूर्वमिदं वचः ।
आसां गवां तु दुग्ध्वैव क्षीरं त्वं सरमे शुभे ॥ 16.18 ॥
16.m: Seeing her, they spoke these soothing words to conciliate her: / 'Having milked these cows, O auspicious Saramā, // 16.18

16.s:
pibasvaivamiti proktā tasyai tad dadurañjasā .
dattvā tu kṣīrapānaṃ tu tasyai te daityanāyakāḥ .. 16.19 ..
16.d:
पिबस्वैवमिति प्रोक्ता तस्यै तद् ददुरञ्जसा ।
दत्त्वा तु क्षीरपानं तु तस्यै ते दैत्यनायकाः ॥ 16.19 ॥
16.m: drink the milk!' So saying, they promptly gave it to her. / Having given her the drink of milk, those Daitya chiefs [said]: // 16.19

16.s:
mā bhadre devarājāya gāścemā vinivedaya .
evamuktvā tato daityā mumucustāṃ śunīṃ vane .. 16.20 ..
16.d:
मा भद्रे देवराजाय गाश्चेमा विनिवेदय ।
एवमुक्त्वा ततो दैत्या मुमुचुस्तां शुनीं वने ॥ 16.20 ॥
16.m: 'Gentle one, do not report these cows to the king of the gods!' / Having spoken thus, the Daityas then let the bitch go in the forest. // 16.20

16.s:
tairmuktā sā surāṃstūrṇaṃ jagāma khalu vepatī .
namaścakre ca devendraṃ saramā surasattamam .. 16.21 ..
16.d:
तैर्मुक्ता सा सुरांस्तूर्णं जगाम खलु वेपती ।
नमश्चक्रे च देवेन्द्रं सरमा सुरसत्तमम् ॥ 16.21 ॥
16.m: Released by them, she went quickly to the gods, trembling indeed, / and Saramā bowed down to Devendra, the best of the gods. // 16.21

16.s:
tasyāśca maruto devā devendreṇa nirūpitāḥ .
gūḍhaṃ gacchata rakṣārthaṃ devaśunyā mahābalāḥ .. 16.22 ..
16.d:
तस्याश्च मरुतो देवा देवेन्द्रेण निरूपिताः ।
गूढं गच्छत रक्षार्थं देवशुन्या महाबलाः ॥ 16.22 ॥
16.m: And the Marut gods had been instructed by Devendra: / 'Go secretly, O mighty ones, to guard the divine bitch!' // 16.22

16.s:
ityuktāstena sūkṣmeṇa vapuṣā jagmurañjasā .
te'pyāgamya surendrāya namaśrakrurdharādhare .. 16.23 ..
16.d:
इत्युक्तास्तेन सूक्ष्मेण वपुषा जग्मुरञ्जसा ।
तेऽप्यागम्य सुरेन्द्राय नमश्रक्रुर्धराधरे ॥ 16.23 ॥
16.m: Thus addressed by him, they went swiftly in subtle bodies. / Having arrived, they also bowed down to Surendra on the mountain. // 16.23

16.s:
tāṃ devarājaḥ papraccha kva gāvaḥ sarame'bhavan .
evamuktā tu saramā na jānāmīti cābravīt .. 16.24 ..
16.d:
तां देवराजः पप्रच्छ क्व गावः सरमेऽभवन् ।
एवमुक्ता तु सरमा न जानामीति चाब्रवीत् ॥ 16.24 ॥
16.m: The king of the gods asked her: 'Saramā, where are the cows?' / When asked this, Saramā said: 'I do not know.' // 16.24

16.s:
tata indro ruṣā yukto yajñārthamupakalpitāḥ .
gāvaḥ kva ceti marutaḥ provācedaṃ śunī katham .. 16.25 ..
16.d:
तत इन्द्रो रुषा युक्तो यज्ञार्थमुपकल्पिताः ।
गावः क्व चेति मरुतः प्रोवाचेदं शुनी कथम् ॥ 16.25 ॥
16.m: Then Indra was filled with anger and spoke to the Maruts: / 'Where are the cows prepared for the sacrifice? Why is the bitch [speaking like] this?' // 16.25

16.s:
evamuktāstu maruto devendreṇa dharādhare .
kathayāmāsuravyagrāḥ karmma tat saramākṛtam .. 16.26 ..
16.d:
एवमुक्तास्तु मरुतो देवेन्द्रेण धराधरे ।
कथयामासुरव्यग्राः कर्म्म तत् सरमाकृतम् ॥ 16.26 ॥
16.m: Thus questioned by Devendra on the mountain, the Maruts / calmly reported the deed done by Saramā. // 16.26

16.s:
tata indraḥ samutthāya padā saṃtāḍayacchunīm .
krodhena mahatāviṣṭo devendraḥ pākaśāsanaḥ .. 16.27 ..
16.d:
तत इन्द्रः समुत्थाय पदा संताडयच्छुनीम् ।
क्रोधेन महताविष्टो देवेन्द्रः पाकशासनः ॥ 16.27 ॥
16.m: Then Indra stood up and struck the bitch with his foot; / Devendra, the chastiser of Pāka, was seized by great fury. // 16.27

16.s:
kṣīraṃ pītaṃ tvayā mūḍhe gāvastāścāsurairhṛtāḥ .
evamuktvā padā tena tāḍitā saramā dhare .. 16.28 ..
16.d:
क्षीरं पीतं त्वया मूढे गावस्ताश्चासुरैर्हृताः ।
एवमुक्त्वा पदा तेन ताडिता सरमा धरे ॥ 16.28 ॥
16.m: 'Foolish one, you drank the milk, and the cows were carried off by the asuras!' / Speaking thus, he kicked Saramā with his foot, O Earth. // 16.28

16.s:
tasyendrapādaghātena kṣīraṃ vaktrāt prasustruve .
stravatā tena payasā sā śunī yatra gā bhavan .
jagāma tatra devendraḥ sahasainyastadā dhare .. 16.29 ..
16.d:
तस्येन्द्रपादघातेन क्षीरं वक्त्रात् प्रसुस्त्रुवे ।
स्त्रवता तेन पयसा सा शुनी यत्र गा भवन् ।
जगाम तत्र देवेन्द्रः सहसैन्यस्तदा धरे ॥ 16.29 ॥
16.m: From the blow of Indra's foot, milk flowed out of her mouth. / Devendra with his army then followed the dripping milk, O Earth, / to the place where the cows were. // 16.29

16.s:
gatvā cāpaśyad devendrastā gā daityairupāhṛtāḥ .
pālanāṃ cakrurye daityā balino bhṛśam .
te sainyairnihatāḥ sadyastatyajurgāḥ svamūrttibhiḥ .. 16.30 ..
16.d:
गत्वा चापश्यद् देवेन्द्रस्ता गा दैत्यैरुपाहृताः ।
पालनां चक्रुर्ये दैत्या बलिनो भृशम् ।
ते सैन्यैर्निहताः सद्यस्तत्यजुर्गाः स्वमूर्त्तिभिः ॥ 16.30 ॥
16.m: Having gone there, Devendra saw the cows taken by the Daityas. / The mighty Daityas who were guarding them / were slain at once by the armies, and abandoned the cows along with their own lives. // 16.30

16.s:
sāmantaiśca surendro'tha vṛtaḥ paramaharṣitaiḥ .
tāśca labdhvā mahendrastu mudā paramayā yutaḥ .. 16.31 ..
16.d:
सामन्तैश्च सुरेन्द्रोऽथ वृतः परमहर्षितैः ।
ताश्च लब्ध्वा महेन्द्रस्तु मुदा परमया युतः ॥ 16.31 ॥
16.m: Then Surendra, surrounded by exceedingly delighted vassals, / having recovered the cows, Mahendra was filled with great joy. // 16.31

16.s:
cakāra yajñān vividhān sahastrānapi sa prabhuḥ .
kriyamāṇaistato yajñairvavṛdhendrasya tad balam .. 16.32 ..
16.d:
चकार यज्ञान् विविधान् सहस्त्रानपि स प्रभुः ।
क्रियमाणैस्ततो यज्ञैर्ववृधेन्द्रस्य तद् बलम् ॥ 16.32 ॥
16.m: That lord performed diverse sacrifices, even by the thousands. / As the sacrifices were being performed, Indra's strength grew. // 16.32

16.s:
varddhitena balenendro devasainyamuvāca ha .
sannahyantāṃ surāḥ śīghraṃ daityānāṃ vadhakarmaṇi .. 16.33 ..
16.d:
वर्द्धितेन बलेनेन्द्रो देवसैन्यमुवाच ह ।
सन्नह्यन्तां सुराः शीघ्रं दैत्यानां वधकर्मणि ॥ 16.33 ॥
16.m: With his strength augmented, Indra said to the divine army: / 'Let the gods quickly arm themselves for the slaying of the Daityas!' // 16.33

16.s:
evamuktāstato devāḥ sannaddhāstatkṣaṇe'bhavan .
asurāṇāmabhāvāya jagmurdevāḥ savāsavāḥ .. 16.34 ..
16.d:
एवमुक्तास्ततो देवाः सन्नद्धास्तत्क्षणेऽभवन् ।
असुराणामभावाय जग्मुर्देवाः सवासवाः ॥ 16.34 ॥
16.m: Thus addressed, the gods armed themselves at that very moment. / Together with Indra, the gods marched for the destruction of the asuras. // 16.34

16.s:
gatvā tu yuyudhustūrṇaṃ vijigyustvāsurīṃ camūm .
jitāśca devairasurā hataśeṣā dharādhare .
mamajjuḥ sāgarajale bhayatrastā vicetasaḥ .. 16.35 ..
16.d:
गत्वा तु युयुधुस्तूर्णं विजिग्युस्त्वासुरीं चमूम् ।
जिताश्च देवैरसुरा हतशेषा धराधरे ।
ममज्जुः सागरजले भयत्रस्ता विचेतसः ॥ 16.35 ॥
16.m: Having gone, they fought swiftly and conquered the army of the asuras. / The asuras, defeated by the gods on the mountain and with few survivors, / plunged into the ocean's waters, terrified and bewildered. // 16.35

16.s:
devarājo'pi tridivaṃ lokapālaiḥ samaṃ dhare .
āruhya bubhuje prāgvat sa devo devarāṭ prabhuḥ .. 16.36 ..
16.d:
देवराजोऽपि त्रिदिवं लोकपालैः समं धरे ।
आरुह्य बुभुजे प्राग्वत् स देवो देवराट् प्रभुः ॥ 16.36 ॥
16.m: The king of the gods also ascended to heaven along with the world-guardians, O Earth; / that lord, the sovereign of the gods, ruled just as before. // 16.36

16.s:
ya enaṃ śrṛṇuyānnityaṃ saramākhyānamuttamam .
sa gomedhasya yajñasya phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ .. 16.37 ..
16.d:
य एनं श्रृणुयान्नित्यं सरमाख्यानमुत्तमम् ।
स गोमेधस्य यज्ञस्य फलं प्राप्नोति मानवः ॥ 16.37 ॥
16.m: Whoever constantly listens to this excellent story of Saramā / attains the fruit of a cow-sacrifice. // 16.37

16.s:
bhraṣṭarājyaśca yo rājā śrṛṇotīdaṃ samāhitaḥ .
sa devendra iva svargaṃ rājyaṃ svaṃ labhate naraḥ .. 16.38 ..
16.d:
भ्रष्टराज्यश्च यो राजा श्रृणोतीदं समाहितः ।
स देवेन्द्र इव स्वर्गं राज्यं स्वं लभते नरः ॥ 16.38 ॥
16.m: And whatever king who has lost his kingdom listens to this with a concentrated mind, / that man regains his own kingdom, just as Devendra regained heaven. // 16.38

16.s: .. iti śrīvarāhapurāṇe bhagavacchātre ṣoḍaśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 16 ..
16.d: ॥ इति श्रीवराहपुराणे भगवच्छात्रे षोडशोऽध्यायः ॥ 16 ॥
16.m: Thus ends the sixteenth chapter in the glorious Varāha Purāṇa, the treatise of the Lord. // 16

17.s:
dharaṇyuvāca .
ye te maṇau tadā deva utpannā narapuṃgavāḥ .
teṣāṃ varo bhagavatā dattastretāyuge kila .. 17.1 ..
17.d:
धरण्युवाच ।
ये ते मणौ तदा देव उत्पन्ना नरपुंगवाः ।
तेषां वरो भगवता दत्तस्त्रेतायुगे किल ॥ 17.1 ॥
17.m: Dharaṇī said: / 'O Lord, a boon was granted by the Blessed One in the Tretā Yuga / to those best of men who were born from the jewel: // 17.1

17.s:
rājāno bhavitāro vai kathaṃ teṣāṃ samudbhavaḥ .
kiṃ ca cakrurhi te karma pṛthaṅ nāmāni śaṃsa me .. 17.2 ..
17.d:
राजानो भवितारो वै कथं तेषां समुद्भवः ।
किं च चक्रुर्हि ते कर्म पृथङ् नामानि शंस मे ॥ 17.2 ॥
17.m: that they would become kings. How did their birth come about? / And what deeds did they do? Tell me their names individually.' // 17.2

17.s:
śrīvarāha uvāca .
suprabho maṇijo yastu rājā nāmnā mahāmanāḥ .
tasyotpattiṃ varārohe śrṛṇu tvaṃ bhūtadhāriṇi .. 17.3 ..
17.d:
श्रीवराह उवाच ।
सुप्रभो मणिजो यस्तु राजा नाम्ना महामनाः ।
तस्योत्पत्तिं वरारोहे श्रृणु त्वं भूतधारिणि ॥ 17.3 ॥
17.m: The glorious Varāha said: / 'He who was born from the jewel, the noble king named Suprabha— / listen to his origin, O fair-hipped one, O bearer of beings! // 17.3

17.s:
āsīd rājā mahābāhurādau kṛtayuge purā .
śrutakīrtiriti khyātastrailokye balavattaraḥ .. 17.4 ..
17.d:
आसीद् राजा महाबाहुरादौ कृतयुगे पुरा ।
श्रुतकीर्तिरिति ख्यातस्त्रैलोक्ये बलवत्तरः ॥ 17.4 ॥
17.m: Formerly, at the beginning of the Kṛta Yuga, there was a mighty-armed king / renowned as Śrutakīrti, exceedingly powerful in the three worlds. // 17.4

17.s:
tasya putratvamāpede suprabho maṇijo dhare .
prajāpāleti vai nāmnā śrutakīrtirmahābalaḥ .. 17.5 ..
17.d:
तस्य पुत्रत्वमापेदे सुप्रभो मणिजो धरे ।
प्रजापालेति वै नाम्ना श्रुतकीर्तिर्महाबलः ॥ 17.5 ॥
17.m: Suprabha, who was born from the jewel, became his son, O Earth, / under the name Prajāpāla, having the mighty Śrutakīrti [as father]. // 17.5

17.s:
saikasmiṃścid dine prāyād vipinaṃ śvāpadākum .
tatrāpaśyadṛṣerdhanyaṃ mahadāśramamaṇḍalam .. 17.6 ..
17.d:
सैकस्मिंश्चिद् दिने प्रायाद् विपिनं श्वापदाकुम् ।
तत्रापश्यदृषेर्धन्यं महदाश्रममण्डलम् ॥ 17.6 ॥
17.m: One day he went to a forest teeming with wild beasts. / There he saw the blessed and vast hermitage-precinct of a sage. // 17.6

17.s:
tasmin mahātapā nāma ṛṣiḥ paradhārmikaḥ .
tapastepe nirāhāro japan brahma sanātanam .. 17.7 ..
17.d:
तस्मिन् महातपा नाम ऋषिः परधार्मिकः ।
तपस्तेपे निराहारो जपन् ब्रह्म सनातनम् ॥ 17.7 ॥
17.m: In it, a most righteous sage named Mahātapas / was performing austerities without food, chanting the eternal sacred syllable. // 17.7

17.s:
tatrāsau pārthivaḥ śrīmān praveśāya matiṃ tadā .
cakāra cāviśad rājā prajāpālo mahātapāḥ .. 17.8 ..
17.d:
तत्रासौ पार्थिवः श्रीमान् प्रवेशाय मतिं तदा ।
चकार चाविशद् राजा प्रजापालो महातपाः ॥ 17.8 ॥
17.m: There that glorious king resolved to enter; / and King Prajāpāla, of great austerity, entered. // 17.8

17.s:
tasmin varāśramapade vanavṛkṣajātyā
dharāprasūtorjitamārgajuṣṭāḥ .
latāgṛhā induraviprakāśino
nāyāsitajñāḥ kulabhṛṅgarājāḥ .. 17.9 ..
17.d:
तस्मिन् वराश्रमपदे वनवृक्षजात्या
धराप्रसूतोर्जितमार्गजुष्टाः ।
लतागृहा इन्दुरविप्रकाशिनो
नायासितज्ञाः कुलभृङ्गराजाः ॥ 17.9 ॥
17.m: In that excellent hermitage ground, graced by paths made powerful by earth-born species of forest trees, / were bower-houses shining like the moon and sun, where swarms of royal bees were ignorant of weariness.

17.s:
suraktapadmodarakomalāgra-
nakhāṅgulībhiḥ prasṛtaiḥ surāṇām .
varāṅganābhiḥ padapaṅktimuccai-
viṃhāya bhūmiṃ tvapi vṛtraśatroḥ .. 17.10 ..
17.d:
सुरक्तपद्मोदरकोमलाग्र-
नखाङ्गुलीभिः प्रसृतैः सुराणाम् ।
वराङ्गनाभिः पदपङ्क्तिमुच्चै-
विंहाय भूमिं त्वपि वृत्रशत्रोः ॥ 17.10 ॥
17.m: [There was] a line of footprints left by the excellent celestial maidens of the enemy of Vṛtra, / reaching out with their soft fingertip-like nails resembling the interior of deep-red lotuses, rising high above the ground.

17.s:
kvacit samīpe tamatīva hṛṣṭai-
rnānādvijaiḥ ṣaṭcṛraṇaiśca mattaiḥ .
vāsadbhiruccairvividhapramāṇāḥ
śākhāḥ supuṣpāḥ samayogayuktāḥ .. 17.11 ..
17.d:
क्वचित् समीपे तमतीव हृष्टै-
र्नानाद्विजैः षट्चृरणैश्च मत्तैः ।
वासद्भिरुच्चैर्विविधप्रमाणाः
शाखाः सुपुष्पाः समयोगयुक्ताः ॥ 17.11 ॥
17.m: Somewhere nearby, branches of various sizes, rich in beautiful blossoms and well-arranged, / were inhabited by exceedingly delighted various birds and intoxicated six-footed bees calling aloud.

17.s:
kadambanīpārjjunaśīlaśāla-
latāgṛhasthairmadhurasvareṇa .
juṣṭaṃ vihaṅgaiḥ sujanaprayogā
nirākulā kāryadhṛtiryathāsthaiḥ .. 17.12 ..
17.d:
कदम्बनीपार्ज्जुनशीलशाल-
लतागृहस्थैर्मधुरस्वरेण ।
जुष्टं विहङ्गैः सुजनप्रयोगा
निराकुला कार्यधृतिर्यथास्थैः ॥ 17.12 ॥
17.m: It was frequented by birds singing with sweet voices, dwelling in bower-houses of kadamba, nīpa, arjuna, śīla, and śāla trees, / just as untroubled steadfastness in duty, employed by virtuous men, is cherished by those who are resolute.

17.s:
makhāgnidhūmairuditāgnihomai-
stataḥ samantāt gṛhamedhibhirdvijaiḥ .
siṃhairivādharmmakarī vidāritaḥ
sa tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭrairvaramattakesaraiḥ .. 17.13 ..
17.d:
मखाग्निधूमैरुदिताग्निहोमै-
स्ततः समन्तात् गृहमेधिभिर्द्विजैः ।
सिंहैरिवाधर्म्मकरी विदारितः
स तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रैर्वरमत्तकेसरैः ॥ 17.13 ॥
17.m: There, on all sides, the lion of irreligion had been torn apart / by the fire-sacrifices offered with the smoke of sacrificial fires by householder twice-born men, as if by sharp teeth and noble, fierce manes.

17.s:
evaṃ sa rājā vividhānupāyān
varāśrame prekṣamāṇo viveśa .
tasmid praviṣṭe tu sa tīvratejā
mahātapāḥ puṇyakṛtāṃ pradhānaḥ .
dṛṣṭo yathā bhānuranantabhānuḥ
kauśyāsane brahmavidāṃ pradhānaḥ .. 17.14 ..
17.d:
एवं स राजा विविधानुपायान्
वराश्रमे प्रेक्षमाणो विवेश ।
तस्मिद् प्रविष्टे तु स तीव्रतेजा
महातपाः पुण्यकृतां प्रधानः ।
दृष्टो यथा भानुरनन्तभानुः
कौश्यासने ब्रह्मविदां प्रधानः ॥ 17.14 ॥
17.m: Thus the king, gazing at the various means [of penance] in that excellent hermitage, entered. / When he had entered, the foremost among the doers of meritorious deeds, of blazing splendor, / Mahātapās, the foremost of knowers of Brahman, was seen on a kuśa grass seat like the sun of endless rays.

17.s:
dṛṣṭvā sa rājā vijayī mṛgāṇāṃ
matiṃ visasmāra muneḥ prasaṅgāt .
cakāra dharmaṃ prati mānasaṃ so
anuttamaṃ prāpya nṛpo muniṃ saḥ .. 17.15 ..
17.d:
दृष्ट्वा स राजा विजयी मृगाणां
मतिं विसस्मार मुनेः प्रसङ्गात् ।
चकार धर्मं प्रति मानसं सो
अनुत्तमं प्राप्य नृपो मुनिं सः ॥ 17.15 ॥
17.m: Having seen him, the victorious king forgot his intent to hunt deer through the association of the sage; / having reached that incomparable sage, the king directed his mind toward dharma.

17.s:
sa munistaṃ nṛpaṃ dṛṣṭvā prajāpālamakalmaṣam .
abhyāgatakriyāṃ cakre āsanasvāgatādibhiḥ .. 17.16 ..
17.d:
स मुनिस्तं नृपं दृष्ट्वा प्रजापालमकल्मषम् ।
अभ्यागतक्रियां चक्रे आसनस्वागतादिभिः ॥ 17.16 ॥
17.m: The sage, seeing that stainless king, the protector of the subjects, / performed the rites of hospitality for a guest with a seat, welcome, and other offerings.

17.s:
tataḥ kṛtāsano rājā praṇamya ṛṣipuṅgavam .
papraccha vasudhe praśnamimaṃ paramadurlabham .. 17.17 ..
17.d:
ततः कृतासनो राजा प्रणम्य ऋषिपुङ्गवम् ।
पप्रच्छ वसुधे प्रश्नमिमं परमदुर्लभम् ॥ 17.17 ॥
17.m: Then the king, having taken his seat and bowed to the bull among sages, / asked this most difficult question, O Vasudhā:

17.s:
bhagavan duḥkhasaṃsāramagnaiḥ pumbhistitīrṣubhiḥ .
yatkāryaṃ tanmamācakṣva praṇate śaṃsitavrata .. 17.18 ..
17.d:
भगवन् दुःखसंसारमग्नैः पुम्भिस्तितीर्षुभिः ।
यत्कार्यं तन्ममाचक्ष्व प्रणते शंसितव्रत ॥ 17.18 ॥
17.m: “O venerable one, tell me, who have bowed down, what ought to be done / by men drowned in the painful saṃsāra and desiring to cross over, O you of lauded vows!”

17.s:
mahātapā uvāca .
saṃsārārṇavamajjamānamanujaiḥ potaḥ sthiro'tidhruvaḥ
kāryaḥ pūjanadānahomavividhairyajñaiḥ samaṃ dhyāyanaiḥ .
kīlaiḥ kīlitamokṣabhiḥ surabhaṭairūrdhvaṃ mahārajjubhiḥ
prāṇādyairadhunā kuruṣva nṛpate potaṃ trilokeśvaram .. 17.19 ..
17.d:
महातपा उवाच ।
संसारार्णवमज्जमानमनुजैः पोतः स्थिरोऽतिध्रुवः
कार्यः पूजनदानहोमविविधैर्यज्ञैः समं ध्यायनैः ।
कीलैः कीलितमोक्षभिः सुरभटैरूर्ध्वं महारज्जुभिः
प्राणाद्यैरधुना कुरुष्व नृपते पोतं त्रिलोकेश्वरम् ॥ 17.19 ॥
