17.m: Mahātapās said: / “By mortals drowning in the ocean of saṃsāra, a firm and most steadfast boat must be built / through worship, gifts, oblations, and diverse sacrifices together with meditations. / Fastened with pegs of liberation, with celestial champions above, with great ropes of the prāṇas and the like— / now, O king, make the Lord of the Three Worlds your boat!

17.s:
nārāyaṇaṃ narakaharaṃ sureśaṃ
bhaktyā namaskurvati yo nṛpeśa .
sa vītaśokaḥ paramaṃ viśokaṃ
prāpnoti viṣṇoḥ padamavyayaṃ tat .. 17.20 ..
17.d:
नारायणं नरकहरं सुरेशं
भक्त्या नमस्कुर्वति यो नृपेश ।
स वीतशोकः परमं विशोकं
प्राप्नोति विष्णोः पदमव्ययं तत् ॥ 17.20 ॥
17.m: Whoever, O lord of kings, bows with devotion to Nārāyaṇa, / the destroyer of hell, the lord of gods, / free from sorrow, he attains that supreme, sorrowless, / imperishable abode of Viṣṇu.”

17.s:
nṛpa uvāca .
bhagavan sarvadharmajña kathaṃ viṣṇuḥ sanātanaḥ .
pūjyate mokṣamicchadbhiḥ puruṣairvada tattvataḥ .. 17.21 ..
17.d:
नृप उवाच ।
भगवन् सर्वधर्मज्ञ कथं विष्णुः सनातनः ।
पूज्यते मोक्षमिच्छद्भिः पुरुषैर्वद तत्त्वतः ॥ 17.21 ॥
17.m: The king said: / “O venerable one, knower of all dharma, tell me in truth: / how is the eternal Viṣṇu worshipped by men desiring liberation?”

17.s:
mahātapā uvāca .
śrṛṇu rājan mahāprājña yathā viṣṇuḥ prasīdati .
puruṣāṇāṃ tathā strīṇāṃ sarvayogīśvaro hariḥ .. 17.22 ..
17.d:
महातपा उवाच ।
श्रृणु राजन् महाप्राज्ञ यथा विष्णुः प्रसीदति ।
पुरुषाणां तथा स्त्रीणां सर्वयोगीश्वरो हरिः ॥ 17.22 ॥
17.m: Mahātapās said: / “Hear, O king of great wisdom, how Viṣṇu, / Hari, the lord of all yogins, is pleased by men and likewise by women.

17.s:
sarve devāḥ sapitaro brahmādyāścāṇḍamadhyagāḥ .
viṣṇoḥ sakāśādutpannā itīyaṃ vaidikī śrutiḥ .. 17.23 ..
17.d:
सर्वे देवाः सपितरो ब्रह्माद्याश्चाण्डमध्यगाः ।
विष्णोः सकाशादुत्पन्ना इतीयं वैदिकी श्रुतिः ॥ 17.23 ॥
17.m: All the gods, together with the ancestors, Brahmā and the rest who dwell within the cosmic egg, / arose from the presence of Viṣṇu; such is this Vedic revelation.

17.s:
agnistathāśvinau gaurī gajavaktrabhujaṃgamāḥ .
kārtikeyastathādityo mātaro durgayā saha .. 17.24 ..
17.d:
अग्निस्तथाश्विनौ गौरी गजवक्त्रभुजंगमाः ।
कार्तिकेयस्तथादित्यो मातरो दुर्गया सह ॥ 17.24 ॥
17.m: Agni, the two Aśvins, Gaurī, the Elephant-faced One, the serpents, / Kārttikeya, the sun, the Mothers together with Durgā,

17.s:
diśo dhanapatirviṣṇuryamo rudraḥ śaśī tathā .
pitaraśceti saṃbhūtāḥ prādhānyena jagatpateḥ .. 17.25 ..
17.d:
दिशो धनपतिर्विष्णुर्यमो रुद्रः शशी तथा ।
पितरश्चेति संभूताः प्राधान्येन जगत्पतेः ॥ 17.25 ॥
17.m: the directions, the Lord of Wealth, Viṣṇu, Yama, Rudra, and the moon, / and the ancestors were born principally from the Lord of the World.

17.s:
hiraṇyagarbhasya tanau sarvaṃ eva samudbhavāḥ .
pṛthakpṛthak tato garvaṃ vahamānāḥ samantataḥ .. 17.26 ..
17.d:
हिरण्यगर्भस्य तनौ सर्वं एव समुद्भवाः ।
पृथक्पृथक् ततो गर्वं वहमानाः समन्ततः ॥ 17.26 ॥
17.m: All indeed arose within the body of Hiraṇyagarbha; / then, bearing pride individually on all sides,

17.s:
ahaṃ yogyastvahaṃ yājya iti teṣāṃ svano mahān .
śrūyate devasamitau sāgarakṣubdhasannibhaḥ .. 17.27 ..
17.d:
अहं योग्यस्त्वहं याज्य इति तेषां स्वनो महान् ।
श्रूयते देवसमितौ सागरक्षुब्धसन्निभः ॥ 17.27 ॥
17.m: a great roar of theirs, like an agitated ocean, was heard in the assembly of the gods: / ‘I am worthy! I am the one to be sacrificed to!’

17.s:
teṣāṃ vivadamānānāṃ vahnirutthāya pārthiva .
uvāca māṃ yajasveti dhyāyadhvaṃ māmiti bruvan .. 17.28 ..
17.d:
तेषां विवदमानानां वह्निरुत्थाय पार्थिव ।
उवाच मां यजस्वेति ध्यायध्वं मामिति ब्रुवन् ॥ 17.28 ॥
17.m: While they were disputing thus, O king, Fire arose / and said, ‘Sacrifice to me! Meditate upon me!’

17.s:
prājāpatyamidaṃ nūnaṃ śarīraṃ madvinākṛtam .
vināśamupapadyeta yato nāhaṃ mahānaham .. 17.29 ..
17.d:
प्राजापत्यमिदं नूनं शरीरं मद्विनाकृतम् ।
विनाशमुपपद्येत यतो नाहं महानहम् ॥ 17.29 ॥
17.m: ‘Surely this body of Prajāpati, bereft of me, / would meet with destruction, for is there anyone greater than I?’

17.s:
evamuktvā śarīraṃ tu tyaktvā vahnirviniryayau .
nirgate'pi tatastasmiṃstaccharīraṃ na śīryate .. 17.30 ..
17.d:
एवमुक्त्वा शरीरं तु त्यक्त्वा वह्निर्विनिर्ययौ ।
निर्गतेऽपि ततस्तस्मिंस्तच्छरीरं न शीर्यते ॥ 17.30 ॥
17.m: Having spoken thus, Fire left the body and departed; / even when he had departed from it, that body did not perish.

17.s:
tato'śvinau mūrtimantau prāṇāpānau śarīragau .
āvāṃ pradhānāvityevamūcaturyājyasattamau .. 17.31 ..
17.d:
ततोऽश्विनौ मूर्तिमन्तौ प्राणापानौ शरीरगौ ।
आवां प्रधानावित्येवमूचतुर्याज्यसत्तमौ ॥ 17.31 ॥
17.m: Then the embodied Aśvins, who are the prāṇa and apāna breaths within the body, / said: ‘We two are preeminent, the best of those to be worshipped!’

17.s:
evamuktvā śarīraṃ tu vihāya kvacidāsthitau .
tayorapi kṣayaṃ kṛtvā kṣetrī tatpuramāsthitaḥ .. 17.32 ..
17.d:
एवमुक्त्वा शरीरं तु विहाय क्वचिदास्थितौ ।
तयोरपि क्षयं कृत्वा क्षेत्री तत्पुरमास्थितः ॥ 17.32 ॥
17.m: Having spoken thus, they left the body and stayed elsewhere; / even having endured the loss of them both, the knower of the field remained in that city [of the body].

17.s:
tato vāgabrabīd gaurī prādhānyaṃ mayi saṃsthitam .
sā'pyevamuktvā kṣetrāt tu niścakrāma bahiḥ śubhā .. 17.33 ..
17.d:
ततो वागब्रबीद् गौरी प्राधान्यं मयि संस्थितम् ।
साऽप्येवमुक्त्वा क्षेत्रात् तु निश्चक्राम बहिः शुभा ॥ 17.33 ॥
17.m: Then Gaurī, who is speech, said: ‘Preeminence resides in me.’ / Having said this, that auspicious one also departed outside of the field.

17.s:
tayā vināpi tatkṣetraṃ vāgūnaṃ vyavatiṣṭhata .
tato gaṇapatirvākyamākāśākhyo'bravīt tadā .. 17.34 ..
17.d:
तया विनापि तत्क्षेत्रं वागूनं व्यवतिष्ठत ।
ततो गणपतिर्वाक्यमाकाशाख्योऽब्रवीत् तदा ॥ 17.34 ॥
17.m: Even without her, that field remained, though lacking speech. / Then Gaṇapati, who is called space, uttered these words:

17.s:
na mayā rahitaṃ kiñciccharīraṃ sthāyi dūrataḥ .
kālāntaretyevamuktvā so'pi niṣkramya dehataḥ .. 17.35 ..
17.d:
न मया रहितं किञ्चिच्छरीरं स्थायि दूरतः ।
कालान्तरेत्येवमुक्त्वा सोऽपि निष्क्रम्य देहतः ॥ 17.35 ॥
17.m: ‘No body lasts long without me in the course of time!’ / Having said this, he too departed from the body.

17.s:
pṛthagbhūtastathāpyetaccharīraṃ nāpyanīnaśat .
vinākāśākhyatattvena tathāpi na viśīryate .. 17.36 ..
17.d:
पृथग्भूतस्तथाप्येतच्छरीरं नाप्यनीनशत् ।
विनाकाशाख्यतत्त्वेन तथापि न विशीर्यते ॥ 17.36 ॥
17.m: Though he stood apart, this body did not perish; / even without the element called space, it did not disintegrate.

17.s:
suṣiraistu vihīnaṃ tu dṛṣṭvā kṣetraṃ vyavasthitam .
śarīradhātavaḥ sarve te brūyurvākyameva hi .. 17.37 ..
17.d:
सुषिरैस्तु विहीनं तु दृष्ट्वा क्षेत्रं व्यवस्थितम् ।
शरीरधातवः सर्वे ते ब्रूयुर्वाक्यमेव हि ॥ 17.37 ॥
17.m: Seeing the field remaining even when devoid of apertures, / all the bodily elements truly spoke these words:

17.s:
asmābhirvyatiriktasya na śarīrasya dhāraṇam .
bhavatītyevamuktvā te jahuḥ sarve śarīriṇaḥ .. 17.38 ..
17.d:
अस्माभिर्व्यतिरिक्तस्य न शरीरस्य धारणम् ।
भवतीत्येवमुक्त्वा ते जहुः सर्वे शरीरिणः ॥ 17.38 ॥
17.m: ‘Without us, no sustaining of the body / is possible!’ Having spoken thus, all those embodied ones departed.

17.s:
tairvyapetamapi kṣetraṃ puruṣeṇa prapālyate .
taṃ dṛṣṭvā tvabravīt skandaḥ so'haṃkāraḥ prakīrtitaḥ .. 17.39 ..
17.d:
तैर्व्यपेतमपि क्षेत्रं पुरुषेण प्रपाल्यते ।
तं दृष्ट्वा त्वब्रवीत् स्कन्दः सोऽहंकारः प्रकीर्तितः ॥ 17.39 ॥
17.m: Even when abandoned by them, the field was protected by the Puruṣa. / Seeing that, Skanda, who is declared to be egoity, spoke:

17.s:
mayā vinā śarīrasya saṃbhūtirapi neṣyate .
evamuktvā śarīrāt tu so'bhyapetaḥ pṛthak sthitaḥ .. 17.40 ..
17.d:
मया विना शरीरस्य संभूतिरपि नेष्यते ।
एवमुक्त्वा शरीरात् तु सोऽभ्यपेतः पृथक् स्थितः ॥ 17.40 ॥
17.m: ‘Without me, even the existence of the body is not accepted.’ / Having spoken thus, he departed from the body and stood apart.

17.s:
tenākṣatena tatkṣetraṃ vinā muktavadāsthitam .
taṃ dṛṣṭvā kupito bhānuḥ sa ādityaḥ prakīrtitaḥ .. 17.41 ..
17.d:
तेनाक्षतेन तत्क्षेत्रं विना मुक्तवदास्थितम् ।
तं दृष्ट्वा कुपितो भानुः स आदित्यः प्रकीर्तितः ॥ 17.41 ॥
17.m: Without him, uninjured, that field remained like one liberated. / Seeing that, the sun, who is declared to be Āditya, was angered:

17.s:
mayā vinā kathaṃ kṣetramimaṃ kṣaṇamapīṣyate .
evamuktvā prayātaḥ sa taccharīraṃ na śīryate .. 17.42 ..
17.d:
मया विना कथं क्षेत्रमिमं क्षणमपीष्यते ।
एवमुक्त्वा प्रयातः स तच्छरीरं न शीर्यते ॥ 17.42 ॥
17.m: ‘Without me, how can this field be maintained even for a moment?’ / Having spoken thus, he went away, yet that body did not disintegrate.

17.s:
tataḥ kāmādirutthāya gaṇo mātṛvisaṃjñitaḥ .
na mayā vyatiriktasya śarīrasya vyavasthitiḥ .
evamuktvā sa yātastu śarīraṃ tanna śīryate .. 17.43 ..
17.d:
ततः कामादिरुत्थाय गणो मातृविसंज्ञितः ।
न मया व्यतिरिक्तस्य शरीरस्य व्यवस्थितिः ।
एवमुक्त्वा स यातस्तु शरीरं तन्न शीर्यते ॥ 17.43 ॥
17.m: Then desire and the rest arose, the host known as the Mothers: / ‘Without me, there is no stability of the body.’ / Having spoken thus, it departed, yet that body did not disintegrate.

17.s:
tato māyā'bravītkopāt sā ca durgā prakīrtitā .
na mayā'sya vinā bhūtirityuktvā'ntardadhe punaḥ .. 17.44 ..
17.d:
ततो मायाऽब्रवीत्कोपात् सा च दुर्गा प्रकीर्तिता ।
न मयाऽस्य विना भूतिरित्युक्त्वाऽन्तर्दधे पुनः ॥ 17.44 ॥
17.m: Then Māyā, who is declared to be Durgā, said in anger: / ‘Without me, it has no existence!’ Having spoken thus, she vanished.

17.s:
tato diśaḥ samuttasthurūcuścedaṃ vaco mahat .
nāsmābhī rahitaṃ kāryaṃ bhavatīti na saṃśayaḥ .
catasra āgatāḥ kāṣṭhā apayātāḥ kṣaṇāt tadā .. 17.45 ..
17.d:
ततो दिशः समुत्तस्थुरूचुश्चेदं वचो महत् ।
नास्माभी रहितं कार्यं भवतीति न संशयः ।
चतस्र आगताः काष्ठा अपयाताः क्षणात् तदा ॥ 17.45 ॥
17.m: Then the directions arose and spoke these great words: / ‘Without us, no action can occur; of this there is no doubt.’ / The four quarters that had gathered then departed in an instant.

17.s:
tato dhanapatirvāyurmayyapete kva saṃbhavaḥ .
śarīrasyeti sopyevamuktvā mūrdhānago'bhavat .. 17.46 ..
17.d:
ततो धनपतिर्वायुर्मय्यपेते क्व संभवः ।
शरीरस्येति सोप्येवमुक्त्वा मूर्धानगोऽभवत् ॥ 17.46 ॥
17.m: Then the lord of wealth [and] the wind [said], "When I depart, where can the body / continue to exist?" Having spoken thus, he went into the head.

17.s:
tato viṣṇurmano brūyānnāyaṃ deho mayā vinā .
kṣaṇamapyutsahet sthātumityuktvā'ntardadhe punaḥ .. 17.47 ..
17.d:
ततो विष्णुर्मनो ब्रूयान्नायं देहो मया विना ।
क्षणमप्युत्सहेत् स्थातुमित्युक्त्वाऽन्तर्दधे पुनः ॥ 17.47 ॥
17.m: Then Viṣṇu, the mind, said, "Without me, this body / could not endure to stand even for an instant." Having spoken thus, he disappeared again.

17.s:
tato dharmo'bravīt sarvamidaṃ pālitavānaham .
idānīmapyupagate kathametadbhaviṣyati .. 17.48 ..
17.d:
ततो धर्मोऽब्रवीत् सर्वमिदं पालितवानहम् ।
इदानीमप्युपगते कथमेतद्भविष्यति ॥ 17.48 ॥
17.m: Then Dharma said, "I have protected all of this. / Now that I too have departed, how will this continue?"

17.s:
evamuktvā gato dharmastaccharīraṃ na śīryate .
tatobravīnmahādevaḥ avyakto bhūtanāyakaḥ .. 17.49 ..
17.d:
एवमुक्त्वा गतो धर्मस्तच्छरीरं न शीर्यते ।
ततोब्रवीन्महादेवः अव्यक्तो भूतनायकः ॥ 17.49 ॥
17.m: Having spoken thus, Dharma departed, [yet] that body did not perish. / Then Mahādeva, the unmanifest lord of beings, spoke:

17.s:
mahatsaṃjño mayā hīnaṃ śarīraṃ no bhaved yathā .
evamuktvā gataḥ śambhustaccharīraṃ na śīryate .. 17.50 ..
17.d:
महत्संज्ञो मया हीनं शरीरं नो भवेद् यथा ।
एवमुक्त्वा गतः शम्भुस्तच्छरीरं न शीर्यते ॥ 17.50 ॥
17.m: "He who is named the Great (Mahat) [said], 'Without me, the body would not exist.'" / Having spoken thus, Śambhu departed, [yet] that body did not perish.

17.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā pitaraścocustanmātrā yāvadasmabhiḥ .
pragatairebhiretacca śarīraṃ śīryate dhruvam .
evamuktvā tu te dehaṃ tyaktvā'ntarddhānamāgatāḥ .. 17.51 ..
17.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा पितरश्चोचुस्तन्मात्रा यावदस्मभिः ।
प्रगतैरेभिरेतच्च शरीरं शीर्यते ध्रुवम् ।
एवमुक्त्वा तु ते देहं त्यक्त्वाऽन्तर्द्धानमागताः ॥ 17.51 ॥
17.m: Seeing him, the ancestors and the subtle elements said, "Since we / have departed, along with these [others], surely this body will perish." / Having spoken thus, they abandoned the body and vanished.

17.s:
agniḥ prāṇo apānaśca ākāśaṃ sarvadhātavaḥ .
kṣetraṃ tadvadahaṃkāro bhānuḥ kāmādayo mayā .
kāṣṭhā vāyurviṣṇurdharma śambhustathendriyārthakāḥ .. 17.52 ..
17.d:
अग्निः प्राणो अपानश्च आकाशं सर्वधातवः ।
क्षेत्रं तद्वदहंकारो भानुः कामादयो मया ।
काष्ठा वायुर्विष्णुर्धर्म शम्भुस्तथेन्द्रियार्थकाः ॥ 17.52 ॥
17.m: Fire, prāṇa and apāna, space, all the bodily humors, / the field, likewise the ego, the sun, desire and the rest through creative illusion, / the directions, the wind, Viṣṇu, Dharma, Śambhu, and likewise the objects of the senses—

17.s:
etairmuktaṃ tu tatkṣetraṃ tat tathaiva vyavasthitam .
somena pālyamānaṃ tu puruṣeṇendurūpiṇā .. 17.53 ..
17.d:
एतैर्मुक्तं तु तत्क्षेत्रं तत् तथैव व्यवस्थितम् ।
सोमेन पाल्यमानं तु पुरुषेणेन्दुरूपिणा ॥ 17.53 ॥
17.m: abandoned by these, that field nevertheless remained just as it was, / protected by Soma, the Person in the form of the moon.

17.s:
evaṃ vyavasthite some ṣoḍaśātmanyathākṣare .
prāgvat tatra guṇopetaṃ kṣetramutthāya babhrama .. 17.54 ..
17.d:
एवं व्यवस्थिते सोमे षोडशात्मन्यथाक्षरे ।
प्राग्वत् तत्र गुणोपेतं क्षेत्रमुत्थाय बभ्रम ॥ 17.54 ॥
17.m: When Soma, the sixteenfold and imperishable, remained thus, / the field, endowed with its qualities as before, rose up and moved about.

17.s:
prāgavasthaṃ śarīraṃ tu dṛṣṭvā sarvajñapālitam .
tāḥ kṣetradevatāḥ sarvā vailakṣaṃ bhāvamāśritāḥ .. 17.55 ..
17.d:
प्रागवस्थं शरीरं तु दृष्ट्वा सर्वज्ञपालितम् ।
ताः क्षेत्रदेवताः सर्वा वैलक्षं भावमाश्रिताः ॥ 17.55 ॥
17.m: Seeing the body restored to its former state, protected by the Omniscient One, / all those deities of the field became confounded.

17.s:
tamevaṃ tuṣṭuvuḥ sarvāstaṃ devaṃ parameśvaram .
svasthānamīyiṣuḥ sarvāstadā nṛpatisattama .. 17.56 ..
17.d:
तमेवं तुष्टुवुः सर्वास्तं देवं परमेश्वरम् ।
स्वस्थानमीयिषुः सर्वास्तदा नृपतिसत्तम ॥ 17.56 ॥
17.m: They all praised that god, the supreme lord, in this manner, / wishing to go to their own stations, O best of kings:

17.s:
tvamagnistvaṃ tathā prāṇastvamapānaḥ sarasvatī .
tvamākāśaṃ dhanādhyakṣastvaṃ śarīrasya dhātavaḥ .. 17.57 ..
17.d:
त्वमग्निस्त्वं तथा प्राणस्त्वमपानः सरस्वती ।
त्वमाकाशं धनाध्यक्षस्त्वं शरीरस्य धातवः ॥ 17.57 ॥
17.m: "You are fire, you are prāṇa, you are apāna and Sarasvatī; / you are space, the guardian of wealth; you are the bodily humors of the body.

17.s:
ahaṃkāro bhavān deva tvamādityo'ṣṭako gaṇaḥ .
tvaṃ māyā pṛthivī durgā tvaṃ diśastvaṃ marutpatiḥ .. 17.58 ..
17.d:
अहंकारो भवान् देव त्वमादित्योऽष्टको गणः ।
त्वं माया पृथिवी दुर्गा त्वं दिशस्त्वं मरुत्पतिः ॥ 17.58 ॥
17.m: You are the ego, O Lord; you are the sun and the group of eight; / you are creative illusion, the Earth, Durgā; you are the directions; you are the lord of the wind.

17.s:
tvaṃ viṣṇustvaṃ tathā dharmastvaṃ jiṣṇustvaṃ parājitaḥ .
akṣarārthasvarūpeṇa parameśvarasaṃjñitaḥ .. 17.59 ..
17.d:
त्वं विष्णुस्त्वं तथा धर्मस्त्वं जिष्णुस्त्वं पराजितः ।
अक्षरार्थस्वरूपेण परमेश्वरसंज्ञितः ॥ 17.59 ॥
17.m: You are Viṣṇu, and likewise Dharma; you are the victorious and the unvanquished; / embodied in the reality of the imperishable syllable, you are designated the supreme lord.

17.s:
asmābhirapayātaistu kathametadbhaviṣyati .
evamatra śarīraṃ tu tyaktamasmābhireva ca .. 17.60 ..
17.d:
अस्माभिरपयातैस्तु कथमेतद्भविष्यति ।
एवमत्र शरीरं तु त्यक्तमस्माभिरेव च ॥ 17.60 ॥
17.m: When we have departed, how could this be? / Thus was the body abandoned by us here.

17.s:
tat paraṃ bhavatā deva tadavasthaṃ prapālyate .
sthānabhaṅgo na naḥ kāryaḥ svayaṃ sṛṣṭvā prajāpate .. 17.61 ..
17.d:
तत् परं भवता देव तदवस्थं प्रपाल्यते ।
स्थानभङ्गो न नः कार्यः स्वयं सृष्ट्वा प्रजापते ॥ 17.61 ॥
17.m: Yet it is fully sustained in that state by You, O God! / You should not bring about the ruin of our stations, having created them Yourself, O creator of beings!"

17.s:
evaṃ stutastato devasteṣāṃ toṣaṃ paraṃ yayau .
uvāca caitān krīḍārthaṃ bhavantotpāditā mayā .. 17.62 ..
17.d:
एवं स्तुतस्ततो देवस्तेषां तोषं परं ययौ ।
उवाच चैतान् क्रीडार्थं भवन्तोत्पादिता मया ॥ 17.62 ॥
17.m: Praised in this way, the god then experienced supreme satisfaction, / and said to them, "You were created by Me for sport.

17.s:
kṛtakṛtyasya me kiṃ nu bhavadbhirviprayojanam .
tathāpi dadmi vo rūpe dve dve pratyekaśo'dhunā .. 17.63 ..
17.d:
कृतकृत्यस्य मे किं नु भवद्भिर्विप्रयोजनम् ।
तथापि दद्मि वो रूपे द्वे द्वे प्रत्येकशोऽधुना ॥ 17.63 ॥
17.m: What need have I of you, since My purpose is accomplished? / Even so, I now grant to each of you two forms:

17.s:
bhūtakāryeṣvamūrtena devaloke tu mūrtinā .
tiṣṭhadhvamapi kālānte layaṃ tvāviśata drutam .. 17.64 ..
17.d:
भूतकार्येष्वमूर्तेन देवलोके तु मूर्तिना ।
तिष्ठध्वमपि कालान्ते लयं त्वाविशत द्रुतम् ॥ 17.64 ॥
17.m: in the activities of elemental beings [remain] formless, but in the realm of the gods, with form; / dwell there, and at the end of time quickly enter dissolution.

17.s:
śarīrāṇi punarnaivaṃ karttavyo'hamiti kvacit .
mūrttīnāṃ ca tathā tubhyaṃ dadmi nāmāni vo'dhunā .. 17.65 ..
17.d:
शरीराणि पुनर्नैवं कर्त्तव्योऽहमिति क्वचित् ।
मूर्त्तीनां च तथा तुभ्यं दद्मि नामानि वोऽधुना ॥ 17.65 ॥
17.m: Never again should [any of you think], 'I am to fashion bodies.' / And I now give you names for your forms.

17.s:
agnervaiśvānaro nāma prāṇāpānau tathāśvinau .
bhaviṣyati tathā gaurī himaśailasutā tathā .. 17.66 ..
17.d:
अग्नेर्वैश्वानरो नाम प्राणापानौ तथाश्विनौ ।
भविष्यति तथा गौरी हिमशैलसुता तथा ॥ 17.66 ॥
17.m: The name of Fire shall be Vaiśvānara; prāṇa and apāna shall be the Aśvins; / likewise there shall be Gaurī, daughter of the snow-mountain.

17.s:
pṛthivyādigaṇastveṣa gajavaktro bhaviṣyati .
śarīradhātavaśceme nānābhūtāni eva tu .
ahaṃkārastathā skandaḥ kārttikeyo bhaviṣyati .. 17.67 ..
17.d:
पृथिव्यादिगणस्त्वेष गजवक्त्रो भविष्यति ।
शरीरधातवश्चेमे नानाभूतानि एव तु ।
अहंकारस्तथा स्कन्दः कार्त्तिकेयो भविष्यति ॥ 17.67 ॥
17.m: This group beginning with the earth shall become the elephant-faced one (Gajavaktra); / and these bodily humors shall indeed become various spirits; / likewise the ego shall become Skanda Kārttikeya.

17.s:
bhānuścādityarūpo'sau mūrttāmūrtta ca cakṣuṣī .
kāmādyo'yaṃ gaṇo bhūyo mātṛrūpo bhaviṣyati .. 17.68 ..
17.d:
भानुश्चादित्यरूपोऽसौ मूर्त्तामूर्त्त च चक्षुषी ।
कामाद्योऽयं गणो भूयो मातृरूपो भविष्यति ॥ 17.68 ॥
17.m: And the sun shall take the form of Āditya, with form and formless, the two eyes; / this group beginning with desire shall further take the form of the Mothers.

17.s:
śarīramāyā durgaiṣā kāraṇānte bhaviṣyati .
daśa kanyā bhaviṣyanti kāṣṭhāstvetāstu vāruṇāḥ .. 17.69 ..
17.d:
शरीरमाया दुर्गैषा कारणान्ते भविष्यति ।
दश कन्या भविष्यन्ति काष्ठास्त्वेतास्तु वारुणाः ॥ 17.69 ॥
17.m: This creative illusion of the body shall become Durgā at the end of the cause; / these directions shall become ten maidens, belonging to Varuṇa.

17.s:
ayaṃ vāyurdhaneśastu kāraṇānte bhaviṣyati .
ayaṃ mano viṣṇunāmā bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ .. 17.70 ..
17.d:
अयं वायुर्धनेशस्तु कारणान्ते भविष्यति ।
अयं मनो विष्णुनामा भविष्यति न संशयः ॥ 17.70 ॥
17.m: This wind shall become the lord of wealth at the end of the cause; / this mind shall without doubt bear the name Viṣṇu.

17.s:
dharmo'pi yamanāmā ca bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ .
mahattattvaṃ ca bhagavān mahādevo bhaviṣyati .. 17.71 ..
17.d:
धर्मोऽपि यमनामा च भविष्यति न संशयः ।
महत्तत्त्वं च भगवान् महादेवो भविष्यति ॥ 17.71 ॥
17.m: Dharma too shall without doubt bear the name Yama; / and the Great Principle (Mahattattva) shall become the Lord Mahādeva.

17.s:
indriyārthāśca pitaro bhaviṣyanti na saṃśayaḥ .
ayaṃ somaḥ svayaṃ bhūtvā yāmitraṃ sarvadāmarāḥ .. 17.72 ..
17.d:
इन्द्रियार्थाश्च पितरो भविष्यन्ति न संशयः ।
अयं सोमः स्वयं भूत्वा यामित्रं सर्वदामराः ॥ 17.72 ॥
17.m: And the sense-objects shall without doubt become the ancestors; / this Soma, becoming himself, [shall be] an ally, always, O immortals."

17.s:
evaṃ vedāntapuruṣaḥ prokto nārāyaṇātmakaḥ .
svasthāne devatāḥ sarvā devastu virarāma ha .. 17.73 ..
17.d:
एवं वेदान्तपुरुषः प्रोक्तो नारायणात्मकः ।
स्वस्थाने देवताः सर्वा देवस्तु विरराम ह ॥ 17.73 ॥
17.m: Thus the Person of the Vedānta, whose essence is Nārāyaṇa, spoke; / all the deities [went] to their own places, and the god fell silent.

17.s:
evaṃ prabhāvo devo'sau vedavedyo janārdanaḥ .
kathito nṛpate tubhyaṃ kimanyacchrotumicchasi .. 17.74 ..
17.d:
एवं प्रभावो देवोऽसौ वेदवेद्यो जनार्दनः ।
कथितो नृपते तुभ्यं किमन्यच्छ्रोतुमिच्छसि ॥ 17.74 ॥
17.m: Such is the majesty of this god Janārdana, who is known through the Vedas. / It has been told to you, O king; what else do you wish to hear?

17.s: .. iti śrīvarāhapurāṇe bhagavacchāstre saptadaśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 17 ..
17.d: ॥ इति श्रीवराहपुराणे भगवच्छास्त्रे सप्तदशोऽध्यायः ॥ 17 ॥
17.m: Thus ends the seventeenth chapter in the sacred Varāhapurāṇa, the scripture of the Lord.

18.s:
prajāpāla uvāca .
kathamagneḥ samutpattiraśvinorvā mahāmune .
gauryā gaṇapatervā'pi nāgānāṃ vā guhasya ca .. 18.1 ..
18.d:
प्रजापाल उवाच ।
कथमग्नेः समुत्पत्तिरश्विनोर्वा महामुने ।
गौर्या गणपतेर्वाऽपि नागानां वा गुहस्य च ॥ 18.1 ॥
18.m: Prajāpāla said: / How did the origin of fire or of the Aśvins occur, O great sage, / or of Gaurī, Gaṇapati, the snakes, or Guha?

18.s:
ādityacandramātṝṇāṃ durgāyā vā diśāṃ tathā .
dhanadasya ca viṣṇorvā dharmasya parameṣṭhinaḥ .. 18.2 ..
18.d:
आदित्यचन्द्रमातॄणां दुर्गाया वा दिशां तथा ।
धनदस्य च विष्णोर्वा धर्मस्य परमेष्ठिनः ॥ 18.2 ॥
18.m: Of the Sun, the Moon, the Mothers, or Durgā, and likewise of the directions, / and of the bestower of wealth, or Viṣṇu, of Dharma, of the supreme lord,

18.s:
śambhorvāpi pitṝṇāṃ ca tathā candramaso mune .
śarīradevatā hyetāḥ kathaṃ mūrttitvamāgatāḥ .. 18.3 ..
18.d:
शम्भोर्वापि पितॄणां च तथा चन्द्रमसो मुने ।
शरीरदेवता ह्येताः कथं मूर्त्तित्वमागताः ॥ 18.3 ॥
18.m: or of Śambhu, and of the ancestors, and likewise of the moon, O sage? / For how did these deities of the body attain embodied form?

18.s:
kiṃ ca tāsāṃ mune bhojyaṃ kā vā saṃjñā tithiśca kā .
yasyāṃ yaṣṭāstvamī puṃsāṃ phalaṃ yacchantyanāmayam .
etanme sarahasyaṃ tu mune tvaṃ vaktumarhasi .. 18.4 ..
18.d:
किं च तासां मुने भोज्यं का वा संज्ञा तिथिश्च का ।
यस्यां यष्टास्त्वमी पुंसां फलं यच्छन्त्यनामयम् ।
एतन्मे सरहस्यं तु मुने त्वं वक्तुमर्हसि ॥ 18.4 ॥
18.m: And what is their food offering, O sage, what is their designation, and what is their lunar day (tithi), / on which, when worshipped, they bestow flawless fruit upon men? / You ought to tell me this secret, O sage!

18.s:
mahātapā uvāca .
yogasādhyaḥ svarūpeṇa ātmā nārāyaṇātmakaḥ .
sarvajñaḥ krīḍatastasya bhogecchā cātmanātmani .
kṣobhite'bhūnmahābhūte etacchabdaṃ tadadbhutam .. 18.5 ..
18.d:
महातपा उवाच ।
योगसाध्यः स्वरूपेण आत्मा नारायणात्मकः ।
सर्वज्ञः क्रीडतस्तस्य भोगेच्छा चात्मनात्मनि ।
क्षोभितेऽभून्महाभूते एतच्छब्दं तदद्भुतम् ॥ 18.5 ॥
18.m: Mahātapās said: / The Self, whose nature is Nārāyaṇa, is attainable through yoga in his true form. / As the omniscient one was sporting, a desire for experience arose within Himself through Himself. / When the great element was agitated, that wondrous sound arose.

18.s:
tamapyaprītimattoyaṃ vikāraṃ samarocayat .
vikurvatastasya tadā mahānagniḥ samutthitaḥ .
koṭijvālāparīvāraḥ śabdavān dahanātmakaḥ .. 18.6 ..
18.d:
तमप्यप्रीतिमत्तोयं विकारं समरोचयत् ।
विकुर्वतस्तस्य तदा महानग्निः समुत्थितः ।
कोटिज्वालापरीवारः शब्दवान् दहनात्मकः ॥ 18.6 ॥
18.m: That water, out of dissatisfaction, took pleasure in modification. / As it underwent transformation, a great fire then arose, / surrounded by millions of flames, possessing sound, and consuming in nature.

18.s:
asāvapyatitejasvī vikāraṃ samarocayat .
vikurvato babhau vahnervāyuḥ paramadāruṇaḥ .
tasmādapi vikārasthādākāśaṃ samapadyata .. 18.7 ..
18.d:
असावप्यतितेजस्वी विकारं समरोचयत् ।
विकुर्वतो बभौ वह्नेर्वायुः परमदारुणः ।
तस्मादपि विकारस्थादाकाशं समपद्यत ॥ 18.7 ॥
18.m: This [fire] too, exceedingly radiant, took pleasure in modification. / From the transforming fire shone forth wind of extreme fierceness. / From that [wind] too, dwelling in modification, space arose.

18.s:
tacchabdalakṣaṇaṃ vyoma sa ca vāyuḥ pratāpavān .
tacca tejo'mbhasā yuktaṃ śliṣṭamanyonyatastadā .. 18.8 ..
18.d:
तच्छब्दलक्षणं व्योम स च वायुः प्रतापवान् ।
तच्च तेजोऽम्भसा युक्तं श्लिष्टमन्योन्यतस्तदा ॥ 18.8 ॥
18.m: That space had sound as its characteristic, and that wind was full of power; / and that fire, united with water, then clung to one another.

18.s:
tejasā śoṣitaṃ toyaṃ vāyunā ugragāminā .
bādhitena tathā vyomnā mārge datte tu tatkṣaṇāt .. 18.9 ..
18.d:
तेजसा शोषितं तोयं वायुना उग्रगामिना ।
बाधितेन तथा व्योम्ना मार्गे दत्ते तु तत्क्षणात् ॥ 18.9 ॥
18.m: The water was dried up by fire and by the fiercely moving wind, / and by space when afflicted, as passage was granted at that instant.

18.s:
piṇḍībhūtaṃ tathā sarvaṃ kāṭhinyaṃ samapadyata .
seyaṃ pṛthvī mahābhāga teṣāṃ vṛddhatarā'bhavat .. 18.10 ..
18.d:
पिण्डीभूतं तथा सर्वं काठिन्यं समपद्यत ।
सेयं पृथ्वी महाभाग तेषां वृद्धतराऽभवत् ॥ 18.10 ॥
18.m: Thus everything became a mass and attained hardness. / This became the Earth, O fortunate one, the eldest among them.

18.s:
caturṇāṃ yogakāṭhinyādekaikaguṇavṛddhitaḥ .
pṛthvī pañcaguṇā jñeyā te'pyetasyāṃ vyavasthitāḥ .. 18.11 ..
18.d:
चतुर्णां योगकाठिन्यादेकैकगुणवृद्धितः ।
पृथ्वी पञ्चगुणा ज्ञेया तेऽप्येतस्यां व्यवस्थिताः ॥ 18.11 ॥
18.m:
From the combining solidity of the four, through the increase of one quality each,
the Earth is known to have five qualities, and they too abide within her.

18.s:
sa ca kāṭhinyakaṃ kurvan brahmāṇḍaṃ samapadyata .
tasmin nārāyaṇo devaścaturmūrtiścaturbhujaḥ .. 18.12 ..
18.d:
स च काठिन्यकं कुर्वन् ब्रह्माण्डं समपद्यत ।
तस्मिन् नारायणो देवश्चतुर्मूर्तिश्चतुर्भुजः ॥ 18.12 ॥
18.m:
And while producing that solidity, the cosmic egg came into being.
Within it was the god Nārāyaṇa, endowed with four forms and four arms.

18.s:
prājāpatyena rūpeṇa sisṛkṣurvividhāḥ prajāḥ .
cintayan nādhigaccheta sṛṣṭiṃ lokapitāmahaḥ .. 18.13 ..
18.d:
प्राजापत्येन रूपेण सिसृक्षुर्विविधाः प्रजाः ।
चिन्तयन् नाधिगच्छेत सृष्टिं लोकपितामहः ॥ 18.13 ॥
18.m:
Assuming the form of Prajāpati, desiring to create diverse creatures,
the Pitāmaha of the worlds reflected, yet could not grasp creation.

18.s:
tato'sya sumahān kopo jajñe paramadāruṇaḥ .
tasmāt kopāt sahastrārciruttasthau dahanātmakaḥ .. 18.14 ..
18.d:
ततोऽस्य सुमहान् कोपो जज्ञे परमदारुणः ।
तस्मात् कोपात् सहस्त्रार्चिरुत्तस्थौ दहनात्मकः ॥ 18.14 ॥
18.m:
Then an immense, exceedingly terrible wrath arose in him;
from that wrath arose a thousand-rayed entity of consuming fire.

18.s:
sa taṃ didhakṣurbrahmāṇaṃ brahmaṇoktastadā nṛpa .
havyaṃ kavyaṃ vahasveti tato'sau havyavāhanaḥ .. 18.15 ..
18.d:
स तं दिधक्षुर्ब्रह्माणं ब्रह्मणोक्तस्तदा नृप ।
हव्यं कव्यं वहस्वेति ततोऽसौ हव्यवाहनः ॥ 18.15 ॥
18.m:
Desiring to burn Brahmā, he was then addressed by Brahmā, O king:
‘Carry the oblations to gods and ancestors’; therefore he is Havyavāhana.

18.s:
brahmāṇaṃ kṣudhitaḥ prāyāt kiṃ karomi prasādhi mām .
sa brahmā pratyuvācātha tridhā tṛptimavāpsyasi .. 18.16 ..
18.d:
ब्रह्माणं क्षुधितः प्रायात् किं करोमि प्रसाधि माम् ।
स ब्रह्मा प्रत्युवाचाथ त्रिधा तृप्तिमवाप्स्यसि ॥ 18.16 ॥
18.m:
Hungry, he went to Brahmā: ‘What shall I do? Command me!’
Brahmā then replied to him: ‘You shall attain satisfaction in three ways.

18.s:
dattāsu dakṣiṇāsvādau tṛptirbhūtvā yato'marān .
nayase dakṣiṇābhāgaṃ dakṣiṇāgnistato'bhavat .. 18.17 ..
18.d:
दत्तासु दक्षिणास्वादौ तृप्तिर्भूत्वा यतोऽमरान् ।
नयसे दक्षिणाभागं दक्षिणाग्निस्ततोऽभवत् ॥ 18.17 ॥
18.m:
When sacrificial gifts are given, having first attained satisfaction, since
you lead the gods to the southern quarter, you therefore became the Dakṣiṇāgni.

18.s:
ā samantāddhutaṃ kiṃcid yat triloke vibhāvaso .
tad vahasva surārthāya tatastvaṃ havyavāhanaḥ .. 18.18 ..
18.d:
आ समन्ताद्धुतं किंचिद् यत् त्रिलोके विभावसो ।
तद् वहस्व सुरार्थाय ततस्त्वं हव्यवाहनः ॥ 18.18 ॥
18.m:
Whatever is offered all around in the three worlds, O Vibhāvasu,
carry that for the sake of the gods; therefore you are Havyavāhana.

18.s:
gṛhaṃ śarīramityuktaṃ tatpatistvaṃ yato'dhunā .
ato vai gārhapatyastvaṃ bhava sarvagato vibho .. 18.19 ..
18.d:
गृहं शरीरमित्युक्तं तत्पतिस्त्वं यतोऽधुना ।
अतो वै गार्हपत्यस्त्वं भव सर्वगतो विभो ॥ 18.19 ॥
18.m:
The house is called the body, and since you are now its master,
therefore be the Gārhapatya, O all-pervading lord.

18.s:
viśvān narān huto yena nayase sadgatiṃ prabho .
ato vaiśvānaro nāma tava vākyaṃ bhaviṣyati .. 18.20 ..
18.d:
विश्वान् नरान् हुतो येन नयसे सद्गतिं प्रभो ।
अतो वैश्वानरो नाम तव वाक्यं भविष्यति ॥ 18.20 ॥
18.m:
Since, being offered unto, you lead all men to a good destination, O lord,
therefore Vaiśvānara shall be your name and call.

18.s:
draviṇaṃ balamityuktaṃ dhanaṃ ca draviṇaṃ yataḥ .
dadāti tad bhavāneva draviṇodāstato'bhavat .. 18.21 ..
18.d:
द्रविणं बलमित्युक्तं धनं च द्रविणं यतः ।
ददाति तद् भवानेव द्रविणोदास्ततोऽभवत् ॥ 18.21 ॥
18.m:
Draviṇa is said to be strength, and draviṇa is wealth; since
it is you who grant it, you therefore became Draviṇodā.

18.s:
tanuṃ pāsyatanuṃ pāsi yena tvaṃ sarvadā vibho .
tatastanūnapānnāma tava vatsa bhaviṣyati .. 18.22 ..
18.d:
तनुं पास्यतनुं पासि येन त्वं सर्वदा विभो ।
ततस्तनूनपान्नाम तव वत्स भविष्यति ॥ 18.22 ॥
18.m:
Since you protect the body and protect that which is not the body at all times, O lord,
therefore Tanūnapāt shall be your name, my son.

18.s:
bhavān jātāni vai veda ajātāni ca yena vai .
ataste nāma bhavatu jātavedā iti prabho .. 18.23 ..
18.d:
भवान् जातानि वै वेद अजातानि च येन वै ।
अतस्ते नाम भवतु जातवेदा इति प्रभो ॥ 18.23 ॥
18.m:
Since you truly know all things born and unborn,
therefore let your name be Jātavedas, O lord.

18.s:
nārāḥ sāmānyataḥ puṃso viśeṣeṇa dvijātayaḥ .
te śaṃsanti yatastvāṃ tu nārāśaṃsastato bhava .. 18.24 ..
18.d:
नाराः सामान्यतः पुंसो विशेषेण द्विजातयः ।
ते शंसन्ति यतस्त्वां तु नाराशंसस्ततो भव ॥ 18.24 ॥
18.m:
Nāras are men in general, especially the twice-born;
since they praise you, therefore be Nārāśaṃsa.

18.s:
agas tirobhavennityaṃ niḥśabdo niścayātmakaḥ .
agastvaṃ sarvagatvācca tenāgnistvaṃ bhaviṣyasi .. 18.25 ..
18.d:
अगस् तिरोभवेन्नित्यं निःशब्दो निश्चयात्मकः ।
अगस्त्वं सर्वगत्वाच्च तेनाग्निस्त्वं भविष्यसि ॥ 18.25 ॥
18.m:
Agas means that which ever vanishes, silent and of a resolute nature;
and because you are agas and all-pervading, you shall thereby be Agni.

18.s:
dhmā prapūraṇaśabdo ya idhmā nāma prakīrtyate .
pūritasyāgatiryena tenedhmastvaṃ bhaviṣyasi .. 18.26 ..
18.d:
ध्मा प्रपूरणशब्दो य इध्मा नाम प्रकीर्त्यते ।
पूरितस्यागतिर्येन तेनेध्मस्त्वं भविष्यसि ॥ 18.26 ॥
18.m:
Dhmā is the word meaning filling, and is proclaimed as idhmā;
since you are the arrival of what is filled, you shall thereby be Idhma.

18.s:
yājyānyetāni nāmāni tava putra mahāmakhe .
yajantastvāṃ narāḥ kāmaistarpayiṣyantyasaṃśayam .. 18.27 ..
18.d:
याज्यान्येतानि नामानि तव पुत्र महामखे ।
यजन्तस्त्वां नराः कामैस्तर्पयिष्यन्त्यसंशयम् ॥ 18.27 ॥
18.m:
These are your sacrificial names in the great sacrifice, my son;
worshipping you with sacrifices, men will surely satisfy you with their desires.’

18.s: .. iti śrīvarāhapurāṇe bhagavacchāstre aṣṭādaśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 18 ..
18.d: ॥ इति श्रीवराहपुराणे भगवच्छास्त्रे अष्टादशोऽध्यायः ॥ 18 ॥
18.m: Thus ends the eighteenth chapter in the holy Varāhapurāṇa, the treatise of the Lord.

19.s:
mahātapā uvāca .
viṣṇorvibhūtimāhātmyaṃ kathitaṃ te prasaṅgataḥ .
tithīnāṃ śrṛṇu māhātmyaṃ kathyamānaṃ mayā nṛpa .. 19.1 ..
itthaṃbhūto mahānagnirbrahmakrodhodbhavo mahān .
uvāca devaṃ brahmāṇaṃ tithirme dīyatāṃ vibho .
yasyāmahaṃ samastasya jagataḥ khyātimāpnuyām .. 19.2 ..
brahmovāca .
devānāmatha yakṣāṇāṃ gandharvāṇāṃ ca sattama .
ādau pratipadā yena tvamutpanno'si pāvaka .. 19.3 ..
tvatpadāt pratipadaṃ cānyā saṃbhaviṣyanti devatāḥ .
ataste pratipannāma tithireṣā bhaviṣyati .. 19.4 ..
tasyāṃ tithau haviṣyeṇa prājāpatyena mūrtinā .
hoṣyanti teṣāṃ prītāḥ syuḥ pitaraḥ sarvadevatāḥ .. 19.5 ..
caturvidhāni bhūtāni manuṣyāḥ paśavo'surāḥ .
devāḥ sarve sagandharvāḥ prītāḥ syustarpite tvayi .. 19.6 ..
yaścopavāsaṃ kurvīta tvadbhaktaḥ pratipaddine .
kṣīrāśano vā vartteta śrṛṇu tasya phalaṃ mahat .. 19.7 ..
caturyugāni ṣaṭtriṃśat svarloke'sau mahīyate .
tejasvī rūpasaṃpanno dravyavān jāyate naraḥ .. 19.8 ..
iha janmanyasau rājā pretya svarge mahīyate .
tūṣṇīṃ babhūva sopyagnirbrahmadattāśrayaṃ yayau .. 19.9 ..
ya idaṃ śrṛṇuyānnityaṃ prātarutthāya mānavaḥ .
agnerjanma sa pāpebhyo mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 19.10 ..
.. iti śrīvarāhapurāṇe bhagavacchāstre ekonaviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 19 ..
19.d:
महातपा उवाच ।
विष्णोर्विभूतिमाहात्म्यं कथितं ते प्रसङ्गतः ।
तिथीनां श्रृणु माहात्म्यं कथ्यमानं मया नृप ॥ 19.1 ॥
इत्थंभूतो महानग्निर्ब्रह्मक्रोधोद्भवो महान् ।
उवाच देवं ब्रह्माणं तिथिर्मे दीयतां विभो ।
यस्यामहं समस्तस्य जगतः ख्यातिमाप्नुयाम् ॥ 19.2 ॥
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
देवानामथ यक्षाणां गन्धर्वाणां च सत्तम ।
आदौ प्रतिपदा येन त्वमुत्पन्नोऽसि पावक ॥ 19.3 ॥
त्वत्पदात् प्रतिपदं चान्या संभविष्यन्ति देवताः ।
अतस्ते प्रतिपन्नाम तिथिरेषा भविष्यति ॥ 19.4 ॥
तस्यां तिथौ हविष्येण प्राजापत्येन मूर्तिना ।
होष्यन्ति तेषां प्रीताः स्युः पितरः सर्वदेवताः ॥ 19.5 ॥
चतुर्विधानि भूतानि मनुष्याः पशवोऽसुराः ।
देवाः सर्वे सगन्धर्वाः प्रीताः स्युस्तर्पिते त्वयि ॥ 19.6 ॥
यश्चोपवासं कुर्वीत त्वद्भक्तः प्रतिपद्दिने ।
क्षीराशनो वा वर्त्तेत श्रृणु तस्य फलं महत् ॥ 19.7 ॥
चतुर्युगानि षट्त्रिंशत् स्वर्लोकेऽसौ महीयते ।
तेजस्वी रूपसंपन्नो द्रव्यवान् जायते नरः ॥ 19.8 ॥
इह जन्मन्यसौ राजा प्रेत्य स्वर्गे महीयते ।
तूष्णीं बभूव सोप्यग्निर्ब्रह्मदत्ताश्रयं ययौ ॥ 19.9 ॥
य इदं श्रृणुयान्नित्यं प्रातरुत्थाय मानवः ।
अग्नेर्जन्म स पापेभ्यो मुच्यते नात्र संशयः ॥ 19.10 ॥
॥ इति श्रीवराहपुराणे भगवच्छास्त्रे एकोनविंशोऽध्यायः ॥ 19 ॥
19.m:
Mahātapas said:
The greatness of Viṣṇu's divine manifestation has been told to you in context.
Hear the greatness of the lunar days being told by me, O king.

Being thus, the great Fire, born of Brahmā's anger, mighty,
spoke to god Brahmā: 'O Lord, let a lunar day be given to me
upon which I may attain renown throughout the entire world.'

Brahmā said:
O best of the gods, yakṣas, and gandharvas,
since you were produced at the beginning, at the first step, O Purifier,

and step by step from your step other deities will come into being,
therefore this lunar day shall have the name Pratipad for you.

On that lunar day, with sacrificial food, with an offering dedicated to Prajāpati,
when they offer oblations, the ancestors and all the deities will be pleased with them.

The four kinds of creatures—human beings, beasts, asuras,
and all the gods with the gandharvas—will be pleased when you are gratified.

And whoever, devoted to you, should observe a fast on the day of Pratipad,
or live eating only milk, hear the great fruit of that:

For thirty-six four-age cycles that person is glorified in the heavenly world;
he is born a man endowed with splendor, endowed with beauty, and wealthy.

In this life he becomes a king, and after dying he is exalted in heaven.'
That Fire fell silent and went to the refuge granted by Brahmā.

The mortal who hears this daily, rising at dawn—
this birth of Fire—is freed from sins; there is no doubt about this.

20.s:
prajāpāla uvāca .
evamagneḥ samutpattirjātā brahman mahātmanaḥ .
prāṇāpānau kathaṃ devāvaśvinau saṃbabhūvatuḥ .. 20.1 ..
20.d:
प्रजापाल उवाच ।
एवमग्नेः समुत्पत्तिर्जाता ब्रह्मन् महात्मनः ।
प्राणापानौ कथं देवावश्विनौ संबभूवतुः ॥ 20.1 ॥
20.m:
Thus ends the nineteenth chapter in the glorious Varāha Purāṇa, the scripture of the Lord.

Prajāpāla said:
‘Thus occurred the birth of the high-souled Fire, O brāhmaṇa;
how did the two gods, the Aśvins, who are prāṇa and apāna, come into being?’

20.s:
marīcirbrahmaṇaḥ putraḥ svayaṃ brahmā dvisaptabhiḥ .
rūpairvyavasthitasteṣāṃ marīciḥ śreṣṭhatāmagāt .. 20.2 ..
20.d:
मरीचिर्ब्रह्मणः पुत्रः स्वयं ब्रह्मा द्विसप्तभिः ।
रूपैर्व्यवस्थितस्तेषां मरीचिः श्रेष्ठतामगात् ॥ 20.2 ॥
20.m:
[Mahātapās said:]
‘Marīci was the son of Brahmā; Brahmā himself stood established
in fourteen forms; among them Marīci attained pre-eminence.

20.s:
tasya putro mahātejāḥ kaśyapo nāma vai muniḥ .
svayaṃ prajāpatiḥ śrīmān devatānāṃ pitā'bhavat .. 20.3 ..
20.d:
तस्य पुत्रो महातेजाः कश्यपो नाम वै मुनिः ।
स्वयं प्रजापतिः श्रीमान् देवतानां पिताऽभवत् ॥ 20.3 ॥
20.m:
His son was the sage named Kaśyapa, of great splendor;
he, the glorious Prajāpati himself, became the father of the gods.

20.s:
tasya putrā babhūvurhi ādityā dvādaśa prabho .
adityapatyāni te sarve ādityāstena kīrtitāḥ .. 20.4 ..
20.d:
तस्य पुत्रा बभूवुर्हि आदित्या द्वादश प्रभो ।
अदित्यपत्यानि ते सर्वे आदित्यास्तेन कीर्तिताः ॥ 20.4 ॥
20.m:
His sons were indeed the twelve Ādityas, O lord;
they were all the offspring of Aditi, and therefore proclaimed Ādityas.

20.s:
teṣāṃ madhye mahātejā mārttaṇḍo lokaviśrutaḥ .
nārāyaṇātmakaṃ tejo dvādaśaṃ saṃprakīrtitam .. 20.5 ..
20.d:
तेषां मध्ये महातेजा मार्त्तण्डो लोकविश्रुतः ।
नारायणात्मकं तेजो द्वादशं संप्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 20.5 ॥
20.m:
Among them, the one of great splendor was Mārtaṇḍa, renowned throughout the world;
the twelfth splendor is proclaimed to consist of the nature of Nārāyaṇa.

20.s:
ye te māsāsta ādityāḥ svayaṃ saṃvatsaro hariḥ .
evaṃ te dvādaśādityā mārttaṇḍaśca pradhānavān .. 20.6 ..
20.d:
ये ते मासास्त आदित्याः स्वयं संवत्सरो हरिः ।
एवं ते द्वादशादित्या मार्त्तण्डश्च प्रधानवान् ॥ 20.6 ॥
20.m:
Those months are the Ādityas, and the year is Hari himself;
thus are the twelve Ādityas, and Mārtaṇḍa is the foremost.

20.s:
tasya tvaṣṭā dadau kanyāṃ saṃjñāṃ nāma mahāprabhām .
tasyāpatyadvayaṃ jajñe yamaśca yamunā tathā .. 20.7 ..
20.d:
तस्य त्वष्टा ददौ कन्यां संज्ञां नाम महाप्रभाम् ।
तस्यापत्यद्वयं जज्ञे यमश्च यमुना तथा ॥ 20.7 ॥
20.m:
To him Tvaṣṭṛ gave his daughter named Saṃjñā, of great radiance;
two children were born to her: Yama and Yamunā.

20.s:
tasya tejo'pyasahatī babhūvāśvī manojavā .
svāṃ chāyāṃ tatra saṃsthāpya sā jagamottarān kurūn .. 20.8 ..
20.d:
तस्य तेजोऽप्यसहती बभूवाश्वी मनोजवा ।
स्वां छायां तत्र संस्थाप्य सा जगमोत्तरान् कुरून् ॥ 20.8 ॥
20.m:
Unable to bear his heat, she became a mare swift as thought;
having stationed her own shadow there, she went to the northern Kurus.

20.s:
tadrūpāṃ tāṃ savarṇāṃ tu bheje mārttaṇḍabhāskaraḥ .
tasyā api dvayaṃ jajñe śaniṃ tapatimeva ca .. 20.9 ..
20.d:
तद्रूपां तां सवर्णां तु भेजे मार्त्तण्डभास्करः ।
तस्या अपि द्वयं जज्ञे शनिं तपतिमेव च ॥ 20.9 ॥
20.m:
Mārtaṇḍa the sun-maker united with that woman of identical form and equal color;
from her too two [children] were born: Śani and Tapatī.

20.s:
yadā tvasadṛśaṃ bheje putrān prati narottama .
saṃjñāṃ provāca bhagavān krodhasaṃraktalocanaḥ .
asamatvaṃ na karttavyaṃ sveṣvapatyeṣu bhāmini .. 20.10 ..
20.d:
यदा त्वसदृशं भेजे पुत्रान् प्रति नरोत्तम ।
संज्ञां प्रोवाच भगवान् क्रोधसंरक्तलोचनः ।
असमत्वं न कर्त्तव्यं स्वेष्वपत्येषु भामिनि ॥ 20.10 ॥
20.m:
When she showed unequal treatment toward the sons, O best of men,
the Lord, his eyes reddened with wrath, said to Saṃjñā:
“Unequal treatment must not be practiced toward one’s own children, O radiant lady!”

20.s:
evamuktā yadā sā tu asamatvaṃ vyarocata .
tadā yamaḥ svapitaraṃ provāca bhṛśaduḥkhitaḥ .. 20.11 ..
20.d:
एवमुक्ता यदा सा तु असमत्वं व्यरोचत ।
तदा यमः स्वपितरं प्रोवाच भृशदुःखितः ॥ 20.11 ॥
20.m:
When, though spoken to thus, she still favored unequal treatment,
then Yama, deeply sorrowful, spoke to his father:

20.s:
neyaṃ mātā bhavet tāta asmākaṃ śatruvat sadā .
sapatnīva vṛthācārā svesvapatyeṣu vatsalā .. 20.12 ..
20.d:
नेयं माता भवेत् तात अस्माकं शत्रुवत् सदा ।
सपत्नीव वृथाचारा स्वेस्वपत्येषु वत्सला ॥ 20.12 ॥
20.m:
“This cannot be our mother, father, acting always like an enemy toward us,
like a co-wife behaving falsely, tender only toward her own offspring.”

20.s:
evaṃ yamavacaḥ śrutvā sā chāyā krodhamūrcchitā .
śaśāpa pretarājastvaṃ bhaviṣyasyacirādiva .. 20.13 ..
20.d:
एवं यमवचः श्रुत्वा सा छाया क्रोधमूर्च्छिता ।
शशाप प्रेतराजस्त्वं भविष्यस्यचिरादिव ॥ 20.13 ॥
20.m:
Hearing those words of Yama, Chāyā, overwhelmed with wrath,
cursed him: “You shall before long become the king of the departed!”

20.s:
evaṃ śrutvā'tha mārttaṇḍastadā putrahitaiṣayā .
uvāca madhyavartī tvaṃ bhavitā dharmapāpayoḥ .
lokapālaśca bhavitā tvaṃ putra divi śobhase .. 20.14 ..
20.d:
एवं श्रुत्वाऽथ मार्त्तण्डस्तदा पुत्रहितैषया ।
उवाच मध्यवर्ती त्वं भविता धर्मपापयोः ।
लोकपालश्च भविता त्वं पुत्र दिवि शोभसे ॥ 20.14 ॥
20.m: Hearing this, Mārttaṇḍa, wishing well for his son, then / said: "You will stand in the middle between righteousness and sin. / You will also become a world-guardian, O son, and shine in heaven." 20.14

20.s:
śaniṃ śaśāpa mārttaṇḍaśchāyākopapradharṣitaḥ .
tvaṃ krūradṛṣṭirbhavitā mātṛdoṣeṇa putraka .. 20.15 ..
20.d:
शनिं शशाप मार्त्तण्डश्छायाकोपप्रधर्षितः ।
त्वं क्रूरदृष्टिर्भविता मातृदोषेण पुत्रक ॥ 20.15 ॥
20.m: Overcome by anger at Chāyā, Mārttaṇḍa cursed Śani: / "You will possess a cruel gaze on account of your mother's fault, my son." 20.15

20.s:
evamuktvā samutthāya yogaṃ bhānurdidṛkṣayā .
tāmapaśyattvasau sāśvī uttareṣu kuruṣvatha .. 20.16 ..
20.d:
एवमुक्त्वा समुत्थाय योगं भानुर्दिदृक्षया ।
तामपश्यत्त्वसौ साश्वी उत्तरेषु कुरुष्वथ ॥ 20.16 ॥
20.m: Having spoken thus, the Sun, rising up in yoga through a desire to see her, / beheld her, transformed into a mare, among the Northern Kurus. 20.16

20.s:
tato'śvarūpaṃ kṛtvā sa gatvā tatrottarān kurūn .
prājāpatyena mārgeṇa yuyojātmānamātmanā .. 20.17 ..
20.d:
ततोऽश्वरूपं कृत्वा स गत्वा तत्रोत्तरान् कुरून् ।
प्राजापत्येन मार्गेण युयोजात्मानमात्मना ॥ 20.17 ॥
20.m: Then, having assumed the form of a stallion and gone to the Northern Kurus, / he united himself with her according to the manner of Prajāpati. 20.17

20.s:
tasyāṃ tvāṣṭryāmaśvarūpyāṃ mārttaṇḍastīvratejasaḥ .
bījaṃ nirvāpayāmāsa tajjvalantaṃ dvidhā'patat .. 20.18 ..
20.d:
तस्यां त्वाष्ट्र्यामश्वरूप्यां मार्त्तण्डस्तीव्रतेजसः ।
बीजं निर्वापयामास तज्ज्वलन्तं द्विधाऽपतत् ॥ 20.18 ॥
20.m: In that daughter of Tvaṣṭṛ in the form of a mare, Mārttaṇḍa of fierce radiance / emitted his seed, which fell, blazing, in two parts. 20.18

20.s:
tatra prāṇastvapānaśca yonau cātmajitau purā .
varadānena ca punarmūrttimantau babhūvatuḥ .. 20.19 ..
20.d:
तत्र प्राणस्त्वपानश्च योनौ चात्मजितौ पुरा ।
वरदानेन च पुनर्मूर्त्तिमन्तौ बभूवतुः ॥ 20.19 ॥
20.m: There, the prāṇa and apāna breaths within the womb, having been restrained by the self long ago, / became embodied once more by the granting of a boon. 20.19

20.s:
tau tvāṣṭryāmaśvarūpiṇyāṃ jātau yena narottamau .
tatastāvaśvinau devau kīrttyete ravinandanau .. 20.20 ..
20.d:
तौ त्वाष्ट्र्यामश्वरूपिण्यां जातौ येन नरोत्तमौ ।
ततस्तावश्विनौ देवौ कीर्त्त्येते रविनन्दनौ ॥ 20.20 ॥
20.m: Because they were born from the daughter of Tvaṣṭṛ who had the form of a mare, O best of men, / those two gods, sons of the Sun, are celebrated as the Aśvins. 20.20

20.s:
prajāpatiḥ svayaṃ bhānustvāṣṭrī śaktiḥ parāparā .
tasyāḥ prāgvaccharīrasthāvamūrttau mūrtimāśritau .. 20.21 ..
20.d:
प्रजापतिः स्वयं भानुस्त्वाष्ट्री शक्तिः परापरा ।
तस्याः प्राग्वच्छरीरस्थावमूर्त्तौ मूर्तिमाश्रितौ ॥ 20.21 ॥
20.m: The Sun is himself Prajāpati, and the daughter of Tvaṣṭṛ is the higher and lower power; / abiding in her body as before, the two formless ones took on form. 20.21

20.s:
tatastāvaśvinau devau mārttaṇḍamupatasthatuḥ .
ūcatuḥ svaruciṃ tāvat kiṃ karttavyamathāvayoḥ .. 20.22 ..
20.d:
ततस्तावश्विनौ देवौ मार्त्तण्डमुपतस्थतुः ।
ऊचतुः स्वरुचिं तावत् किं कर्त्तव्यमथावयोः ॥ 20.22 ॥
20.m: Then those two gods, the Aśvins, approached Mārttaṇḍa / and declared their wish: "What should we two do now?" 20.22

20.s:
mārttaṇḍa uvāca .
putrau prajāpatiṃ devaṃ bhaktyārādhayatāṃ varam .
nārāyaṇaṃ sa vo dātā varaṃ nūnaṃ bhaviṣyati .. 20.23 ..
20.d:
मार्त्तण्ड उवाच ।
पुत्रौ प्रजापतिं देवं भक्त्याराधयतां वरम् ।
नारायणं स वो दाता वरं नूनं भविष्यति ॥ 20.23 ॥
20.m: Mārttaṇḍa said: / "My sons, worship with devotion the supreme god Prajāpati, / Nārāyaṇa; he will certainly grant you a boon." 20.23

20.s:
evaṃ tāvaśvinau proktau mārttaṇḍena mahātmanā .
tepatustīvratapasau tapaḥ paramaduścaram .
brahmapāramayaṃ stotraṃ japantau tu samāhitau .. 20.24 ..
20.d:
एवं तावश्विनौ प्रोक्तौ मार्त्तण्डेन महात्मना ।
तेपतुस्तीव्रतपसौ तपः परमदुश्चरम् ।
ब्रह्मपारमयं स्तोत्रं जपन्तौ तु समाहितौ ॥ 20.24 ॥
20.m: Thus addressed by the high-souled Mārttaṇḍa, the two Aśvins / performed fierce austerities, an austerity most difficult to practice, / reciting the hymn leading to the supreme Brahman, with minds concentrated. 20.24

20.s:
tayoḥ kālena mahatā brahmā nārāyaṇātmakaḥ .
tutoṣa paramaprītyā varaṃ caitaṃ dadau tayoḥ .. 20.25 ..
20.d:
तयोः कालेन महता ब्रह्मा नारायणात्मकः ।
तुतोष परमप्रीत्या वरं चैतं ददौ तयोः ॥ 20.25 ॥
20.m: After a long time, Brahmā, who is of the nature of Nārāyaṇa, / was pleased with great delight and granted them this boon: 20.25

20.s:
prajāpāla uvāca .
aśvibhyāmīritaṃ stotraṃ brahmaṇo'vyaktajanmanaḥ .
śrotumicchāmyahaṃ brahmaṃstvatprasādānmahāmune .. 20.26 ..
20.d:
प्रजापाल उवाच ।
अश्विभ्यामीरितं स्तोत्रं ब्रह्मणोऽव्यक्तजन्मनः ।
श्रोतुमिच्छाम्यहं ब्रह्मंस्त्वत्प्रसादान्महामुने ॥ 20.26 ॥
20.m: Prajāpāla said: / "O great sage, by your grace I wish to hear, O holy one, / the hymn recited by the Aśvins to Brahmā of unmanifest birth." 20.26

20.s:
mahātapā uvāca .
śrṛṇu rājan yathā stotramaśvibhyāṃ brahmaṇaḥ kṛtam .
īdṛśaṃ ca phalaṃ prāptaṃ tayoḥ stotrasya cānagha .. 20.27 ..
20.d:
महातपा उवाच ।
श्रृणु राजन् यथा स्तोत्रमश्विभ्यां ब्रह्मणः कृतम् ।
ईदृशं च फलं प्राप्तं तयोः स्तोत्रस्य चानघ ॥ 20.27 ॥
20.m: Mahātapās said: / "Listen, O king, to the hymn offered by the Aśvins to Brahmā, / and to such fruit obtained from their hymn, O sinless one: 20.27

20.s:
oṃnamaste niṣkriya niṣprapañca nirāśraya nirapekṣa nirālamba
nirguṇa nirāloka nirādhāra nirjaya nirākāra .
brahman mahābrahman brāhmaṇapriya puruṣa mahāpuruṣottama .
deva mahādevottama sthāṇo sthitasthāpaka .
bhūta mahābhūta bhūtādhipati yakṣa mahāyakṣa yakṣādhipate .
guhya mahāguhyādhipate saumya mahāsaumya saumyādhipate .
pakṣi mahāpakṣipate daitya mahādaityādhipate .
rudra mahārudrādhipate viṣṇu mahāviṣṇupate .
parameśvara nārāyaṇa prajāpataye namaḥ .
evaṃ stutastadā tābhyāmaśvibhyāṃ sa prajāpatiḥ .
tutoṣa paramaprītyā vākyaṃ cedamuvāca ha .. 20.28 ..
20.d:
ओंनमस्ते निष्क्रिय निष्प्रपञ्च निराश्रय निरपेक्ष निरालम्ब
निर्गुण निरालोक निराधार निर्जय निराकार ।
ब्रह्मन् महाब्रह्मन् ब्राह्मणप्रिय पुरुष महापुरुषोत्तम ।
देव महादेवोत्तम स्थाणो स्थितस्थापक ।
भूत महाभूत भूताधिपति यक्ष महायक्ष यक्षाधिपते ।
गुह्य महागुह्याधिपते सौम्य महासौम्य सौम्याधिपते ।
पक्षि महापक्षिपते दैत्य महादैत्याधिपते ।
रुद्र महारुद्राधिपते विष्णु महाविष्णुपते ।
परमेश्वर नारायण प्रजापतये नमः ।
एवं स्तुतस्तदा ताभ्यामश्विभ्यां स प्रजापतिः ।
तुतोष परमप्रीत्या वाक्यं चेदमुवाच ह ॥ 20.28 ॥
20.m: "Oṃ, homage to you, inactive one, free of phenomenal creation, without refuge, independent, without support, / devoid of qualities, without light, foundationless, unconquered, formless! / O Brahman, O Mahābrahman, lover of brāhmaṇas, O Puruṣa, O highest supreme person! / O Deva, highest of the Mahādevas, O pillar, stabilizer of all that stands! / O Bhūta, O Mahābhūta, lord of beings, O Yakṣa, O Mahāyakṣa, lord of yakṣas! / O Guhya, O lord of the Mahāguhyas, O gentle one, O most gentle one, lord of the gentle! / O bird, lord of the great birds, O Daitya, lord of the great daityas! / O Rudra, lord of the great rudras, O Viṣṇu, lord of the great viṣṇus! / O Parameśvara, O Nārāyaṇa, homage to Prajāpati!" / Thus praised at that time by the two Aśvins, Prajāpati / was pleased with great delight, and indeed spoke this word: 20.28

20.s:
varaṃ varayatāṃ śīghraṃ devaiḥ paramadurlabham .
yena me varadānena caratastridivaṃ sukham .. 20.29 ..
20.d:
वरं वरयतां शीघ्रं देवैः परमदुर्लभम् ।
येन मे वरदानेन चरतस्त्रिदिवं सुखम् ॥ 20.29 ॥
20.m: "Choose quickly a boon most difficult for the gods to obtain, / through the granting of which you two may roam heaven in happiness." 20.29

20.s:
aśvināvūcatuḥ .
āvayoryajñabhāgaṃ tu dehi deva prajāpate .
somapatvaṃ ca devānāṃ sāmānyatvaṃ ca śāśvatam .. 20.30 ..
20.d:
अश्विनावूचतुः ।
आवयोर्यज्ञभागं तु देहि देव प्रजापते ।
सोमपत्वं च देवानां सामान्यत्वं च शाश्वतम् ॥ 20.30 ॥
20.m: The Aśvins said: / "Grant us two a share of the sacrifice, O god, O Prajāpati, / and the status of soma-drinkers, and eternal equality with the gods." 20.30

20.s:
brahmovāca .
rūpaṃ kāntiranaupamyaṃ bhiṣaktvaṃ sarvavastuṣu .
somapatvaṃ ca lokeṣu sarvametad bhaviṣyati .. 20.31 ..
20.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
रूपं कान्तिरनौपम्यं भिषक्त्वं सर्ववस्तुषु ।
सोमपत्वं च लोकेषु सर्वमेतद् भविष्यति ॥ 20.31 ॥
20.m: Brahmā said: / "Beauty, radiance, matchlessness, the nature of physicians in all matters, / and the status of soma-drinkers in the worlds—all this shall be yours." 20.31

20.s:
etat sarvaṃ dvitīyāyāmaśvibhyāṃ brahmaṇā purā .
dattaṃ yasmādatasteṣāṃ tithīnāmuttamā tithiḥ .. 20.32 ..
20.d:
एतत् सर्वं द्वितीयायामश्विभ्यां ब्रह्मणा पुरा ।
दत्तं यस्मादतस्तेषां तिथीनामुत्तमा तिथिः ॥ 20.32 ॥
20.m: Because all this was given to the Aśvins by Brahmā long ago on the second lunar day, / therefore this lunar day is the best among the lunar days for them. 20.32

20.s:
etasyāṃ rūpakāmastu puṣpāhāro bhavennaraḥ .
saṃvatsaraṃ śucirnityaṃ susvarūpī bhavennaraḥ .
aśvibhyāṃ ye guṇāḥ proktāste tasyāpi bhavanti ca .. 20.33 ..
20.d:
एतस्यां रूपकामस्तु पुष्पाहारो भवेन्नरः ।
संवत्सरं शुचिर्नित्यं सुस्वरूपी भवेन्नरः ।
अश्विभ्यां ये गुणाः प्रोक्तास्ते तस्यापि भवन्ति च ॥ 20.33 ॥
20.m: A man desiring beauty should subsist on flowers on this day, / pure at all times for a year; that man will become endowed with a handsome form, / and those virtues spoken of for the Aśvins will also belong to him. 20.33

20.s:
ya idaṃ śrṛṇuyānnityamaśvibhyāṃ janma cottamam .
sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ putravān jāyate naraḥ .. 20.34 ..
20.d:
य इदं श्रृणुयान्नित्यमश्विभ्यां जन्म चोत्तमम् ।
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तः पुत्रवान् जायते नरः ॥ 20.34 ॥
20.m: A man who constantly hears this, the excellent birth of the Aśvins, / becomes freed from all sins and endowed with sons. 20.34

20.s: .. iti śrīvarāhapurāṇe bhagavacchāstre viṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 20 ..
20.d: ॥ इति श्रीवराहपुराणे भगवच्छास्त्रे विंशोऽध्यायः ॥ 20 ॥
20.m: Thus ends the twentieth chapter in the glorious Varāha Purāṇa, a sacred scripture of the Lord. 20

21.s:
mahātapā uvāca .
pūrvaṃ prajāpatirdevaḥ sisṛkṣurvividhāḥ prajāḥ .
cintayāmāsa dharmātmā yadā tā nādhyagacchata .. 21.2 ..
21.d:
महातपा उवाच ।
पूर्वं प्रजापतिर्देवः सिसृक्षुर्विविधाः प्रजाः ।
चिन्तयामास धर्मात्मा यदा ता नाध्यगच्छत ॥ 21.2 ॥
21.m: Mahātapās said: / Formerly, the divine Prajāpati, wishing to create various creatures, / reflected, righteous in nature, when he did not attain them. 21.2

21.s:
tadā'sya kopāt saṃjajñe sa ca rudraḥ pratāpavān .
rodanāt tasya rudratvaṃ saṃjātaṃ parameṣṭhinaḥ .. 21.3 ..
21.d:
तदाऽस्य कोपात् संजज्ञे स च रुद्रः प्रतापवान् ।
रोदनात् तस्य रुद्रत्वं संजातं परमेष्ठिनः ॥ 21.3 ॥
21.m: Then from his wrath was born that powerful Rudra. / Because of his crying, his name 'Rudra' came to be, given by the supreme deity. 21.3

21.s:
tasya brahmā śubhāṃ kanyāṃ bhāryārthaṃ mūrttisaṃbhavām .
gaurī nāmnā svayaṃ devī bhāratī tāṃ dadau pitā .. 21.4 ..
21.d:
तस्य ब्रह्मा शुभां कन्यां भार्यार्थं मूर्त्तिसंभवाम् ।
गौरी नाम्ना स्वयं देवी भारती तां ददौ पिता ॥ 21.4 ॥
21.m: For him, the father Brahmā himself gave an auspicious maiden born of his form / to be his wife, the goddess named Gaurī, who is speech. 21.4

21.s:
rudrāyāmitadehāya svayaṃ brahmā prajāpatiḥ .
sa tāṃ labdhvā varārohāṃ mudā paramayā yutaḥ .. 21.5 ..
21.d:
रुद्रायामितदेहाय स्वयं ब्रह्मा प्रजापतिः ।
स तां लब्ध्वा वरारोहां मुदा परमया युतः ॥ 21.5 ॥
21.m: Brahmā Prajāpati himself [gave her] to Rudra of immeasurable body. / Having obtained her of fair hips, he was filled with supreme joy. 21.5

21.s:
sargakāleṣu taṃ brahmā tapasā pratyuvāca ha .
rudra prajāḥ sṛjasveti paunaḥpunyena coditaḥ .
asamartho'hamiti jale nimajjata mahābalaḥ .. 21.6 ..
21.d:
सर्गकालेषु तं ब्रह्मा तपसा प्रत्युवाच ह ।
रुद्र प्रजाः सृजस्वेति पौनःपुन्येन चोदितः ।
असमर्थोऽहमिति जले निमज्जत महाबलः ॥ 21.6 ॥
21.m: At the times of creation, Brahmā spoke back to him through austerity: / "O Rudra, create creatures!" Thus repeatedly impelled, / saying "I am unable," the mighty one plunged into the water. 21.6

21.s:
taporthitvaṃ tapohīnaḥ straṣṭuṃ śaknoti na prajāḥ .
evaṃ cintya jale magnastato rudraḥ pratāpavān .. 21.7 ..
21.d:
तपोर्थित्वं तपोहीनः स्त्रष्टुं शक्नोति न प्रजाः ।
एवं चिन्त्य जले मग्नस्ततो रुद्रः प्रतापवान् ॥ 21.7 ॥
21.m: "One who lacks austerity and desires [fruits of] austerity cannot create creatures." / Having thought thus, the mighty Rudra then plunged into the water. 21.7

21.s:
tasmin nimagne deveśe tāṃ brahmā kanyakāṃ punaḥ .
antaḥśarīragāṃ kṛtvā gaurīṃ paramaśobhanām .. 21.8 ..
21.d:
तस्मिन् निमग्ने देवेशे तां ब्रह्मा कन्यकां पुनः ।
अन्तःशरीरगां कृत्वा गौरीं परमशोभनाम् ॥ 21.8 ॥
21.m: When that lord of gods had plunged, Brahmā again / placed inside his own body that maiden Gaurī of supreme beauty. 21.8

21.s:
punaḥ sisṛkṣurbhagavānasṛjat sapta mānasān .
dakṣaṃ ca teṣāmārabhya prajāḥ samyag vyavarddhitāḥ .. 21.9 ..
21.d:
पुनः सिसृक्षुर्भगवानसृजत् सप्त मानसान् ।
दक्षं च तेषामारभ्य प्रजाः सम्यग् व्यवर्द्धिताः ॥ 21.9 ॥
21.m: Wishing to create anew, the Lord created seven mind-born [sons]; / beginning with Dakṣa among them, creatures were thoroughly multiplied. 21.9

21.s:
tatra dākṣāyaṇīputrāḥ sarve devāḥ savāsavāḥ .
vasavo'ṣṭau ca rudrāśca ādityā marutastathā .. 21.10 ..
21.d:
तत्र दाक्षायणीपुत्राः सर्वे देवाः सवासवाः ।
वसवोऽष्टौ च रुद्राश्च आदित्या मरुतस्तथा ॥ 21.10 ॥
21.m: There, the sons of the daughter of Dakṣa were all the gods headed by Indra, / the eight Vasus, the Rudras, the Ādityas, and likewise the Maruts. 21.10

21.s:
sā'pi dakṣāya suśroṇī gaurī dattātha brahmaṇā .
duhitṛtve purā yā hi rudreṇoḍhā mahātmanā .. 21.11 ..
21.d:
साऽपि दक्षाय सुश्रोणी गौरी दत्ताथ ब्रह्मणा ।
दुहितृत्वे पुरा या हि रुद्रेणोढा महात्मना ॥ 21.11 ॥
21.m: Brahmā then gave to Dakṣa as a daughter that Gaurī of lovely hips / who had previously been married to the high-souled Rudra. 21.11

21.s:
sā ca dākṣāyaṇī devī punarbhūtā nṛpottama .
tato dakṣaḥ prahṛṣṭātmā dauhitrān svān sa vṛddhikṛt .
dṛṣṭvā yajñamathārebhe prīṇanāya prajāpatiḥ .. 21.12 ..
21.d:
सा च दाक्षायणी देवी पुनर्भूता नृपोत्तम ।
ततो दक्षः प्रहृष्टात्मा दौहित्रान् स्वान् स वृद्धिकृत् ।
दृष्ट्वा यज्ञमथारेभे प्रीणनाय प्रजापतिः ॥ 21.12 ॥
21.m: She was reborn as the daughter of Dakṣa, O best of kings. / Then Prajāpati Dakṣa, glad-hearted, having seen his grandsons / who caused prosperity, began a sacrifice in order to please [the gods]. 21.12

21.s:
tatra brahmasutāḥ sarve marīcyādaya eva ca .
cakrurārttvijyakaṃ karmma sve sve mārge vyavasthitāḥ .. 21.13 ..
21.d:
तत्र ब्रह्मसुताः सर्वे मरीच्यादय एव च ।
चक्रुरार्त्त्विज्यकं कर्म्म स्वे स्वे मार्गे व्यवस्थिताः ॥ 21.13 ॥
21.m: There, all the sons of Brahmā, Marīci and the others, / performed the duties of priests, each stationed in his own path. 21.13

21.s:
brahmā svayaṃ marīcyastu babhūvā'nye tathāpare .
atristu yajñakarmastha āgnīdhrastvaṅgirā bhavat .. 21.14 ..
21.d:
ब्रह्मा स्वयं मरीच्यस्तु बभूवाऽन्ये तथापरे ।
अत्रिस्तु यज्ञकर्मस्थ आग्नीध्रस्त्वङ्गिरा भवत् ॥ 21.14 ॥
21.m: Brahmā himself was Marīci, and likewise others were other [priests]; / Atri was established in the sacrificial act, and Aṅgiras was the āgnīdhra priest. 21.14

21.s:
hotā pulastyastvabhavadudgātā pulaho'bhavat .
kratau kratustu prastotā tadā yajñe mahātapāḥ .. 21.15 ..
21.d:
होता पुलस्त्यस्त्वभवदुद्गाता पुलहोऽभवत् ।
क्रतौ क्रतुस्तु प्रस्तोता तदा यज्ञे महातपाः ॥ 21.15 ॥
21.m: Pulastya became the hotṛ priest, and Pulaha was the udgātṛ; / Kratu was the prastotṛ in that sacrifice, O you of great austerities. 21.15

21.s:
pratihartā pracetāstu tasmin kratuvare babhau .
subrahmaṇyo vasiṣṭhastu sanakādyāḥ sabhāsadaḥ .
tatra yājyaḥ svayaṃ brahmā sa ca ijyastu pūjyate .. 21.16 ..
21.d:
प्रतिहर्ता प्रचेतास्तु तस्मिन् क्रतुवरे बभौ ।
सुब्रह्मण्यो वसिष्ठस्तु सनकाद्याः सभासदः ।
तत्र याज्यः स्वयं ब्रह्मा स च इज्यस्तु पूज्यते ॥ 21.16 ॥
21.m: Pracetas shone as the pratihartṛ priest in that excellent sacrifice, / while Vasiṣṭha was the subrahmaṇya, and Sanaka and the others were the assembly members. / There Brahmā himself was the patron of the sacrifice, and he, the one to be worshipped, was honored.

21.s:
pūjyā dakṣasya dauhitrā rudrādityāṅgirādayaḥ .
pratyakṣapitaraste hi taiḥ prītaiḥ prīyate jagat .. 21.17 ..
21.d:
पूज्या दक्षस्य दौहित्रा रुद्रादित्याङ्गिरादयः ।
प्रत्यक्षपितरस्ते हि तैः प्रीतैः प्रीयते जगत् ॥ 21.17 ॥
21.m: Dakṣa's grandsons—the Rudras, Ādityas, Aṅgirases, and others—were worthy of worship; / for they are fathers before one's very eyes, and when they are pleased, the world is pleased.

21.s:
tatra bhāgārthino devā ādityā vasavastathā .
viśvedevāḥ sapitaro gandharvādyā marudgaṇāḥ .. 21.18 ..
21.d:
तत्र भागार्थिनो देवा आदित्या वसवस्तथा ।
विश्वेदेवाः सपितरो गन्धर्वाद्या मरुद्गणाः ॥ 21.18 ॥
21.m: There the gods desiring their shares—the Ādityas as well as the Vasus, / the Viśvedevas along with the ancestors, the Gandharvas and others, and the hosts of Maruts—

21.s:
jagṛhuryajñabhāgān svān yāvat te haviṣorpitān .
tāvatkālaṃ jalāt sadya uttasthau brahmaṇaḥ punaḥ .. 21.19 ..
21.d:
जगृहुर्यज्ञभागान् स्वान् यावत् ते हविषोर्पितान् ।
तावत्कालं जलात् सद्य उत्तस्थौ ब्रह्मणः पुनः ॥ 21.19 ॥
21.m: received their sacrificial shares offered in the oblation. / Just at that time, there arose again from the water, from Brahmā,

21.s:
rudraḥ kopodbhavo yastu pūrvaṃ magno mahājale .
sa sahastrārkasaṃkāśo niścakrāma jalāt tataḥ .. 21.20 ..
21.d:
रुद्रः कोपोद्भवो यस्तु पूर्वं मग्नो महाजले ।
स सहस्त्रार्कसंकाशो निश्चक्राम जलात् ततः ॥ 21.20 ॥
21.m: Rudra, born of anger, who had previously plunged into the great waters. / Resembling a thousand suns, he then emerged from the water.

21.s:
sarvajñānamayo devaḥ sarvadevamayo'malaḥ .
pratyakṣadarśī sarvasya jagatastapasā babhau .. 21.21 ..
21.d:
सर्वज्ञानमयो देवः सर्वदेवमयोऽमलः ।
प्रत्यक्षदर्शी सर्वस्य जगतस्तपसा बभौ ॥ 21.21 ॥
21.m: The spotless god, composed of all knowledge and containing all the gods, / seeing all the world directly before his eyes, shone with his ascetic power.

21.s:
tasmiṃstu kāle pañcānāṃ jātaḥ sargo narottama .
divyānāṃ pṛthivīsthānāṃ caturṇāmarajātinām .. 21.22 ..
21.d:
तस्मिंस्तु काले पञ्चानां जातः सर्गो नरोत्तम ।
दिव्यानां पृथिवीस्थानां चतुर्णामरजातिनाम् ॥ 21.22 ॥
21.m: At that very time, O best of men, there occurred the creation of five [groups], / divine and dwelling on earth, belonging to the four classes of beings.

21.s:
raudrasargasya saṃbhūtistadā sadyo'pi jāyate .
idānīṃ rudrasargaṃ tvaṃ śrṛṇu pārthivasattama .. 21.23 ..
21.d:
रौद्रसर्गस्य संभूतिस्तदा सद्योऽपि जायते ।
इदानीं रुद्रसर्गं त्वं श्रृणु पार्थिवसत्तम ॥ 21.23 ॥
21.m: The arising of the creation of Rudra also happened right then. / Now hear about the creation by Rudra, O best of kings:

21.s:
daśavarṣasahastrāṇi tapaścīrtvā mahajjale .
pratibuddho yadā rudrastadā corvoṃ sakānanām .
dṛṣṭvā sasyavatīṃ ramyāṃ manuṣyapaśusaṃkulām .. 21.24 ..
21.d:
दशवर्षसहस्त्राणि तपश्चीर्त्वा महज्जले ।
प्रतिबुद्धो यदा रुद्रस्तदा चोर्वों सकाननाम् ।
दृष्ट्वा सस्यवतीं रम्यां मनुष्यपशुसंकुलाम् ॥ 21.24 ॥
21.m: Having performed austerities for ten thousand years in the great waters, / when Rudra awoke, he saw the earth adorned with forests, / rich in crops, delightful, and teeming with humans and cattle.

21.s:
śuśrāva ca tadā śabdānṛtvijāṃ dakṣasadmani .
āśrame yajñināṃ coccairyogasthairiti kīrttitam .. 21.25 ..
21.d:
शुश्राव च तदा शब्दानृत्विजां दक्षसद्मनि ।
आश्रमे यज्ञिनां चोच्चैर्योगस्थैरिति कीर्त्तितम् ॥ 21.25 ॥
21.m: And he heard then the chants of the priests in Dakṣa’s abode, / loudly proclaimed by those absorbed in meditation in the hermitage of the sacrificers.

21.s:
tataḥ śrutvā mahātejāḥ sarvajñaḥ parameśvaraḥ .
cukopa subhṛśaṃ devo vākyaṃ cedamuvāca ha .. 21.26 ..
21.d:
ततः श्रुत्वा महातेजाः सर्वज्ञः परमेश्वरः ।
चुकोप सुभृशं देवो वाक्यं चेदमुवाच ह ॥ 21.26 ॥
21.m: Then, having heard that, the all-knowing Supreme Lord of great splendor / became exceedingly furious and spoke these words:

21.s:
ahaṃ pūrvaṃ tu kavinā sṛṣṭaḥ sarvātmanā vibhuḥ .
prajāḥ sṛjasveti tadā vākyametat tathoktavān .. 21.27 ..
21.d:
अहं पूर्वं तु कविना सृष्टः सर्वात्मना विभुः ।
प्रजाः सृजस्वेति तदा वाक्यमेतत् तथोक्तवान् ॥ 21.27 ॥
21.m: ‘Formerly, I, the all-pervading one, was created by the wise [Brahmā] as the soul of all, / and he spoke to me this command: “Create offspring!”

21.s:
idānīṃ kena tatkarma kṛtaṃ sṛṣṭyādivarṇanam .
evamuktvā bhṛśaṃ kopānnanāda parameśvaraḥ .. 21.28 ..
21.d:
इदानीं केन तत्कर्म कृतं सृष्ट्यादिवर्णनम् ।
एवमुक्त्वा भृशं कोपान्ननाद परमेश्वरः ॥ 21.28 ॥
21.m: Now, by whom has that work of creation and the rest been accomplished?’ / Having spoken thus, the Supreme Lord roared violently out of anger.

21.s:
tasya nānadato jvālāḥ śrotrebhyo niryayustadā .
tatra bhūtāni vetālā ucchruṣmāḥ pretapūtanāḥ .. 21.29 ..
21.d:
तस्य नानदतो ज्वालाः श्रोत्रेभ्यो निर्ययुस्तदा ।
तत्र भूतानि वेताला उच्छ्रुष्माः प्रेतपूतनाः ॥ 21.29 ॥
21.m: As he roared, flames issued from his ears; / there bhūtas, vetālas, ucchruṣmas, pretas, pūtanās,

21.s:
kūṣmāṇḍā yātudhānāśca sarve prajvalitānanāḥ .
uttasthuḥ koṭiśastatra nānāpraharaṇāvṛtāḥ .. 21.30 ..
21.d:
कूष्माण्डा यातुधानाश्च सर्वे प्रज्वलिताननाः ।
उत्तस्थुः कोटिशस्तत्र नानाप्रहरणावृताः ॥ 21.30 ॥
21.m: kūṣmāṇḍas, and yātudhānas—all with blazing faces— / arose by the millions, armed with various weapons.

21.s:
te dṛṣṭvā bhūtasaṃghātā vividhāyudhapāṇayaḥ .
sasarja vedavidyāṅgaṃ rathaṃ paramaśobhanam .. 21.31 ..
21.d:
ते दृष्ट्वा भूतसंघाता विविधायुधपाणयः ।
ससर्ज वेदविद्याङ्गं रथं परमशोभनम् ॥ 21.31 ॥
21.m: Seeing those multitudes of beings with diverse weapons in hand, / he created a most splendid chariot whose parts were the knowledge of the Vedas:

21.s:
tasminnṛgādayastvaśvāstritattvaṃ ca triveṇukam .
tripūjakaṃ triṣavaṇaṃ dharmākṣaṃ mārutadhvanim .. 21.32 ..
21.d:
तस्मिन्नृगादयस्त्वश्वास्त्रितत्त्वं च त्रिवेणुकम् ।
त्रिपूजकं त्रिषवणं धर्माक्षं मारुतध्वनिम् ॥ 21.32 ॥
21.m: in it, the Ṛgveda and other Vedas were the horses, the three principles were the three bamboo poles, / the triple worship was the three daily pressings, dharma was the axle, and the sound of the wind was its rumble;

21.s:
ahorātre patāke dve dharmādharme tu daṇḍake .
śakaṭaṃ sarvavidyāśca svayaṃ brahmādisārathiḥ .. 21.33 ..
21.d:
अहोरात्रे पताके द्वे धर्माधर्मे तु दण्डके ।
शकटं सर्वविद्याश्च स्वयं ब्रह्मादिसारथिः ॥ 21.33 ॥
21.m: day and night were the two banners, dharma and adharma were the two side-poles, / all branches of knowledge formed the carriage body, and Brahmā and the others were the charioteer;

21.s:
gāyatrī ca dhanustasya oṅkāro guṇa eva ca .
svarāḥ sapta śarāstasya devadevasya suvrata .. 21.34 ..
21.d:
गायत्री च धनुस्तस्य ओङ्कारो गुण एव च ।
स्वराः सप्त शरास्तस्य देवदेवस्य सुव्रत ॥ 21.34 ॥
21.m: the Gāyatrī was his bow, and the syllable Oṃ was the bowstring; / the seven musical notes were the arrows of that god of gods, O one of good vows.

21.s:
evaṃ kṛtvā sa sāmagrīṃ devadevaḥ pratāpavān .
jagāma dakṣayajñāya kopād rudraḥ pratāpavān .. 21.35 ..
21.d:
एवं कृत्वा स सामग्रीं देवदेवः प्रतापवान् ।
जगाम दक्षयज्ञाय कोपाद् रुद्रः प्रतापवान् ॥ 21.35 ॥
21.m: Having thus prepared his equipment, the glorious god of gods, / the mighty Rudra, set out toward Dakṣa's sacrifice in wrath.

21.s:
gacchatastasya devasya ambarāṅgirasaṃ nayat .
ṛtvijāṃ mantranicayo naṣṭo rudrāgame tadā .. 21.36 ..
21.d:
गच्छतस्तस्य देवस्य अम्बराङ्गिरसं नयत् ।
ऋत्विजां मन्त्रनिचयो नष्टो रुद्रागमे तदा ॥ 21.36 ॥
21.m: As that god advanced, sweeping up the sky, / the collection of mantras of the sacrificial priests was lost at the arrival of Rudra.

21.s:
viparītamidaṃ dṛṣṭvā tadā sarve ca ṛtvijaḥ .
ūcuḥ saṃnahyatāṃ devā mahad vo bhayamāgatam .. 21.37 ..
21.d:
विपरीतमिदं दृष्ट्वा तदा सर्वे च ऋत्विजः ।
ऊचुः संनह्यतां देवा महद् वो भयमागतम् ॥ 21.37 ॥
21.m: Seeing this reversal, all the priests then / said: ‘Arm yourselves, O gods! A great danger has come upon you!

21.s:
kaścidāyāti balavānasuro brahmanirmitaḥ .
yajñabhāgārthametasmin kratau paramadurlabham .. 21.38 ..
21.d:
कश्चिदायाति बलवानसुरो ब्रह्मनिर्मितः ।
यज्ञभागार्थमेतस्मिन् क्रतौ परमदुर्लभम् ॥ 21.38 ॥
21.m: Some powerful asura created by Brahmā is approaching / to take a sacrificial share, which is extremely rare in this sacrifice.’

21.s:
evamuktāstato devā ūcurmātāmahaṃ tadā .
dakṣa tāta kimatrāsmatkāryaṃ brūhi vivakṣitam .. 21.39 ..
21.d:
एवमुक्तास्ततो देवा ऊचुर्मातामहं तदा ।
दक्ष तात किमत्रास्मत्कार्यं ब्रूहि विवक्षितम् ॥ 21.39 ॥
21.m: Having been told this, the gods then said to their maternal grandfather: / ‘O Dakṣa! O father! Tell us what our duty here is.’

21.s:
dakṣa uvāca .
gṛhyantāṃ drutamastrāṇi saṃgrāmo'tra vidhīyatām .
evamukte tadā devairvividhāyudhadhāribhiḥ .
rudrasyānucaraiḥ sārdhaṃ mahadyuddhaṃ pravartitam .. 21.40 ..
21.d:
दक्ष उवाच ।
गृह्यन्तां द्रुतमस्त्राणि संग्रामोऽत्र विधीयताम् ।
एवमुक्ते तदा देवैर्विविधायुधधारिभिः ।
रुद्रस्यानुचरैः सार्धं महद्युद्धं प्रवर्तितम् ॥ 21.40 ॥
21.m: Dakṣa said: / ‘Quickly take up weapons! Let battle be joined here!’ / When he had spoken thus, a great battle was begun by the gods / wielding various weapons against the followers of Rudra.

21.s:
tatra vetālabhūtāni kūṣmāṇḍā grahapūtanāḥ .
yuyudhurlokapālaiśca nānāśastradharāṇi ca .. 21.41 ..
21.d:
तत्र वेतालभूतानि कूष्माण्डा ग्रहपूतनाः ।
युयुधुर्लोकपालैश्च नानाशस्त्रधराणि च ॥ 21.41 ॥
21.m: There vetālas, bhūtas, kūṣmāṇḍas, grahas, and pūtanās / fought against the guardians of the world, bearing various weapons.

21.s:
devā raudrāṇi bhūtāni nirasanto yamālayam .
cikṣipuḥ sāyakān ghorānasīṃśca saparaśvadhān .. 21.42 ..
21.d:
देवा रौद्राणि भूतानि निरसन्तो यमालयम् ।
चिक्षिपुः सायकान् घोरानसींश्च सपरश्वधान् ॥ 21.42 ॥
21.m: The gods, driving the fierce beings to the abode of Yama, / discharged dreadful arrows, swords, and battle-axes.

21.s:
bhūtānyapi mṛdhe dhorāṇyulmukairasthibhiḥ śaraiḥ .
jagmurdevān mṛdhe roṣād rudrasya purato balāt .. 21.43 ..
21.d:
भूतान्यपि मृधे धोराण्युल्मुकैरस्थिभिः शरैः ।
जग्मुर्देवान् मृधे रोषाद् रुद्रस्य पुरतो बलात् ॥ 21.43 ॥
21.m: The fierce spirits too in battle, with firebrands, bones, and arrows, / assaulted the gods in combat with force out of wrath before Rudra.

21.s:
tatastasmin mahāraudre saṃgrāme bhīmarūpiṇi .
rudro bhagasya netre tu bibhedaikeṣuṇā mṛdhe .. 21.44 ..
21.d:
ततस्तस्मिन् महारौद्रे संग्रामे भीमरूपिणि ।
रुद्रो भगस्य नेत्रे तु बिभेदैकेषुणा मृधे ॥ 21.44 ॥
21.m: Then, in that exceedingly fierce and terrifying battle, / Rudra pierced the eyes of Bhaga with a single arrow in combat.

21.s:
rudrasya śarapātena naṣṭanetraṃ bhagaṃ tadā .
dṛṣṭvā'sya krodhāt tejasvī pūṣā rudramayodhayat .. 21.45 ..
21.d:
रुद्रस्य शरपातेन नष्टनेत्रं भगं तदा ।
दृष्ट्वाऽस्य क्रोधात् तेजस्वी पूषा रुद्रमयोधयत् ॥ 21.45 ॥
21.m: Seeing Bhaga blinded by the strike of Rudra's arrow, / the radiant Pūṣan then fought Rudra out of wrath.

21.s:
sṛjantamiṣujālāni pūṣaṇaṃ tu mahāmṛdhe .
dṛṣṭvā rudro'sya dantāṃstu cakarṣaṃ paravīrahā .. 21.46 ..
21.d:
सृजन्तमिषुजालानि पूषणं तु महामृधे ।
दृष्ट्वा रुद्रोऽस्य दन्तांस्तु चकर्षं परवीरहा ॥ 21.46 ॥
21.m: Seeing Pūṣan shooting flights of arrows in the great battle, / Rudra, the slayer of enemy warriors, tore out his teeth.

21.s:
tasya dantāṃstadā dṛṣṭvā pūṣṇo rudreṇa pātitān .
dudruvuḥ vasavo dikṣu rudrāstvekādaśa drutam .. 21.47 ..
21.d:
तस्य दन्तांस्तदा दृष्ट्वा पूष्णो रुद्रेण पातितान् ।
दुद्रुवुः वसवो दिक्षु रुद्रास्त्वेकादश द्रुतम् ॥ 21.47 ॥
21.m: Seeing the teeth of Pūṣan knocked down by Rudra, / the Vasus and the eleven Rudras quickly fled in all directions.

21.s:
tān bhagnān sahasā dikṣu dṛṣṭvā viṣṇuḥ pratāpavān .
ādityāvarajo vākyamuvāca svabalaṃ tadā .. 21.48 ..
21.d:
तान् भग्नान् सहसा दिक्षु दृष्ट्वा विष्णुः प्रतापवान् ।
आदित्यावरजो वाक्यमुवाच स्वबलं तदा ॥ 21.48 ॥
21.m: Seeing them suddenly broken and fleeing in all directions, the glorious Viṣṇu, / the younger brother of Indra, then addressed his army:

21.s:
kva yāta pauruṣaṃ tyaktvā darpaṃ māhātmyameva ca .
vyavasāyaṃ kulaṃ bhūtiṃ kathaṃ na smaryate drutam .. 21.49 ..
21.d:
क्व यात पौरुषं त्यक्त्वा दर्पं माहात्म्यमेव च ।
व्यवसायं कुलं भूतिं कथं न स्मर्यते द्रुतम् ॥ 21.49 ॥
21.m: ‘Where are you fleeing, having abandoned virility, pride, and majesty? / How do you not swiftly remember your resolve, your lineage, and your power?

21.s:
parameṣṭhiguṇairyukto laghuvadbhītitaḥ purā .
namaskaṃ kurute moghaṃ pṛthivyāṃ padmajaḥ svayam .. 21.50 ..
21.d:
परमेष्ठिगुणैर्युक्तो लघुवद्भीतितः पुरा ।
नमस्कं कुरुते मोघं पृथिव्यां पद्मजः स्वयम् ॥ 21.50 ॥
21.m: Endowed with the virtues of the Supreme Being, the lotus-born [Brahmā] himself, / like a trivial person out of fear, formerly bowed down in vain on the earth.’

21.s:
evamuktvā garutmantamāruroha haristadā .
śaṅkhacakragadāpāṇiḥ pītavāsā janārdanaḥ .. 21.51 ..
21.d:
एवमुक्त्वा गरुत्मन्तमारुरोह हरिस्तदा ।
शङ्खचक्रगदापाणिः पीतवासा जनार्दनः ॥ 21.51 ॥
21.m: Having spoken thus, Hari then mounted Garuḍa— / Janārdana, holder of the conch, discus, and mace, clad in yellow garments.

21.s:
tato hariharaṃ yuddhamabhavallomaharṣaṇam .
rudraḥ pāśupatāstreṇa vivyādha harimojasā .
harirnārāyaṇāstreṇa rudraṃ vivyādha kopavān .. 21.52 ..
21.d:
ततो हरिहरं युद्धमभवल्लोमहर्षणम् ।
रुद्रः पाशुपतास्त्रेण विव्याध हरिमोजसा ।
हरिर्नारायणास्त्रेण रुद्रं विव्याध कोपवान् ॥ 21.52 ॥
21.m: Then a hair-raising duel took place between Hari and Hara. / Rudra forcefully pierced Hari with the Pāśupata weapon; / Hari, full of anger, pierced Rudra with the Nārāyaṇa weapon.

21.s:
nārāyaṇaṃ pāśupatamubhe'stre vyomni roṣite .
yuyudhāte bhṛśaṃ divyaṃ parasparajighāṃsayā .
divyaṃ varṣasahastraṃ tu tayoryuddhamabhūt tadā .. 21.53 ..
21.d:
नारायणं पाशुपतमुभेऽस्त्रे व्योम्नि रोषिते ।
युयुधाते भृशं दिव्यं परस्परजिघांसया ।
दिव्यं वर्षसहस्त्रं तु तयोर्युद्धमभूत् तदा ॥ 21.53 ॥
21.m: The two weapons, the Nārāyaṇa and the Pāśupata, enraged in the sky, / fought fiercely and divinely, each wishing to destroy the other; / their combat then lasted for a divine thousand years.

21.s:
tatraikaṃ mukuṭodbaddhaṃ mūrddhanyaṃ jaṭajālakam .
ekaṃ pradhmāpayacchaṅkhamanyaḍumarukaṃ śubham .. 21.54 ..
21.d:
तत्रैकं मुकुटोद्बद्धं मूर्द्धन्यं जटजालकम् ।
एकं प्रध्मापयच्छङ्खमन्यडुमरुकं शुभम् ॥ 21.54 ॥
21.m: There one had a mass of matted locks bound on his head like a diadem; / one blew a conch shell, while the other sounded an auspicious small drum;

21.s:
ekaṃ khaṅgakaraṃ tatra tathā'nyaṃ daṇḍadhāriṇam .
ekaṃ kaustubhadīptāṅgamanyaṃ bhūtivibhūṣitam .. 21.55 ..
21.d:
एकं खङ्गकरं तत्र तथाऽन्यं दण्डधारिणम् ।
एकं कौस्तुभदीप्ताङ्गमन्यं भूतिविभूषितम् ॥ 21.55 ॥
21.m: there one had a sword in hand, while the other carried a staff; / one had his body radiant with the Kaustubha gem, while the other was adorned with ashes.

21.s:
ekaṃ gadāṃ bhrāmayati dvitīyaṃ daṇḍameva ca .
ekaṃ śobhati kaṇṭhasthairmaṇibhistvasthibhiḥ param .
ekaṃ pītāmbaraṃ tatra dvitīyaṃ sarpamekhalam .. 21.56 ..
21.d:
एकं गदां भ्रामयति द्वितीयं दण्डमेव च ।
एकं शोभति कण्ठस्थैर्मणिभिस्त्वस्थिभिः परम् ।
एकं पीताम्बरं तत्र द्वितीयं सर्पमेखलम् ॥ 21.56 ॥
21.m: One whirled a mace, and the second a staff; / one shone with jewels worn on the neck, but the other with bones; / one had yellow garments, the other a snake for a girdle.

21.s:
evaṃ tau sparddhināvastrau raudranārāyaṇātmakau .
anyo'nyātiśayopetau tadālokya pitāmahaḥ .. 21.57 ..
21.d:
एवं तौ स्पर्द्धिनावस्त्रौ रौद्रनारायणात्मकौ ।
अन्योऽन्यातिशयोपेतौ तदालोक्य पितामहः ॥ 21.57 ॥
21.m: Thus the two weapons, embodying Rudra and Nārāyaṇa, vied with each other, / each excelling the other. Seeing this, Pitāmaha

21.s:
uvāca śāmyatāmastrau svasvabhāvena suvratau .
evaṃ te brahmaṇā coktau śāntabhāvaṃ prajagmatuḥ .. 21.58 ..
21.d:
उवाच शाम्यतामस्त्रौ स्वस्वभावेन सुव्रतौ ।
एवं ते ब्रह्मणा चोक्तौ शान्तभावं प्रजग्मतुः ॥ 21.58 ॥
21.m: said: "Subside, you two weapons of good vows, into your own natures!" / Addressed thus by Brahmā, the two subsided into peacefulness.

21.s:
tathā viṣṇuharau brahmā vākyametaduvāca ha .
ubhau hariharau devau loke khyātiṃ gamiṣyathaḥ .. 21.59 ..
21.d:
तथा विष्णुहरौ ब्रह्मा वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह ।
उभौ हरिहरौ देवौ लोके ख्यातिं गमिष्यथः ॥ 21.59 ॥
21.m: Then Brahmā spoke these words to Viṣṇu and Hara: / "You two gods, Hari and Hara, shall become renowned in the world.

21.s:
ayaṃ ca yajño vidhvastaḥ saṃpūrṇatvaṃ gamiṣyati .
dakṣasya khyātimām̐llokaḥ saṃtatyā'yaṃ bhaviṣyati .. 21.60 ..
21.d:
अयं च यज्ञो विध्वस्तः संपूर्णत्वं गमिष्यति ।
दक्षस्य ख्यातिमाम्̐ल्लोकः संतत्याऽयं भविष्यति ॥ 21.60 ॥
21.m: And this ruined sacrifice shall reach completion; / this world shall become renowned through Dakṣa's progeny."

21.s:
evamuktvā hariharau tadā lokapitāmahaḥ .
brahmā lokānuvācedaṃ rudrabhāgo'sya dīyatām .. 21.61 ..
21.d:
एवमुक्त्वा हरिहरौ तदा लोकपितामहः ।
ब्रह्मा लोकानुवाचेदं रुद्रभागोऽस्य दीयताम् ॥ 21.61 ॥
21.m: Having spoken thus to Hari and Hara, Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, / then said to the worlds: "Let Rudra's portion be given to him!

21.s:
rudrabhāgo jyeṣṭhabhāga itīyaṃ vaidikī śrutiḥ .
stutiṃ ca devāḥ kuruta rudrasya parameṣṭhi naḥ .. 21.62 ..
21.d:
रुद्रभागो ज्येष्ठभाग इतीयं वैदिकी श्रुतिः ।
स्तुतिं च देवाः कुरुत रुद्रस्य परमेष्ठि नः ॥ 21.62 ॥
21.m: Rudra's portion is the foremost portion—such is the Vedic revelation. / And gods, offer praise to Rudra, the supreme lord!

21.s:
bhaganetraharaṃ devaṃ pūṣṇo dantavināśanam .
stutiṃ kurutamā śīghraṃ gītairetaistu nāmabhiḥ .
yenāyaṃ vaḥ prasannātmā varadatvaṃ bhajeta ha .. 21.63 ..
21.d:
भगनेत्रहरं देवं पूष्णो दन्तविनाशनम् ।
स्तुतिं कुरुतमा शीघ्रं गीतैरेतैस्तु नामभिः ।
येनायं वः प्रसन्नात्मा वरदत्वं भजेत ह ॥ 21.63 ॥
21.m: Quickly praise the god who tore out Bhaga's eyes and smashed Pūṣan's teeth / with these chanted names, / so that he, pleased at heart, will grant you boons."

21.s:
evamuktāstu te devāḥ stotraṃ śaṃbhormahātmanaḥ .
cakruḥ paramayā bhaktyā namaskṛtya svayaṃbhuve .. 21.64 ..
21.d:
एवमुक्तास्तु ते देवाः स्तोत्रं शंभोर्महात्मनः ।
चक्रुः परमया भक्त्या नमस्कृत्य स्वयंभुवे ॥ 21.64 ॥
21.m: Addressed thus, the gods bowed to the self-born one / and praised noble Śambhu with supreme devotion.

21.s:
devā ūcuḥ .
namo viṣamanetrāya namaste tryambakāya ca .
namaḥ sahastranetrāya namaste śūlapāṇaye .. 21.65 ..
21.d:
देवा ऊचुः ।
नमो विषमनेत्राय नमस्ते त्र्यम्बकाय च ।
नमः सहस्त्रनेत्राय नमस्ते शूलपाणये ॥ 21.65 ॥
21.m: The gods said: / "Homage to the odd-eyed one, and homage to you, Tryambaka! / Homage to the thousand-eyed one, and homage to you, bearer of the trident!

21.s:
namaḥ khaṭvāṅgahastāya namo daṇḍabhṛte kare .
tvaṃ deva hutabhugjvālākoṭibhānusamaprabhaḥ .. 21.66 ..
21.d:
नमः खट्वाङ्गहस्ताय नमो दण्डभृते करे ।
त्वं देव हुतभुग्ज्वालाकोटिभानुसमप्रभः ॥ 21.66 ॥
21.m: Homage to the one who holds a skull-topped staff, homage to the one bearing a club in hand! / You, O god, possess a splendour equal to ten million suns and the fire's flame!

21.s:
adarśane'nayad deva mūḍhavijñānato'dhunā .
kṛtamasmābhireveśa tadatra kṣamyatāṃ prabho .. 21.67 ..
21.d:
अदर्शनेऽनयद् देव मूढविज्ञानतोऽधुना ।
कृतमस्माभिरेवेश तदत्र क्षम्यतां प्रभो ॥ 21.67 ॥
21.m: Through foolish understanding, O god, we brought about your exclusion just now; / this was done by us, O Lord, so forgive us in this, O master!

21.s:
namastrinetrārttiharāya śaṃbho
triśūlapāṇe vikṛtāsyarūpa .
samastadeveśvara śuddhabhāva
prasīda rudrācyuta sarvabhāva .. 21.68 ..
21.d:
नमस्त्रिनेत्रार्त्तिहराय शंभो
त्रिशूलपाणे विकृतास्यरूप ।
समस्तदेवेश्वर शुद्धभाव
प्रसीद रुद्राच्युत सर्वभाव ॥ 21.68 ॥
21.m: Homage to the three-eyed one who removes distress, O Śambhu, / bearer of the trident, one of transformed countenance and form! / Sovereign of all gods, pure-natured one, / be gracious, O Rudra, imperishable one of all natures!

21.s:
pūṣṇo'sya dantāntaka bhīmarūpa
pralambabhogīndralulantakaṇṭha .
viśāladehācyuta nīlakaṇṭha
prasīda viśveśvara viśvamūrtte .. 21.69 ..
21.d:
पूष्णोऽस्य दन्तान्तक भीमरूप
प्रलम्बभोगीन्द्रलुलन्तकण्ठ ।
विशालदेहाच्युत नीलकण्ठ
प्रसीद विश्वेश्वर विश्वमूर्त्ते ॥ 21.69 ॥
21.m: Destroyer of Pūṣan's teeth, one of terrible form, / whose neck bears the swaying great serpent dangling down! / One of vast body, imperishable one, blue-throated one, / be gracious, lord of the universe, universal form!

21.s:
bhagākṣisaṃsphoṭanadakṣakarmā
gṛhāṇa bhāgaṃ makhataḥ pradhānam .
prasīda deveśvara nīlakaṇṭha
prapāhi naḥ sarvaguṇopapanna .. 21.70 ..
21.d:
भगाक्षिसंस्फोटनदक्षकर्मा
गृहाण भागं मखतः प्रधानम् ।
प्रसीद देवेश्वर नीलकण्ठ
प्रपाहि नः सर्वगुणोपपन्न ॥ 21.70 ॥
21.m: You whose action struck out Bhaga's eyes, / receive the foremost portion from the sacrifice! / Be gracious, lord of gods, blue-throated one, / protect us, endowed with all virtues!

21.s:
sitāṅgarāgāpratipannamūrtte
kapāladhāriṃstripuraghna deva .
prapāhi naḥ sarvabhayeṣu caiva
umāpate puṣkaranālajanma .. 21.71 ..
21.d:
सिताङ्गरागाप्रतिपन्नमूर्त्ते
कपालधारिंस्त्रिपुरघ्न देव ।
प्रपाहि नः सर्वभयेषु चैव
उमापते पुष्करनालजन्म ॥ 21.71 ॥
21.m: One of white body-ointment and unassailable form, / skull-bearer, slayer of Tripura, O god! / Protect us indeed in all fears, / lord of Umā, born from the lotus-stalk!

21.s:
paśyāma te dehagatān sureśa
sargādayo vedavarānananta .
sāṅgān savidyān sapadakramāṃśca
sarvān nilīnāṃstvayi devadeva .. 21.72 ..
21.d:
पश्याम ते देहगतान् सुरेश
सर्गादयो वेदवराननन्त ।
साङ्गान् सविद्यान् सपदक्रमांश्च
सर्वान् निलीनांस्त्वयि देवदेव ॥ 21.72 ॥
21.m: We see the creations and the foremost Vedas situated in your body, lord of gods, / boundless one, along with their limbs, lore, and recited word-sequences, / all dissolved in you, O god of gods!

21.s:
bhava śarva mahādeva pinākin rudra te hara .
natāḥ sma sarve viśveśa trāhi naḥ parameśvara .. 21.73 ..
21.d:
भव शर्व महादेव पिनाकिन् रुद्र ते हर ।
नताः स्म सर्वे विश्वेश त्राहि नः परमेश्वर ॥ 21.73 ॥
21.m: Bhava, Śarva, Mahādeva, Pināka-bearer, Rudra, Hara, / all of us bow to you, lord of the universe; protect us, supreme Lord!"

21.s:
itthaṃ stutastadā devairdevadevo maheśvaraḥ .
tutoṣa sarvadevānāṃ vākyaṃ cedamuvāca ha .. 21.74 ..
21.d:
इत्थं स्तुतस्तदा देवैर्देवदेवो महेश्वरः ।
तुतोष सर्वदेवानां वाक्यं चेदमुवाच ह ॥ 21.74 ॥
21.m: Praised thus by the gods, the god of gods, Maheśvara, / was pleased with all the gods and spoke these words:

21.s:
rudra uvāca .
bhagasya netraṃ bhavatu pūṣṇo dantāstathā makhaḥ .
dakṣasyācchidratāṃ yātu yajñaścāpyaditeḥ sutāḥ .
paśubhāvaṃ tathā cāpi apaneṣyāmi vo surāḥ .. 21.75 ..
21.d:
रुद्र उवाच ।
भगस्य नेत्रं भवतु पूष्णो दन्तास्तथा मखः ।
दक्षस्याच्छिद्रतां यातु यज्ञश्चाप्यदितेः सुताः ।
पशुभावं तथा चापि अपनेष्यामि वो सुराः ॥ 21.75 ॥
21.m: Rudra said: / "Let Bhaga have his eye, Pūṣan his teeth, / Dakṣa's sacrifice become faultless, O sons of Aditi, / and I will remove your state of beasts, O gods.

21.s:
maddarśanena yo jātaḥ paśubhāvo divaukasām .
sa mayā'pahṛtaḥ sadyaḥ patitvaṃ vo bhaviṣyati .. 21.76 ..
21.d:
मद्दर्शनेन यो जातः पशुभावो दिवौकसाम् ।
स मयाऽपहृतः सद्यः पतित्वं वो भविष्यति ॥ 21.76 ॥
21.m: The state of beasts that befell the heaven-dwellers upon seeing me / has now been taken away by me; you shall have mastery.

21.s:
ahaṃ ca sarvavidyānāṃ patirādyaḥ sanātanaḥ .
ahaṃ vai patibhāvena paśumadhye vyavasthitaḥ .. 21.77 ..
21.d:
अहं च सर्वविद्यानां पतिराद्यः सनातनः ।
अहं वै पतिभावेन पशुमध्ये व्यवस्थितः ॥ 21.77 ॥
21.m: And I am the master of all kinds of knowledge, the primal and eternal one; / indeed, I remain among the beasts in the capacity of their master.

21.s:
ataḥ paśupatirnāma mama loke bhaviṣyati .
ye māṃ yajanti teṣāṃ syād dīkṣā pāśupatī bhavet .. 21.78 ..
21.d:
अतः पशुपतिर्नाम मम लोके भविष्यति ।
ये मां यजन्ति तेषां स्याद् दीक्षा पाशुपती भवेत् ॥ 21.78 ॥
21.m: Therefore my name in the world shall be Paśupati. / For those who sacrifice to me, there shall be the Pāśupata initiation."

21.s:
evamukte'tha rudreṇa brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ .
uvāca rudraṃ sasnehaṃ smitapūrvamidaṃ vacaḥ .. 21.79 ..
21.d:
एवमुक्तेऽथ रुद्रेण ब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः ।
उवाच रुद्रं सस्नेहं स्मितपूर्वमिदं वचः ॥ 21.79 ॥
21.m: When Rudra had spoken thus, Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, / said to Rudra affectionately with a smile:

21.s:
dhruvaṃ pāśupatirdeva tvaṃ loke khyātimesyati .
ayaṃ ca devastvannāmnā loke khyātiṃ gamiṣyati .
ārādhyaśca samastānāṃ devādīnāṃ gamiṣyasi .. 21.80 ..
21.d:
ध्रुवं पाशुपतिर्देव त्वं लोके ख्यातिमेस्यति ।
अयं च देवस्त्वन्नाम्ना लोके ख्यातिं गमिष्यति ।
आराध्यश्च समस्तानां देवादीनां गमिष्यसि ॥ 21.80 ॥
